title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
所求乎臣以事君未能也
黃文煒
同考試官教諭劉批孔子以事君未能蓋有見
於臣道之大作者率多浮汎此作辭典重而理躍如宜錄以式多士
同考試官教諭黎批詞理精到筆勢翩翩
同考試官教諭金批事君以忠之道發明殆盡
考試官教諭蔡批孔子教忠之訓意正如此
===
考試官教諭林批雅暢雄渾
聖人以忠道望天下而必引已以自責焉甚矣
事君莫大乎忠也一有不盡其心斯無以畢臣
之分矣而可乎此夫子所以自歉於君子之道
而教天下以作忠也其意豈不曰天下莫重於
君臣之大倫而亦莫難盡於事使之大義丘所
未能於君子之道者此其四之一乎何則君尊
臣卑其分嚴矣而君之屬任豈徒以爵祿乎臣
哉蓋實以當務之職付之也此而不力則干君
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

所求乎臣以事君，未能也。

黃文煒

同考試官教諭劉批：孔子以事君未能，蓋有見於臣道之大。作者率多浮汎，此作辭典重而理躍如，宜錄以式多士。

同考試官教諭黎批：詞理精到，筆勢翩翩。

同考試官教諭金批：事君以忠之道，發明殆盡。

考試官教諭蔡批：孔子教忠之訓，意正如此。

考試官教諭林批：雅暢雄渾。

聖人以忠道望天下，而必引已以自責焉。甚矣，事君莫大乎忠也！一有不盡其心，斯無以畢臣之分矣，而可乎？此夫子所以自歉於君子之道，而教天下以作忠也。其意豈不曰：天下莫重於君臣之大倫，而亦莫難盡於事使之大義。丘所未能於君子之道者，此其四之一乎？何則？君尊臣卑，其分嚴矣，而君之屬任，豈徒以爵祿乎臣哉？蓋實以當務之職付之也。此而不力，則干君
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“What I require of a minister, I have not yet been able to fulfill in serving my ruler.”

Huang Wenwei

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Confucius’s statement that he had not yet been able to fulfill his service to his ruler surely reflects his recognition of the magnitude of a minister’s duty. Most writers treat this superficially. This composition is dignified in expression and brings its principles vividly to life. It should be included as a model for the assembled scholars.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The language and reasoning are finely accomplished; the writing flows gracefully.

Comment by Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor: The way of serving one’s ruler with loyalty is elucidated almost exhaustively.

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: This is precisely the meaning of Confucius’s teaching on loyalty.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Elegant and fluent, vigorous and full-bodied.

The sage expects all under Heaven to follow the way of loyalty, yet invariably brings himself forward for self-reproach. How momentous it is: in serving one’s ruler, nothing is greater than loyalty! If one fails in any respect to devote one’s whole heart, one cannot fulfill a minister’s duty. Could that be acceptable? This is why the Master considered himself deficient in the way of the gentleman, and taught all under Heaven to practice loyalty. Was his meaning not this: “Nothing under Heaven carries greater weight than the cardinal relationship between ruler and minister; nor is anything harder to fulfill than the great moral obligations of serving and commanding. Among the aspects of the gentleman’s way that I, Qiu, have not yet mastered, is this not one of the four? Why is this so? The ruler is exalted and the minister lowly: the distinction between their stations is strict. Yet when the ruler entrusts responsibilities to a minister, is it merely to bestow rank and emoluments upon him? In truth, he entrusts him with the duties that must be performed. If he does not exert himself in these, then toward the ruler [?] …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
有重負矣君逸臣勞其義辨矣而臣之委贄亦
豈徒以順承乎君哉蓋實以當爲之分任之也
此而不盡則臣道有餘責矣故丘嘗學之而夙
夜匪懈之義未嘗不望之人人然我儀圖之而
鞠躬盡瘁之誠寔固恒歉於事事爲委吏爲乗
田非不以一命爲榮而思有以稱塞也然其職
則末其道則詳而敢曰服采之易勝乎而司寇
而攝相非不以百司是總而圖所以負荷也然
其任愈隆其責愈重而敢曰服休之無忝乎蓋
===
其可竭者吾之心而不容以易畢者臣之分雖
忠愛由於自靖而臣盡臣道則實未能以自信
矣可致者吾之身而不容以易盡者臣之禮雖
分義本於天植而爲上爲德則固未敢以自誣
矣吁此君子以臣事君之道丘嘗反巳而有歉
於懷也歟是知君臣之道道之不遠於人也求
盡事君之道不遠人以爲道也而世之遠人爲
道者獨何哉抑觀孔子之在當時蓋欲堯舜其
君而以堯舜之臣望臣者是故則天賛堯恭巳
punctuated:
有重負矣。君逸臣勞，其義辨矣。而臣之委贄，亦豈徒以順承乎君哉？蓋實以當爲之分任之也。此而不盡，則臣道有餘責矣。故丘嘗學之，而夙夜匪懈之義，未嘗不望之人人。然我儀圖之，而鞠躬盡瘁之誠，寔固恒歉於事事。爲委吏，爲乗田，非不以一命爲榮，而思有以稱塞也；然其職則末，其道則詳，而敢曰服采之易勝乎？而司寇，而攝相，非不以百司是總，而圖所以負荷也；然其任愈隆，其責愈重，而敢曰服休之無忝乎？蓋其可竭者吾之心，而不容以易畢者臣之分。雖忠愛由於自靖，而臣盡臣道，則實未能以自信矣。可致者吾之身，而不容以易盡者臣之禮。雖分義本於天植，而爲上爲德，則固未敢以自誣矣。吁！此君子以臣事君之道，丘嘗反巳而有歉於懷也歟？
是知君臣之道，道之不遠於人也；求盡事君之道，不遠人以爲道也。而世之遠人爲道者，獨何哉？抑觀孔子之在當時，蓋欲堯舜其君，而以堯舜之臣望臣者。是故則天賛堯，恭巳
translation_en:
…there would be a grave failure toward the ruler. That the ruler rests while his ministers labor is a clearly distinguished obligation. When a minister presents his ceremonial gift upon entering service, is it merely to submit obediently to his ruler? He truly takes upon himself the duties proper to his station. If he does not fulfill them, his obligations as a minister remain undischarged. Thus I, Qiu, have sought to learn this, and have always expected everyone to uphold the duty of remaining tireless morning and night. Yet when I consider the matter, I find myself continually wanting in every undertaking in the sincerity needed to devote myself utterly to service. When serving as a granary clerk or as an overseer of livestock, I did indeed regard even the lowest appointment as an honor and seek to discharge it worthily. Yet although these offices were minor, their proper conduct required attention to detail: would I dare say that official duties were easily fulfilled? When serving as Minister of Justice and as acting chief minister, I did indeed seek ways to shoulder the burden of overseeing the hundred offices. Yet the higher the appointment, the heavier its responsibilities: would I dare claim to have received such favor without bringing it dishonor? For what I can exhaust is my own heart’s exertion; what cannot readily be discharged is a minister’s duty. Although loyalty and love arise from setting oneself right, I cannot truly feel confident that, as a minister, I have fulfilled the ministerial way. What I can offer wholly is my own person; what cannot readily be fulfilled is the ritual propriety required of a minister. Although the obligations of one’s station are rooted in Heaven-given nature, I would certainly not dare deceive myself by claiming to have cultivated virtue for my sovereign. Ah! Is this not the gentleman’s way of serving his ruler as a minister, upon which I, Qiu, have reflected and found my heart wanting?
From this we know that the way of ruler and minister exemplifies how the Way is never far from human beings. To seek to fulfill the way of serving one’s ruler is to practice the Way without departing from human beings. Why, then, do people in this world pursue a Way remote from humanity? Consider Confucius in his own time: he wished to make his ruler a Yao or a Shun, and expected ministers to be like the ministers of Yao and Shun. Thus he praised Yao for modeling himself on Heaven, and [spoke of] reverently composing oneself…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
贊舜其心惓惓焉必欲君之爲唐虞而其論臣
事君也不曰以忠則曰以道是所望之於臣者
又何莫而非禹臯稷契謨明弼諧之事耶玆曰
未能所以教天下之不能也不然鄉黨一篇所
記乎在朝之容事君之禮夫固無一不盡者而
豈眞有所未能哉噫公孫碩膚赤舄几几周公
不自聖之心也而孔子之未能其亦心周公之
心者哉
畏天命畏大人畏聖人之言
===
羅用敬
同考試官教諭古批詞理精到無滲漏處他作
莫及也
同考試官教諭張批天命大人聖言卽三畏條目
作者多以天命爲主牽强可厭此篇理趣完密皆自得之語佳士也
考試官教諭蔡批莊重爾雅
考試官教諭林批善發明君子主敬之學
聖人列言君子之所畏亦惟一理而已蓋理貫
天人而一之者也然理所當畏君子有一之弗
punctuated:
贊舜，其心惓惓焉，必欲君之爲唐虞。而其論臣事君也，不曰以忠，則曰以道。是所望之於臣者，又何莫而非禹臯稷契謨明弼諧之事耶？玆曰未能，所以教天下之不能也。不然，《鄉黨》一篇所記乎在朝之容、事君之禮，夫固無一不盡者，而豈眞有所未能哉？噫！公孫碩膚，赤舄几几，周公不自聖之心也。而孔子之未能，其亦心周公之心者哉！
畏天命，畏大人，畏聖人之言。
羅用敬
同考試官教諭古批：詞理精到，無滲漏處，他作莫及也。
同考試官教諭張批：天命、大人、聖言，卽三畏條目。作者多以天命爲主，牽强可厭。此篇理趣完密，皆自得之語，佳士也。
考試官教諭蔡批：莊重爾雅。
考試官教諭林批：善發明君子主敬之學。
聖人列言君子之所畏，亦惟一理而已。蓋理貫天人而一之者也。然理所當畏，君子有一之弗
translation_en:
…praising Shun, his heart was earnestly intent upon having his ruler become like the sovereigns of Tang and Yu. When discussing how a minister should serve his ruler, he spoke either of loyalty or of the Way. What, then, did he expect of ministers that was not exemplified by the enlightened counsels and harmonious assistance of Yu, Gao, Ji, and Xie? Here he says that he has not been able to accomplish this in order to instruct those throughout the world who cannot do so. Otherwise, the chapter “Xiangdang” (“Among His Village Community”) records his bearing at court and his ritual conduct in serving his ruler: in none of these did he fail to fulfill his duties. How could there truly have been something he could not accomplish? Ah! “The duke was humble, yet of great merit; his red ceremonial shoes were dignified”—this expresses the Duke of Zhou’s refusal to regard himself as a sage. When Confucius said that he had not been able to accomplish this, was he not likewise taking the Duke of Zhou’s heart as his own?
“He stands in awe of Heaven’s Mandate, of great men, and of the words of sages.”
Luo Yongjing
Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning are exact and penetrating, with no gaps or omissions. Other compositions cannot match it.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Heaven’s Mandate, great men, and the words of sages are precisely the three objects of awe. Writers commonly make Heaven’s Mandate the dominant theme, producing strained and tiresome interpretations. This essay’s exposition of principle is complete and closely reasoned; its words all express the writer’s own understanding. He is an excellent scholar.”
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “Grave, correct, and elegant.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “It admirably elucidates the noble man’s learning centered on reverent attentiveness.”
The sage enumerates the things of which the noble man stands in awe, yet they amount to just one principle. For principle pervades Heaven and humanity and unites them. Yet, among the manifestations of principle that warrant awe, is there even one of which the noble man does not…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
畏乎哉夫子之意若謂天下無心外之理亦無
心外之學是故吾觀於三畏有以見君子之心
矣何則性道之原有天命焉蓋流行于物與之
初昭受于有生之後而人之所以爲人者此而
已矣不畏則罔之生也而非所語事天之學矣
是以君子則畏之隨在而致夫顧諟之誠儼乎
日監之在茲也隨處而敕夫時保之念凜乎帝
則之必察也蓋恐恐焉惟懼夫奉若之弗力而
罔敢以或怠矣畏天命其非畏之一乎有所謂
===
大人焉蓋天命之獨厚所以統天而經世者也
不畏則肆非所語事大之學矣是以君子則畏
之道之所在覿其德而欽翼之懷篤也位之所
在共其法而嚴憚之情切也以之而利見亦卽
以之而祗承畏大人其非畏之一乎有所謂聖
人之言焉闡天命之精微可以信今而法後者
也不畏則玩非所語事聖之學矣是以君子則
畏之聖有謨訓遵之爲定保之徵而罔敢忽也
皇極敷言迪之爲會歸之準而罔敢斁也以之
punctuated: 畏乎哉？夫子之意，若謂天下無心外之理，亦無心外之學。是故吾觀於三畏，有以見君子之心矣。何則？性道之原，有天命焉，蓋流行于物與之初，昭受于有生之後，而人之所以爲人者，此而已矣。不畏則罔之生也，而非所語事天之學矣。是以君子則畏之，隨在而致夫顧諟之誠，儼乎日監之在茲也；隨處而敕夫時保之念，凜乎帝則之必察也。蓋恐恐焉，惟懼夫奉若之弗力，而罔敢以或怠矣。畏天命，其非畏之一乎？有所謂大人焉，蓋天命之獨厚，所以統天而經世者也。不畏則肆，非所語事大之學矣。是以君子則畏之，道之所在，覿其德而欽翼之懷篤也；位之所在，共其法而嚴憚之情切也。以之而利見，亦卽以之而祗承。畏大人，其非畏之一乎？有所謂聖人之言焉，闡天命之精微，可以信今而法後者也。不畏則玩，非所語事聖之學矣。是以君子則畏之，聖有謨訓，遵之爲定保之徵，而罔敢忽也；皇極敷言，迪之爲會歸之準，而罔敢斁也。以之
translation_en:
…hold it in awe? The Master's meaning seems to be that under Heaven there is no principle outside the mind, nor any learning outside the mind. Thus, in contemplating the three objects of awe, I find a means of discerning the gentleman's mind. Why is this? At the source of human nature and the Way lies Heaven's mandate. It flows forth when things are first endowed and is manifestly received after life comes into being [?]; this alone is what makes human beings human. Without awe, one lives by evading principle: this cannot be called the learning of serving Heaven. Therefore the gentleman holds it in awe. Wherever he is, he brings complete sincerity to keeping Heaven's bright mandate constantly in view, solemnly conscious that Heaven watches over him daily, here and now. In every circumstance, he disciplines his resolve continually to preserve it, reverently mindful that the Supreme Lord's standards must be scrutinized. Apprehensive and vigilant, he fears only that his efforts to obey will fall short, and dares never grow slack. Is awe of Heaven's mandate not one of these objects of awe?

There are also those called great men. Exceptionally favored by Heaven's mandate, they embody Heaven's order and bring order to the world. Without awe, one becomes unrestrained: this cannot be called the learning of serving the great. Therefore the gentleman holds them in awe. Where the Way resides in them, he beholds their virtue, and his reverent attentiveness deepens; where they occupy positions of authority, he respectfully observes their rules, and his feelings of solemn awe become keen. Accordingly, he finds benefit in seeing them and likewise receives their directions with reverence. Is awe of great men not one of these objects of awe?

There are also what are called the words of sages. These elucidate the subtle essence of Heaven's mandate, commanding trust in the present and providing models for later generations. Without awe, one treats them lightly: this cannot be called the learning of serving the sages. Therefore the gentleman holds them in awe. The sages have counsels and instructions: he follows them as evidence of how to secure lasting preservation, never daring to neglect them. The August Standard is expounded in words: he follows these as the criterion toward which all should converge, never daring to weary of them. Through these…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而誦服亦即以之而恪守畏聖言又非所畏之
一乎夫天命也大人也聖人之言也天下之理
盡之矣而君子之三畏在焉則事心之學盡之
矣心以會理而敬以約心斯其貫天人之道而
爲君子之學也乎雖然是道也實聖學傳心之
要也堯之兢兢舜之業業而欽天勅天見之典
謨者不一而足此天命之所以常存而言爲世
法動爲世道則大人聖言又其兼總之而無外
者矣故曰敬也者聖學之所以成始成終者也
===
然則君子之畏有三而事天之功統其大矣善
學者當自得之
奮乎百世之上百世之下聞者莫不興起
也
曾如衢
同考試官教諭郭批孟子論夷惠感人之遠止
見其爲百世師作者類能言之獨此作圓活流動如明珠走盤洵不
出於𣪠佳士佳士
同考試官教諭周批藻績蔚然可以爲文矣
punctuated:
而誦服，亦即以之而恪守。畏聖言，又非所畏之一乎？夫天命也，大人也，聖人之言也，天下之理盡之矣，而君子之三畏在焉，則事心之學盡之矣。心以會理，而敬以約心，斯其貫天人之道而爲君子之學也乎？雖然，是道也，實聖學傳心之要也。堯之兢兢，舜之業業，而欽天勅天，見之典謨者，不一而足。此天命之所以常存，而言爲世法，動爲世道，則大人聖言，又其兼總之而無外者矣。故曰：敬也者，聖學之所以成始成終者也。然則君子之畏有三，而事天之功統其大矣。善學者當自得之。

「奮乎百世之上，百世之下，聞者莫不興起也。」
曾如衢

同考試官教諭郭批：孟子論夷惠感人之遠，止見其爲百世師。作者類能言之，獨此作圓活流動，如明珠走盤，洵不出於𣪠。佳士！佳士！

同考試官教諭周批：藻績蔚然，可以爲文矣。
translation_en:
…and recite and embrace them, and likewise observe them scrupulously. Is reverence for the words of sages not also one of the objects of reverence? Heaven’s Mandate, great men, and the words of sages encompass all the principles under Heaven. Since the gentleman’s three objects of reverence lie here, they also encompass the whole learning of tending the mind. The mind comprehends principle, while reverent attentiveness disciplines the mind: is this not the learning of the gentleman that unites the Way of Heaven and humanity? Yet this Way is indeed the essential means by which the learning of the sages transmits the mind. Yao’s vigilance and Shun’s conscientious care, their revering Heaven and ordering affairs in accordance with Heaven, appear in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents in more instances than can be enumerated. This is how Heaven’s Mandate is constantly preserved. Their words serve as models for the world, and their actions as its guide; thus great men and the words of sages are also comprehensively embraced within it, with nothing left outside. Hence it is said: reverent attentiveness is what brings the learning of the sages to fulfillment from beginning to end. Thus, although the gentleman has three objects of reverence, the work of serving Heaven comprehends them all. Those skilled in learning should attain this understanding for themselves.

“Rising to prominence a hundred generations ago, they cause all who hear of them a hundred generations later to be stirred to action.”
Zeng Ruqu

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: When Mencius discusses how far the influence of Boyi and Liuxia Hui extends, he simply shows that they are teachers for a hundred generations. Most writers can explain this, but this composition alone is supple and flowing, like a lustrous pearl rolling on a tray. It truly does not issue from [𣪠, unclear: ?]. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: The literary embellishment and texture are luxuriant: this may indeed count as accomplished writing.

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭蔡批說風動處讀之令人興起
考試官教諭林批流麗中自有典則
大賢於前聖之特行而深賛其風動之遠焉夫
聖人雖遠其可風者固在也是以曠百世而猶
足以動乎人焉謂非百世之師而何哉孟子表
而出之其所感者深矣意蓋曰行之未造其極
者不足以語聖風之未被於遠者不足以語師
以予觀於夷惠夫固得聖人之風而孚信於無
窮者矣何以明之彼夷之前非無聖也而未始
聞乎聖之清惟夷以介乎不可汗之志而特立
於百世之上故言潔已之節而極天下之清者
必歸焉惠之前非無聖也而未始聞乎聖之和
惟惠以由然其可親之行而特起於百世之表
故言同人之量而極天下之和者必歸焉是二
子之獨行無前固先百世而有作然其人已遠
亦宜後百世而無聞矣殊不知夷雖往矣而清
風之播於今者則不與其人俱往焉有感斯興
自足以錫類於不匱惠雖往矣而和風之流於
punctuated:
考試官教諭蔡批：說風動處，讀之令人興起。

考試官教諭林批：流麗中自有典則。

大賢於前聖之特行而深賛其風動之遠焉。夫聖人雖遠，其可風者固在也，是以曠百世而猶足以動乎人焉，謂非百世之師而何哉？孟子表而出之，其所感者深矣。意蓋曰：行之未造其極者，不足以語聖；風之未被於遠者，不足以語師。以予觀於夷惠，夫固得聖人之風而孚信於無窮者矣。何以明之？彼夷之前非無聖也，而未始聞乎聖之清。惟夷以介乎不可汗之志而特立於百世之上，故言潔已之節而極天下之清者，必歸焉。惠之前非無聖也，而未始聞乎聖之和。惟惠以由然其可親之行而特起於百世之表，故言同人之量而極天下之和者，必歸焉。是二子之獨行無前，固先百世而有作；然其人已遠，亦宜後百世而無聞矣。殊不知夷雖往矣，而清風之播於今者，則不與其人俱往焉。有感斯興，自足以錫類於不匱。惠雖往矣，而和風之流於
translation_en:
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of the transforming power of moral influence stirs the reader to emulation.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Within its fluent elegance, it possesses classical standards of its own.”

The great worthy, considering the distinctive conduct of earlier sages, deeply praises the far-reaching power of their moral influence. Though the sages are distant in time, what makes them exemplary assuredly remains. Thus, even across a hundred generations, they can still move others. What could they be called but teachers of a hundred generations? Mencius brings this to light; profound indeed was the impression they made upon him. His meaning is, perhaps: conduct that has not reached its utmost perfection does not warrant speaking of sagehood; influence that has not extended far does not warrant speaking of a teacher. As I see Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui, they indeed possessed the moral influence of sages and commanded trust without end.

How can this be demonstrated? Before Bo Yi, there certainly were sages, but one had not yet heard of purity as the distinctive quality of a sage. Bo Yi alone, with his resolute determination that could not be sullied [?], stood preeminent a hundred generations ago. Hence, when speaking of integrity in keeping oneself pure and of the utmost purity in the world, one must turn to him. Before Liu Xiahui, there certainly were sages, but one had not yet heard of harmony as the distinctive quality of a sage. Liu Xiahui alone, through his naturally approachable conduct [?], rose preeminent beyond a hundred generations. Hence, when speaking of the breadth of spirit that enables one to associate with others and of the utmost harmony in the world, one must turn to him.

The distinctive conduct of these two men was unprecedented: they made their mark a hundred generations ago. Yet, since they themselves are now remote, one might expect that a hundred generations later nothing more would be heard of them. What this overlooks is that, although Bo Yi has passed away, his influence of purity, spreading down to the present, has not passed away with him. Wherever people feel its touch, they rise to emulate him; it is sufficient to bestow goodness upon others without exhaustion. Although Liu Xiahui has passed away, his influence of harmony flows on to …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
後者則不因其人俱泯焉有觸斯動自足以淑
世而益光是故聞夷之風者恥不爲夷聞惠之
風者樂於爲惠風聲所被殆莫已其激發之懷
矣而時其得以限之乎凡有慕清之行者必不
自淪於汙凡有慕和之行者必不自處於薄風
教所孚殆咸動乎思齊之念矣而世其得以間
之乎是非夷之求信於人也蓋以清爲行亦不
過自行其志而已而勃然興思皆欲志夷之志
者固夫人好德之懷也機相感而自速夷特有
===
以啓之耳由是而雖謂清之風至今存焉亦可
也亦非惠之求率乎人也蓋以和爲行亦不過
自信其心而已而翕然嚮風皆欲爲惠之徒者
固夫人秉彞之良也情相協而自應惠特有以
鼓之耳由是而雖謂和之風至今存焉亦宜也
我故曰百世之師也吁後世若此而當世不可
知乎聞風者若此而親炙者不可知乎信乎百
世之師非夷惠不足以當之也雖然孟子甞願
學孔子矣而謂夷惠爲君子所不由兹顧以聖
punctuated: 後者，則不因其人俱泯焉。有觸斯動，自足以淑世而益光。是故聞夷之風者，恥不爲夷；聞惠之風者，樂於爲惠。風聲所被，殆莫已其激發之懷矣，而時其得以限之乎？凡有慕清之行者，必不自淪於汙；凡有慕和之行者，必不自處於薄。風教所孚，殆咸動乎思齊之念矣，而世其得以間之乎？是非夷之求信於人也。蓋以清爲行，亦不過自行其志而已，而勃然興思，皆欲志夷之志者，固夫人好德之懷也。機相感而自速，夷特有以啓之耳。由是而雖謂清之風至今存焉，亦可也。亦非惠之求率乎人也。蓋以和爲行，亦不過自信其心而已，而翕然嚮風，皆欲爲惠之徒者，固夫人秉彞之良也。情相協而自應，惠特有以鼓之耳。由是而雖謂和之風至今存焉，亦宜也。我故曰百世之師也。吁！後世若此，而當世不可知乎？聞風者若此，而親炙者不可知乎？信乎百世之師，非夷惠不足以當之也。雖然，孟子甞願學孔子矣，而謂夷惠爲君子所不由，兹顧以聖
translation_en:
…to later generations does not vanish along with the man himself. Those whom it touches are stirred; this alone suffices to improve the world and shine ever more brightly. Thus those who hear of Bo Yi’s example are ashamed not to emulate him; those who hear of Liu Xiahui’s example delight in emulating him. Wherever their reputation reaches, people can scarcely restrain the inspiration it awakens in their hearts. Can time impose a limit upon it? All who admire purity of conduct will surely not sink into defilement; all who admire harmony of conduct will surely not settle for meanness. Wherever their moral influence wins people’s trust, all are stirred to aspire to equal them. Can the passing generations stand in its way?

This is not because Bo Yi sought recognition from others. In making purity his practice, he merely carried out his own resolve. That people eagerly turn their thoughts toward him, all wishing to share his resolve, arises from the love of virtue inherent in everyone. Their inner impulses resonate and spontaneously draw them onward; Bo Yi merely provides the means to awaken them. Thus it is quite acceptable to say that his influence of purity survives to this day. Nor did Liu Xiahui seek to lead others. In making harmony his practice, he merely remained true to his own heart. That people turn toward his example with one accord, all wishing to become his followers, arises from the goodness of the enduring moral nature everyone possesses. Their feelings accord and respond spontaneously; Liu Xiahui merely provides the means to stir them. Thus it is also fitting to say that his influence of harmony survives to this day.

That is why I call them teachers for a hundred generations. Ah! If their influence upon later generations is like this, can we not infer what it was in their own time? If those who merely hear of their example respond like this, can we not infer how those who received their teaching in person responded? Truly, none but Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui could merit the title of teachers for a hundred generations. Nevertheless, Mengzi once expressed the wish to learn from Kongzi, and said that the paths of Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui were not those a gentleman would follow. Yet here he instead speaks of them as sages…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
人百世之師而亟稱之何哉蓋孔子道大德宏
而無迹學之者沒身鑽仰而不足夷惠志行孤
高而迹著慕之者一日感發興起而有餘故願
學孔子者孟子自待之志也而亟稱夷惠者所
以望天下之人也奈何夫人之學夷惠者未必
能清而先失之隘未得其和而先失之不恭遂
使人曰夷不可學也惠不可學也噫此豈夷惠
之過哉
易
===
與日月合其明
黃文煒
同考試官教諭劉批日月無私照大人合明處
亦只是無私此篇形容殆盡讀之其光燁然
同考試官教諭黎批充暢是大手筆
考試官教諭蔡批發揮大人與日月合明處
詞瑩意足宜冠本房
考試官教諭林批清朗可誦
即大人明同乎天象而利見之義昭矣甚矣至
punctuated:
人、百世之師而亟稱之，何哉？蓋孔子道大德宏而無迹，學之者沒身鑽仰而不足；夷惠志行孤高而迹著，慕之者一日感發興起而有餘。故願學孔子者，孟子自待之志也；而亟稱夷惠者，所以望天下之人也。奈何夫人之學夷惠者，未必能清而先失之隘，未得其和而先失之不恭，遂使人曰：「夷不可學也，惠不可學也。」噫！此豈夷惠之過哉？

易

與日月合其明

黃文煒

同考試官教諭劉批：「日月無私照，大人合明處亦只是無私。此篇形容殆盡，讀之，其光燁然。」

同考試官教諭黎批：「充暢，是大手筆。」

考試官教諭蔡批：「發揮大人與日月合明處，詞瑩意足，宜冠本房。」

考試官教諭林批：「清朗可誦。」

即大人明同乎天象，而利見之義昭矣。甚矣，至
translation_en:
…sages and teachers for a hundred generations, and repeatedly praises them—why is this? Confucius’s Way was great and his virtue vast, yet left no discernible traces. Those who study him spend their whole lives probing and looking up to him, yet still fall short. Boyi and Liuxia Hui were uniquely lofty in aspiration and conduct, and their traces were manifest. Those who admire them can find more than enough inspiration and encouragement in a single day. Thus, wishing to learn from Confucius expressed Mencius’s aspirations for himself; repeatedly praising Boyi and Liuxia Hui expressed his hopes for the people of the world. Yet how is it that those who learn from Boyi and Liuxia Hui fall into narrowness before attaining purity, and into disrespect before attaining harmony? They thereby lead people to say: “Boyi cannot be emulated; Liuxia Hui cannot be emulated.” Alas! How could this be the fault of Boyi and Liuxia Hui?

Book of Changes

“He accords in his brightness with the sun and moon”

Huang Wenwei 黃文煒

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The sun and moon illuminate impartially. Where the great man accords with them in brightness, this too is simply impartiality. This essay describes it almost exhaustively; as one reads it, its radiance shines brilliantly.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “Full and fluent: this is the work of a masterly writer.”

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “It develops the point at which the great man accords in brightness with the sun and moon. Its language is polished and its meaning fully expressed. It deserves first place in this examining section.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Clear and lucid, worthy of recitation.”

Since the great man’s brightness is the same as that of the heavenly bodies, the meaning of ‘it is beneficial to see him’ becomes clear. How great indeed is the utmost…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
明莫大乎日月也而大人之明與之合焉則其
人之利見也宜哉文言申乾九五之義如此其
意若謂德必至於無私者而後爲大聖明必至
於無私者而後爲大明予觀九五之大人蓋以
道爲體而造化爲徒者也無私之心豈獨合德
於天地已乎彼容光必照日月之著其明也吾
見其大而無外矣得天久照日月之貞其明也
吾見其乆而無窮矣大人何以合之蓋其聰明
得之天縱而懋昭丕爽有以旁燭乎萬化之原
===
睿智本於夙成而緝煕光明有以獨炳夫先天
之哲語其體則湛一無累而至虛至靈以通神
明之德者一日月之互其宅也語其用則昭明
有融而常明常覺以通晝夜之道者一日月之
中乎天也故無不照臨者日月以無私之體而
懸象於兩間無不光被者大人以無私之德而
並明於二曜在天在人均之兼照於無外也雖
謂日月先大人而示其精可也謂大人後日月
而會其精亦可也豈非天下之所共仰者乎且
punctuated: 明莫大乎日月也，而大人之明與之合焉，則其人之利見也宜哉！文言申乾九五之義如此。其意若謂德必至於無私者，而後爲大聖；明必至於無私者，而後爲大明。予觀九五之大人，蓋以道爲體而造化爲徒者也。無私之心，豈獨合德於天地已乎？彼容光必照，日月之著其明也，吾見其大而無外矣；得天久照，日月之貞其明也，吾見其乆而無窮矣。大人何以合之？蓋其聰明得之天縱，而懋昭丕爽，有以旁燭乎萬化之原；睿智本於夙成，而緝煕光明，有以獨炳夫先天之哲。語其體，則湛一無累，而至虛至靈，以通神明之德者，一日月之互其宅也；語其用，則昭明有融，而常明常覺，以通晝夜之道者，一日月之中乎天也。故無不照臨者，日月以無私之體而懸象於兩間；無不光被者，大人以無私之德而並明於二曜。在天在人，均之兼照於無外也。雖謂日月先大人而示其精可也，謂大人後日月而會其精亦可也。豈非天下之所共仰者乎？且
translation_en:
…no brightness is greater than that of the sun and moon. Since the great man's brightness accords with theirs, how fitting that it should be beneficial to see him! Thus does the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) elaborate the meaning of the nine in the fifth place of the Qian hexagram. Its intent seems to be that only when virtue reaches complete impartiality does one become a great sage, and only when illumination reaches complete impartiality does it become great illumination. As I contemplate the great man of the nine in the fifth place, he is one who takes the Way as his substance and the processes of creation and transformation as his companions. Does his impartial heart merely accord in virtue with Heaven and Earth?

The sun and moon illuminate even the smallest opening that admits light: this is the manifestation of their brightness, whose greatness, I see, leaves nothing outside it. In accord with Heaven, they shine enduringly: this is the constancy of their brightness, whose duration, I see, is inexhaustible. How does the great man accord with them? His acuity of hearing and sight is Heaven-endowed; brilliantly luminous and greatly discerning, he can shed light everywhere upon the source of all transformations. His sagacity and wisdom were formed early; sustaining and extending his radiance, he alone can manifest the understanding that anticipates Heaven.

As to his substance, it is pure, unified, and unencumbered, utterly empty and utterly responsive. Through it he communes with the potency of spiritual illumination, just as the sun and moon alternate in their dwelling places [?]. As to his operation, it is luminous and pervasive, ever bright and ever aware. Through it he comprehends the Way of day and night, just as the sun and moon occupy the heavens. Thus, illuminating all without exception, the sun and moon hang as celestial images between Heaven and Earth by virtue of their impartial substance. Extending his radiance to all without exception, the great man shines alongside these two luminaries by virtue of his impartial virtue. Whether in Heaven or in the human realm, both shed their light universally, leaving nothing outside it. One may say that the sun and moon precede the great man and reveal their essential brilliance; one may also say that the great man follows the sun and moon and comprehends their essential brilliance. Are these not what all under Heaven look up to together? Moreover…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
月以至明照萬物而麗天之體自成夫不匱之
功大人以大明蒞萬國而光天之下自著夫無
疆之化形上形下均之貞明於不息也雖謂大
人以日月爲紀可也謂日月卽大人之用亦可
也又非天下之所共睹者乎是知自天下有日
月而後際天所覆極地所載者無一不囿之於
光明帲冒之中自天下有大人而後際天所覆
極地所載者無一不納之於廣大高明之内此
大人之明德光輝所以合諸日月而無間也豈
===
有大人興起於上天下顧不利見之而自外者
哉雖然大人豈特同明於日月哉蓋大人在上
則中和位育之所及而陰陽無愆伏日月不薄
蝕何者非其參賛之能事也是故堯舜作而太
和文明之治至今可想謂非聖人有功於造化
可乎噫此至誠無息而高明悠久之化所以與
天地同無極也
自天祐之吉无不利子曰祐者助也天之
所助者順也
punctuated:
月以至明照萬物，而麗天之體自成夫不匱之功；大人以大明蒞萬國，而光天之下自著夫無疆之化。形上形下，均之貞明於不息也。雖謂大人以日月爲紀可也，謂日月卽大人之用亦可也，又非天下之所共睹者乎？是知自天下有日月，而後際天所覆、極地所載者，無一不囿之於光明帲冒之中；自天下有大人，而後際天所覆、極地所載者，無一不納之於廣大高明之内。此大人之明德光輝所以合諸日月而無間也。豈有大人興起於上，天下顧不利見之而自外者哉？雖然，大人豈特同明於日月哉？蓋大人在上，則中和位育之所及，而陰陽無愆伏，日月不薄蝕，何者非其參賛之能事也？是故堯舜作，而太和文明之治至今可想，謂非聖人有功於造化可乎？噫！此至誠無息而高明悠久之化，所以與天地同無極也。

自天祐之，吉无不利。子曰：「祐者，助也。天之所助者，順也。」
translation_en:
…the moon illuminates the myriad things with consummate brightness, and its substance, attached to heaven, naturally achieves an inexhaustible efficacy. The great man presides over the myriad states with his great illumination, and his radiance beneath heaven naturally manifests a boundless transforming influence. What lies above physical form and what lies within physical form alike remain steadfastly luminous without cease. One may say that the great man takes the sun and moon as his standard; one may also say that the sun and moon are themselves the functioning of the great man. Is this not also something witnessed by all under Heaven?

Thus we know that, once the sun and moon existed in the world, nothing throughout the utmost extent of what heaven covers and earth sustains lay outside the shelter of their light. Once the great man existed in the world, nothing throughout the utmost extent of what heaven covers and earth sustains remained outside the embrace of his breadth, grandeur, loftiness, and illumination. This is why the radiance of the great man’s luminous virtue accords seamlessly with the sun and moon. Could a great man arise in high station, yet those under Heaven fail to find benefit in seeing him and instead exclude themselves?

Even so, does the great man merely share the brightness of the sun and moon? When the great man occupies high station, equilibrium and harmony extend their influence, setting things in their proper places and nourishing their growth: yin and yang neither transgress their proper seasons nor remain hidden, and the sun and moon suffer no obscuration or eclipse. Which of these is not an achievement of his participation in and assistance to the work of transformation? Thus, when Yao and Shun arose, they brought about a reign of supreme harmony and cultured illumination that we can still envision today. Can one say that the sages made no contribution to the processes of creation and transformation? Ah! Such is the transforming influence of utmost sincerity, unceasing, lofty, luminous, and enduring: hence it shares the boundlessness of heaven and earth.

“Heaven blesses him. Auspicious; nothing is unfavorable.” The Master said: “To bless means to assist. Those whom Heaven assists are those who accord with it.”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吳學詩
同考試官教諭金批上九以順德得天自是感
通之理此作詞意渾融發明詳盡必究心於易道者
同考試官教諭黎批順字就上九持盈處發
揮良是
考試官教諭蔡批天人相與之際藹然言意之表
考試官教諭林批潔淨精微
大傳釋上爻得天之義必推天心之所與者以
見之焉蓋天者理而已矣上九能順乎理則亦
===
何疑於天之祐也哉大傳舉而釋之所以慶聖
人之得天也若曰天人相與之際至遠而至邇
者也感通之機不爽而昭格之本在德周公於
大有上九曰自天祐之吉无不利者豈無謂哉
蓋天下有徼福於回者徼非祐也乃其上帝厚
寵綏之命而以達衆動之宜者莫非吉也若或
翼之俾不迷也而我無心於徼也一人承簡在
之休而以衍豐亨之業者莫非利也若或引之
俾不替也而非有心於求也是祐之爲言助也
punctuated:
吳學詩

同考試官教諭金批：上九以順德得天，自是感通之理。此作詞意渾融，發明詳盡，必究心於易道者。

同考試官教諭黎批：順字就上九持盈處發揮，良是。

考試官教諭蔡批：天人相與之際，藹然言意之表。

考試官教諭林批：潔淨精微。

大傳釋上爻得天之義，必推天心之所與者以見之焉。蓋天者，理而已矣。上九能順乎理，則亦何疑於天之祐也哉？大傳舉而釋之，所以慶聖人之得天也。若曰：天人相與之際，至遠而至邇者也。感通之機不爽，而昭格之本在德。周公於大有上九曰：「自天祐之，吉无不利。」者，豈無謂哉？蓋天下有徼福於回者，徼非祐也。乃其上帝厚寵綏之命，而以達衆動之宜者，莫非吉也。若或翼之，俾不迷也，而我無心於徼也。一人承簡在之休，而以衍豐亨之業者，莫非利也。若或引之，俾不替也，而非有心於求也。是祐之爲言，助也。
translation_en:
Wu Xueshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor: The top nine wins Heaven’s favor through compliant virtue: this is naturally the principle of stimulus and response. This composition thoroughly integrates wording and meaning, and its exposition is detailed and exhaustive. Its author must have devoted himself to the Way of the Changes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: It is very sound to develop the word “compliance” in terms of the top nine’s preservation of fullness.

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: The relationship between Heaven and humanity is richly apparent beyond the explicit words and ideas.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Pure and clear, subtle and refined.

In explaining how the top line wins Heaven’s favor, the Great Commentary necessarily traces what Heaven’s heart approves, thereby making the meaning apparent. Heaven is simply principle. If the top nine can comply with principle, what doubt can there be that Heaven will aid it? The Great Commentary cites and explains this to celebrate the sage’s attainment of Heaven’s favor. It is as though it says: The relationship between Heaven and humanity is at once most distant and most intimate. The workings of stimulus and response never err, and the foundation for reaching Heaven lies in virtue. In the top nine of Great Possession, the Duke of Zhou says, “Heaven itself aids him. Auspicious; nothing is unfavorable.” Could these words be without significance?

There are those in the world who seek blessings through crooked means [?]; seeking them in this way is not receiving aid. But when the Lord on High bestows abundant favor and a mandate of reassurance, enabling every action to attain what is fitting, all is auspicious. It is as though someone supports him, keeping him from going astray, while he himself has no intention of soliciting blessings. When the One Man receives the blessing of being chosen by Heaven, thereby extending his enterprise of abundance and prosperity, all is favorable. It is as though someone guides him, keeping him from falling away, without his deliberately seeking it. Thus, what “aid” means is “assistance” …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而豈天之有私於上九也哉蓋以上九當大有
之時而慎守乎持盈之戒斯其於動也順矣則
一德之潜通天心之所與者恒在焉履全盛之
運而每廑夫不溢之防斯其於理也得矣則至
順之克當而上帝之所歆者胥此焉是以鑒其
衷而陰隲之自莫巳其繁祉之綏戩穀俾矣而
昌熾繼之祿位名壽之必得者固德福相因之
理也而謂順德非天之所祐可乎篤其祜而申
錫之自莫替其景福之介純嘏俾矣而耆艾因
===
之安富尊榮之大備者固天人感應之機也而
謂天之不祐順德也又可乎是知動不過則而
動罔不吉者因之其吉也天之俾爾多益也而
實人之昭受用休也行無越思而行無不利者
因之其利也天之降爾遐福也而實人之體信
達順也噫此上九備至順之德而又履信尚賢
焉則其自天祐之也焉可誣哉大抵天祐聖人
與聖人之得天又不屑屑在於形迹昭著之間
而惟顧在我所以感格之者何如耳是故天心
punctuated: 而豈天之有私於上九也哉？蓋以上九當大有之時，而慎守乎持盈之戒，斯其於動也順矣，則一德之潜通，天心之所與者恒在焉。履全盛之運，而每廑夫不溢之防，斯其於理也得矣，則至順之克當，而上帝之所歆者胥此焉。是以鑒其衷而陰隲之，自莫巳其繁祉之綏。戩穀俾矣，而昌熾繼之；祿位名壽之必得者，固德福相因之理也，而謂順德非天之所祐，可乎？篤其祜而申錫之，自莫替其景福之介。純嘏俾矣，而耆艾因之；安富尊榮之大備者，固天人感應之機也，而謂天之不祐順德也，又可乎？是知動不過則，而動罔不吉者因之。其吉也，天之俾爾多益也，而實人之昭受用休也。行無越思，而行無不利者因之。其利也，天之降爾遐福也，而實人之體信達順也。噫！此上九備至順之德，而又履信尚賢焉，則其自天祐之也，焉可誣哉？大抵天祐聖人，與聖人之得天，又不屑屑在於形迹昭著之間，而惟顧在我所以感格之者何如耳。是故天心
translation_en:
… Yet how could Heaven be showing partiality to the topmost nine? For the topmost nine, occupying its position in the time of Great Possession, carefully observes the admonition to preserve fullness. Its actions thus accord with Heaven, and through the unseen communion of its undivided virtue, Heaven’s favor remains constantly with it. Amid the utmost flourishing, it continually takes care to guard against overflowing. It thereby accords with principle: its perfect compliance is fitting, and all that the Lord on High delights in lies here. Thus Heaven examines its innermost intentions and secretly establishes its fortunes, never ceasing to bestow abundant blessings. Prosperity and goodness are granted, and flourishing abundance follows. That emolument, rank, reputation, and longevity must be obtained is indeed the principle by which virtue and blessings follow upon one another. Can one then say that compliant virtue is not what Heaven assists? Heaven deepens its blessings and repeatedly bestows them, never failing to grant great felicity. Ample blessings are granted, and ripe old age follows. The full possession of peace, wealth, honor, and glory is indeed the working of the mutual response between Heaven and humanity. Can one then say that Heaven does not assist compliant virtue?

From this we know that when actions do not exceed the rule, unfailing good fortune in action follows. This good fortune is Heaven’s granting you manifold benefits; yet in truth it is a person’s illustriously receiving and enjoying Heaven’s favor. When conduct does not go beyond proper deliberation, unfailing advantage in conduct follows. This advantage is Heaven’s sending down enduring blessings upon you; yet in truth it is a person’s embodying trustworthiness and fully realizing compliance. Ah! This topmost nine possesses the virtue of perfect compliance, and moreover practices trustworthiness and honors the worthy. How, then, could its being “assisted by Heaven” be deemed false? Generally speaking, Heaven’s assistance to the sage, and the sage’s gaining Heaven’s favor, are not narrowly confined to outward signs and manifest traces. They depend solely on how well we ourselves move Heaven and bring about its response. Thus Heaven’s heart …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
降康祐也而天心仁愛亦祐也此堯湯之際而
儆予而自責者其心曰惓惓焉惟下民之咨而
必欲置之於各得其所之天而後已焉斯其爲
敬天之至而得天之實也乎夫民心悅而天意
得則善得天心者得諸民心而已矣故又曰人
之所助者信也
書
夔曰戛擊鳴球搏拊琴瑟以詠祖考來格
虞賓在位羣后德讓下管鼗鼓合止柷
===
敔笙鏞以間鳥獸蹌蹌簫韶九成鳳凰
來儀夔曰於予擊石拊石百獸率舞庶
尹允諧
吳國宗
同考試官教諭郭批此題不難于作而難於隱
括對待是篇悠揚婉曲讀之鏘然若有餘韻佳士也宜冠本房
同考試官教諭周批聖世太和氣象形容殆盡
考試官教諭蔡批長題收斂悉中矩矱
考試官教諭林批莊重明確
punctuated:
降康，祐也；而天心仁愛，亦祐也。此堯湯之際，而儆予而自責者，其心曰：「惓惓焉，惟下民之咨，而必欲置之於各得其所之天而後已焉。」斯其爲敬天之至，而得天之實也乎！夫民心悅而天意得，則善得天心者，得諸民心而已矣。故又曰：「人之所助者，信也。」
書
夔曰：「戛擊鳴球，搏拊琴瑟以詠，祖考來格。虞賓在位，羣后德讓。下管鼗鼓，合止柷敔，笙鏞以間。鳥獸蹌蹌。簫韶九成，鳳凰來儀。」夔曰：「於！予擊石拊石，百獸率舞，庶尹允諧。」
吳國宗
同考試官教諭郭批：「此題不難于作，而難於隱括對待。是篇悠揚婉曲，讀之鏘然，若有餘韻。佳士也，宜冠本房。」
同考試官教諭周批：「聖世太和氣象，形容殆盡。」
考試官教諭蔡批：「長題收斂，悉中矩矱。」
考試官教諭林批：「莊重明確。」
translation_en:
…To send down well-being is assistance; Heaven’s benevolent concern is also assistance. Thus, in the times of Yao and Tang, their admonishing themselves and taking blame upon themselves expressed this thought: “With tireless solicitude, we attend to the common people’s laments, determined not to rest until we have placed them in a world where each finds a fitting place.” Is this not the utmost reverence for Heaven and the true attainment of Heaven’s favor? When the people’s hearts are pleased, Heaven’s intent is fulfilled. Thus those who know how to win Heaven’s heart do so simply through the hearts of the people. Hence it is also said: “What earns a person the assistance of others is trustworthiness.”
Book of Documents
Kui said: “I strike the resonant jade chimes, beat the hand drums, and play the qin and se zithers to accompany singing; the ancestral spirits come to us. The guest of Yu occupies his place, and the assembled lords defer to one another in virtue. Below the hall, pipes, pellet drums, and drums sound; the wooden zhu and yu mark the music’s beginning and end, while mouth organs and great bells alternate. Birds and beasts move rhythmically. When the nine movements of the Shao music have been performed, phoenixes come in stately bearing.” Kui said: “Ah! I strike the stones and tap the stones; all the beasts dance together, and the many officials are truly in harmony.”
Wu Guozong
Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: “The difficulty of this topic lies not in composing an essay, but in drawing its contents together and balancing its corresponding parts. This essay flows melodiously, with graceful turns; read aloud, it rings out as though its resonance lingered. A fine scholar: he should rank first in this examination room.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The atmosphere of supreme harmony in a sage’s age is depicted almost exhaustively.”
Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The lengthy topic is drawn into a compact whole, entirely in keeping with the standards.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Dignified, clear, and precise.”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖臣兩述聖樂感通之妙以見和德之致也甚
矣韶樂之盡美也觀其感通之妙見於聖臣自
述者其太和之盛為何如哉虞史記樂載后夔
之言其意豈不以樂也者所以崇德象成者也
有虞之時舜以帝德召和于上矣以予典樂而
親承帝命其播帝德之和亦久矣感通之妙豈
無可言者乎以宗廟之樂言之有作于堂上者
鳴球琴瑟是也或戛擊之或搏拊之其聲清越
已有餘音而因以合夫人聲之詠歌者但見洋
===
洋在上祖考格焉虞賓遜焉有作于堂下者竹
管鼗鼓祝敔笙鏞是也或從其律或均其節其
聲廣大已有餘韻而因以間夫人聲之詠歌者
但見蹌蹌鳥獸翔于庭焉止于階焉夫固幽足
以感神微足以動物矣若乃自一成以至九成
而此簫韶之樂有以極始終條理之全則九敘
之歌九韶之舞于是大備將見太和動盪而鳳
凰且來儀焉予固甞摠觀其間而有感于苞彩
之德輝矣以朝廷之樂言之有大石之磬焉其
punctuated:
聖臣兩述聖樂感通之妙，以見和德之致也。甚矣，韶樂之盡美也！觀其感通之妙，見於聖臣自述者，其太和之盛為何如哉！虞史記樂，載后夔之言，其意豈不以樂也者，所以崇德象成者也？有虞之時，舜以帝德召和于上矣。以予典樂，而親承帝命，其播帝德之和亦久矣，感通之妙豈無可言者乎？

translation_en:
The sage minister twice recounts the marvels of the spiritual resonance elicited by sagely music, thereby revealing the fullest realization of harmonious virtue. How consummate is the beauty of Shao music! When we consider the marvelous resonance described by the sage minister himself, how abundant must that supreme harmony have been! In recording music, the historian of Yu included the words of Kui, the Director of Music. Was not his meaning that music exalts virtue and gives visible form to accomplished achievement? In the time of Yu, Shun, through his imperial virtue, summoned harmony from above. Charged with directing music, I personally received the emperor’s command and have long disseminated the harmony of his virtue. Could there be nothing to recount of its marvelous power to elicit a response?
Speaking of the music of the ancestral temple, there are instruments played above in the hall: the resonant jade chimes and the qin and se zithers. They are struck or tapped [?]; their tones are clear and far-reaching, with lingering echoes. When joined with the singing of human voices, one perceives an abundant presence above: the ancestral spirits arrive, and the guest of Yu yields his place. There are instruments played below the hall: bamboo pipes, pellet drums, drums, the wooden zhu and yu percussion instruments, mouth organs, and great bells. Some follow the pitches; others regulate the rhythm. Their sound is broad and ample, with lingering resonance. When interspersed with the singing of human voices, birds and beasts appear, moving rhythmically, soaring in the courtyard and alighting upon the steps. In its unseen workings, this music is sufficient to move spirits; in its subtle influence, it is sufficient to stir living creatures. From the first completed movement through the ninth, this music of Xiao Shao fully realizes an ordered coherence from beginning to end. The songs of the nine ordered accomplishments and the dances of the nine Shao movements are thus fully arrayed. One will then see supreme harmony surging forth, and even phoenixes coming to present themselves with stately bearing. I have indeed surveyed all this and been moved by the radiance of virtue embodied in their splendid plumage [?].

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
聲易斂則擊之以揚其訕然之響有小石之磬
焉其聲易揚則拊之以斂其悠然之節夫固立
辨以彰角聲之美和平以啓五音之依矣由是
自脂者以至鱗者而此百獸之類有感于元聲
元氣之和咸相率而舞有賁其容無不畢至至
于庶官之長亦皆和於朝焉予又嘗會逢其盛
而有感于太和之充盈矣吁觀夔之自述如此
一時雍容氣象真有以擅百代聲氣之盛後有
作者虞帝其弗可及矣抑此未易致也舜以重
===
華協德于上而一時如禹如皐如益如稷如契
如龍皆聖人亞匹相聚一堂都俞吁咈以至于
州牧侯伯皆九德吉士和氣薰蒸宇內融液鳳
凰希瑞天所以昭聖治而表帝功豈偶然者哉
予于是乎重有感矣
乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣曰明禋拜手稽首
休享
勞惪
同考試官敎諭郭 批 成王周公以誕保文武受命
punctuated:
聲易斂，則擊之以揚其訕然之響；有小石之磬焉，其聲易揚，則拊之以斂其悠然之節。夫固立辨以彰角聲之美，和平以啓五音之依矣。由是自脂者以至鱗者，而此百獸之類有感于元聲元氣之和，咸相率而舞，有賁其容，無不畢至。至于庶官之長，亦皆和於朝焉。予又嘗會逢其盛，而有感于太和之充盈矣。吁！觀夔之自述如此，一時雍容氣象，真有以擅百代聲氣之盛。後有作者，虞帝其弗可及矣。抑此未易致也。舜以重華協德于上，而一時如禹、如皐、如益、如稷、如契、如龍，皆聖人亞匹，相聚一堂，都俞吁咈。以至于州牧侯伯，皆九德吉士，和氣薰蒸，宇內融液。鳳凰希瑞，天所以昭聖治而表帝功，豈偶然者哉？予于是乎重有感矣。
乃命寧予以秬鬯二卣，曰：「明禋。」拜手稽首，休享。
勞惪
同考試官敎諭郭批：成王、周公以誕保文武受命
translation_en:
…its sound readily subsides, so it is struck to bring forth its ringing resonance [?]. There are also small stone chimes: their sound readily rises, so they are tapped to restrain their lingering cadence. Thus clear distinctions are established [?] to display the beauty of the jue note, while harmonious balance establishes the mutual dependence of the five notes. Consequently, creatures ranging from the fat-bearing [?] to the scaled—all these kinds of beasts—respond to the harmony of primal sound and primal vital energy. They follow one another in dancing, splendid in appearance, and all arrive. Even the heads of the various offices are harmonious at court. I too have encountered this flourishing spectacle and felt the fullness of supreme harmony.
Ah! From Kui’s account of himself, the gracious and composed atmosphere of that age truly possessed a richness of sound and vital energy unsurpassed through a hundred generations. Should another arise afterward, surely he could not equal the emperor of Yu! Yet this was not easily achieved. Above, Shun continued the brilliance of his predecessor and matched his virtue; meanwhile, men such as Yu, Gao, Yi, Ji, Xie, and Long, all near equals of the sage, gathered in one hall, voicing approval and dissent. Even the regional governors and the lords were worthy men endowed with the nine virtues. Harmonious energy permeated everything, blending throughout the realm. The phoenix was a rare auspicious sign through which Heaven made manifest sagely government and displayed the emperor’s achievements. Could this have been mere chance? At this I am moved once again.

Lao De

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
交相望此作獨能言之而辭語典雅可錄以式
同考試官教諭周批能言盛世君臣相與之意取之
考試官教諭蔡批曲贍明確
考試官教諭林批辭暢意足
大臣述賢王命寧乎已禮盛而詞恭焉夫禮莫
盛於事神而賢王以之致敬於大臣焉其尊崇
之意為何如哉大臣述之以達於王其意有在
矣昔周公之在周也王之懿親尊莫至焉作洛
定鼎功莫隆焉則成王之所以致敬于公者宜
===
無所不至而公則述其命寧之詞復達之王以
見君臣相與之盛也其意盖曰誕保重任予所
不敢辭命寧重禮予所不敢當盖王以毖殷頑
民予旦與有責焉而命寧之舉因伻來以達之
然其禮何如哉彼醞黍為酒雖旨且多不過餽
問之常而以秬之和合鬯之香則為交神之禮
王之命寧于予也而以秬鬯二卣焉是以少為
貴也清酤既載而知至敬之無文固不事夫繁
縟黄流在中而知大禮之必簡固不假于備物
punctuated:
交相望，此作獨能言之，而辭語典雅，可錄以式。
同考試官教諭周批：能言盛世君臣相與之意，取之。
考試官教諭蔡批：曲贍明確。
考試官教諭林批：辭暢意足。
大臣述賢王命寧乎已，禮盛而詞恭焉。夫禮莫盛於事神，而賢王以之致敬於大臣焉，其尊崇之意為何如哉！大臣述之以達於王，其意有在矣。昔周公之在周也，王之懿親，尊莫至焉；作洛定鼎，功莫隆焉。則成王之所以致敬于公者，宜無所不至。而公則述其命寧之詞，復達之王，以見君臣相與之盛也。其意盖曰：誕保重任，予所不敢辭；命寧重禮，予所不敢當。盖王以毖殷頑民，予旦與有責焉，而命寧之舉，因伻來以達之。然其禮何如哉？彼醞黍為酒，雖旨且多，不過餽問之常；而以秬之和合鬯之香，則為交神之禮。王之命寧于予也，而以秬鬯二卣焉，是以少為貴也。清酤既載，而知至敬之無文，固不事夫繁縟；黄流在中，而知大禮之必簡，固不假于備物。
translation_en:
…looked to one another with these expectations. This composition alone succeeds in expressing this; its language is dignified and elegant, and it merits inclusion as a model.
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: It succeeds in expressing the spirit of relations between ruler and ministers in a flourishing age. Accept it.
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: Detailed and ample, clear and precise.
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: Fluent in expression and full in meaning.
The great minister recounts how the worthy king commanded that he be honored and comforted [?]: the ceremony was grand, and his words were reverent. No rites are grander than those for serving the spirits, yet the worthy king used these to show respect to a great minister. How profound was his intention to exalt and honor him! The great minister recounted this to the king with a particular purpose.
In former times, when the Duke of Zhou served Zhou, no one surpassed him in dignity as a close kinsman of the king; no achievement surpassed his founding of Luo and installation of the tripods there. Thus King Cheng ought to have spared nothing in showing respect to the duke. Yet the duke repeated the words commanding that he be honored and comforted, addressing them back to the king to reveal the flourishing relationship between ruler and minister. His meaning was essentially this: The weighty responsibility of preserving on a grand scale is one I dare not decline; the solemn rites for honoring and comforting me are something I dare not accept.
For the king seeks to keep the recalcitrant people of Yin under watch, and I, Dan, share responsibility for this. He therefore sent a messenger to convey his intention to honor and comfort me. But what kind of ceremonial offering was this? Millet brewed into wine, however fine and abundant, amounts only to an ordinary gift of greeting. But when the mellow quality of black millet is combined with the fragrance of aromatic wine, it becomes an offering for communion with the spirits. In commanding that I be honored and comforted, the king bestowed two you vessels of aromatic black-millet wine: here, small quantity is prized. With the clear wine set out, one recognizes that the utmost reverence needs no ornament, and certainly does not pursue elaborate embellishment. With the yellow liquor within, one recognizes that the grandest rites must be simple, and certainly do not depend upon a full array of objects…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
其為禮隆矣且其詞曰禮主於潔弗潔則褻斯
秬鬯也致其潔而潔焉禮主於敬弗敬則瀆斯
秬鬯也致其敬而敬焉斯禮也宗廟之所以殷
薦者在是休之至也而拜手稽首以將之饗以
殷薦之休示不敢褻之義也祀禮之所以裸將
者在是美之至也而拜手稽首以達之饗以裸
將之禮示不敢瀆之義也其詞之恭有如此者
蓋王以元祀之典所以報功宗也以功宗之禮
寧予此固非予敢居而受命篤弼豈敢以之自
===
諉哉誕保受命所以繼文武也以所事文武事
予此固非予所敢承而揚文武烈又敢不以之
自勵哉吁周公述成王之所以致敬者如此而
因使以達之萬年之祝責難之恭公之忠愛亦
因之以傳也與抑成王以周公有大勳勞而以
事神之禮事之則是矣其後復賜以郊禘之禮
則非也周公之功周公之分禮非有所可假者
也此豈所以康周公哉故夫子曰魯之郊禘非
禮也又曰禘自既灌而往者吾不欲觀之矣故
punctuated:
其為禮隆矣。且其詞曰：「禮主於潔，弗潔則褻。斯秬鬯也，致其潔而潔焉。禮主於敬，弗敬則瀆。斯秬鬯也，致其敬而敬焉。」斯禮也，宗廟之所以殷薦者在是，休之至也，而拜手稽首以將之；饗以殷薦之休，示不敢褻之義也。祀禮之所以裸將者在是，美之至也，而拜手稽首以達之；饗以裸將之禮，示不敢瀆之義也。其詞之恭有如此者。
蓋王以元祀之典，所以報功宗也。以功宗之禮寧予，此固非予敢居，而受命篤弼，豈敢以之自諉哉？誕保受命，所以繼文武也。以所事文武事予，此固非予所敢承，而揚文武烈，又敢不以之自勵哉？
吁！周公述成王之所以致敬者如此，而因使以達之。萬年之祝，責難之恭，公之忠愛亦因之以傳也與！抑成王以周公有大勳勞，而以事神之禮事之，則是矣；其後復賜以郊禘之禮，則非也。周公之功，周公之分，禮非有所可假者也。此豈所以康周公哉？故夫子曰：「魯之郊禘，非禮也。」又曰：「禘自既灌而往者，吾不欲觀之矣。」故
translation_en:
…The ritual honor was indeed exalted. Moreover, his words declared: “Ritual rests upon purity; without purity, it becomes disrespectful. With this fragrant black-millet wine, he brings purity to its utmost and thereby makes the offering pure. Ritual rests upon reverence; without reverence, it becomes irreverent. With this fragrant black-millet wine, he brings reverence to its utmost and thereby makes the offering reverent.” This ritual embodies what is offered in the grand presentations at the ancestral temple: beneficence in its highest degree. He therefore bows with hands joined and touches his forehead to the ground in receiving it. To be honored with the blessings of a grand presentation calls forth his resolve not to treat it disrespectfully. This also embodies the libation offered in sacrificial ritual: excellence in its highest degree. He therefore bows with hands joined and touches his forehead to the ground to express his response. To be honored with the ritual of libation calls forth his resolve not to treat it irreverently. Such was the humility of his words.
The king employed the rites of the great sacrifice to recompense one preeminent in merit. “To honor me with rites for one preeminent in merit is a distinction I certainly dare not claim. Yet, having received the command to render wholehearted assistance, how could I dare use this as an excuse to evade my duty? To preserve in full the Mandate received is to carry on the work of Kings Wen and Wu. To serve me as one serves Wen and Wu is an honor I certainly dare not accept. Yet how could I dare fail to spur myself on to exalt the achievements of Wen and Wu?”
Ah! The Duke of Zhou thus recounted how King Cheng had shown him reverence, and conveyed his response through the envoy. In his wish that the king might reign for ten thousand years, and in the respect he showed by urging the king to undertake difficult duties, the duke’s loyalty and affection were also passed down! Now, King Cheng was right to honor the Duke of Zhou with rites used in serving the spirits, in recognition of his great meritorious service. But subsequently to grant him the suburban sacrifice and the di ancestral sacrifice was wrong. The Duke of Zhou’s merit was one matter, and his allotted standing another; ritual prerogatives could not be lent to him. How could this bring peace to the Duke of Zhou? Thus the Master said: “Lu’s suburban and di sacrifices are contrary to ritual.” He also said: “At the di sacrifice, once the libation has been poured, I have no wish to watch what follows.” Therefore…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
當周公之時而用裸禮則爲報功當周公之後
而用禘祭則爲失禮使魯而可禘也則當其時
也周公何以曰予不敢宿禋于文王武王哉
詩

執訊獲醜薄言還歸

氣象今猶想見其盛
===
同考試官教諭古批曲盡王者勞還率之意
考試官教諭蔡批發明凱還之樂結復歸功
君上尤爲有見

詩人述大將乘時而遂凱還之慶太平之象見
矣夫凱還之慶王國之所深願而况事與時會
其樂寧有極耶出車之詩王者勞還率而作也
述其凱還之事乃曰王者之命將也固貴有可
成之功而戎功之告成也每難於及時之遇我

If Lu were entitled to perform the di sacrifice, why did the Duke of Zhou say at the time, “I dare not delay in sacrificing to King Wen and King Wu” [?]?

Book of Odes
“The spring days lengthen; plants and trees grow luxuriantly. Orioles sing in harmony; those gathering white southernwood are numerous. We seize prisoners for interrogation and capture the enemy host; then we return home.”
Chen Wensui

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “Achievement and triumphant celebration—the feelings and scene are vividly present. Even now one can imagine the grandeur of this age of peace.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Brilliantly expressive language: an excellent composition.”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
大將制勝以班師也獨無可言者乎故仰觀於
天有春日焉則遲遲而暄妍者有以發舒其大
和之氣俯察于地有卉木焉則萋萋而暢茂者
有以顯洩乎化育之神至於倉庚得氣之先感
時而鳴者也傾聽之下吾聞其喈喈耳矣無情
之物若有情以和唱之者采蘩治蠶之務女工
伊始者也拭目之餘吾見其祁祁耳矣用力之
齊若有意以順助之者是景與事而適會人與
物而咸熈乘斯時也樂斯景也我大將何幸而
===
値之蓋蠢茲醜虜敢於陸梁倡之者渠魁而脅
從之者羣醜也此人心所共憤使弗獲而執之
則疆埸猶未之靖而大將亦用是爲戚矣今執
彼訊焉罪人斯得莫我敢膺也獲此醜焉黨惡
悉除無或奔突也於是慶膚功之日奏而振旅
以言旋撫景興懷非復黍稷之方華矣一時相
關之意不協上下以承休乎樂塵氛之無警而
奏凱以言歸感時觸物非復雨雪之載塗矣一
念交暢之情不與人物而共適乎是則大將將
punctuated: 大將制勝以班師也，獨無可言者乎？故仰觀於天，有春日焉，則遲遲而暄妍者，有以發舒其大和之氣；俯察于地，有卉木焉，則萋萋而暢茂者，有以顯洩乎化育之神。至於倉庚，得氣之先、感時而鳴者也，傾聽之下，吾聞其喈喈耳矣，無情之物若有情以和唱之者；采蘩，治蠶之務、女工伊始者也，拭目之餘，吾見其祁祁耳矣，用力之齊若有意以順助之者。是景與事而適會，人與物而咸熈。乘斯時也，樂斯景也，我大將何幸而値之！蓋蠢茲醜虜，敢於陸梁，倡之者渠魁，而脅從之者羣醜也。此人心所共憤，使弗獲而執之，則疆埸猶未之靖，而大將亦用是爲戚矣。今執彼訊焉，罪人斯得，莫我敢膺也；獲此醜焉，黨惡悉除，無或奔突也。於是慶膚功之日奏，而振旅以言旋，撫景興懷，非復黍稷之方華矣，一時相關之意，不協上下以承休乎？樂塵氛之無警，而奏凱以言歸，感時觸物，非復雨雪之載塗矣，一念交暢之情，不與人物而共適乎？是則大將將
translation_en:
…our great general has won victory and brought his army home: is there nothing here worth recounting? Looking upward to heaven, we see the spring days, long, warm, and lovely, unfolding the breath of supreme harmony. Looking downward to earth, we see plants and trees, lush and flourishing, revealing the wondrous workings of nature’s nurture. As for the orioles, they are the first to receive the season’s vital breath and sing in response. Listening intently, I hear their harmonious calls: creatures without human feeling seem endowed with feeling, joining in the song. Gathering white southernwood is a task of tending silkworms, marking the beginning of women’s work. Rubbing my eyes to look, I see the women in their numbers: their concerted effort seems deliberately offered in willing assistance. Thus the scenery and the occasion fittingly coincide, and people and all other beings alike flourish. To return at this time and delight in this scene—how fortunate our great general is to encounter it!
These vile foes had stirred and dared to run rampant. Their ringleaders instigated the trouble, while the host of lesser villains followed under coercion. This aroused indignation in every heart. Had they not been captured and seized, the frontier would still have been unsettled, and the great general would likewise have grieved over it. Now those captives have been seized for questioning: the guilty have been taken, and none dares oppose us. These villains have been captured: their wicked confederates are wholly eliminated, and none remains to charge about unchecked. Thus, rejoicing that great achievements are being reported day after day, he orders his troops for the return. Contemplating the scene, his thoughts stir: it is no longer the season when the millet crops were just flowering. Does not the sense of mutual concern at this moment unite high and low in receiving these blessings? Delighting that no alarm arises from the dust of warfare, he returns to the strains of victory. Moved by the season and the things around him, he finds that snow and rain no longer mire the roads. Does not this shared feeling of joy bring him contentment together with people and all other beings? Thus the great general, in carrying out …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
命以成功慶莫大焉及時以奏凱樂莫加焉一
者探情而代言之而中興氣象不亦可想見乎
大抵三軍之命係於將兆民之慶係於君分閫
而治而王者實為王焉豈惟師貞丈人吉哉故
徐方既同天子之功成周之世道出萬全而禦
戎之策至今尚之則夫西戎伐而獫狁平又不
特一南仲耳雖然柔遠能邇必內順治而後外
威嚴其本又豈在威強而已哉故曰明王慎德
四夷咸賓
===
君子萬年介爾昭明
羅用敬
同考試官教諭張批臣子忠愛之誠祝願之意
最難措詞此作獨得敷揚之體
同考試官教諭朱批講昭明字識見精到
考試官教諭蔡批平易中有雋永之味即氣
充詞暢錄之
考試官教諭林批文思縝密
周臣之祝君惟欲其永膺乎光大之休焉蓋福
punctuated:
命以成功，慶莫大焉；及時以奏凱，樂莫加焉。一者探情而代言之，而中興氣象不亦可想見乎？大抵三軍之命係於將，兆民之慶係於君。分閫而治，而王者實為王焉，豈惟「師貞，丈人吉」哉？故徐方既同，天子之功，成周之世道，出萬全而禦戎之策，至今尚之。則夫西戎伐而獫狁平，又不特一南仲耳。雖然，柔遠能邇，必內順治而後外威嚴，其本又豈在威強而已哉？故曰：「明王慎德，四夷咸賓。」

君子萬年，介爾昭明。
羅用敬

同考試官教諭張批：臣子忠愛之誠、祝願之意，最難措詞。此作獨得敷揚之體。
同考試官教諭朱批：講昭明字，識見精到。
考試官教諭蔡批：平易中有雋永之味，即氣充詞暢，錄之。
考試官教諭林批：文思縝密。

周臣之祝君，惟欲其永膺乎光大之休焉。蓋福
translation_en:
…having fulfilled his commission with success, no celebration could be greater; returning in good time with songs of victory, no joy could surpass it. The poet probes these feelings and gives voice to them [?]: can we not thereby envision the flourishing restoration? In general, the lives of the armies depend upon the general, and the blessings of the myriad people depend upon the ruler. Though a general exercises authority within his allotted command, it is the king who truly acts as king. Is this merely what is meant by “The army must be steadfast; for a mature man, good fortune”? Thus, when the lands of Xu were brought into concord, the achievement belonged to the Son of Heaven. The political order of the Zhou, and its strategy for resisting the Rong with complete assurance of success, remain esteemed to this day. Hence the campaign against the Western Rong and the pacification of the Xianyun were not the achievement of Nan Zhong alone. Nevertheless, to conciliate those far away and win over those nearby, there must first be orderly government within before authority commands respect abroad. How could its foundation lie in coercive strength alone? Thus it is said: “The enlightened king attends carefully to his virtue, and the peoples of the four quarters all come as guests.”

“May the lord live ten thousand years; may you be blessed with radiant glory.”
Luo Yongjing

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “A subject’s sincere loyalty and love, and his wishes for his ruler, are exceedingly difficult to put into words. This composition alone achieves the proper manner of expounding them.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: “The discussion of the words ‘radiant glory’ displays precise and penetrating insight.”
Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “Within its plain simplicity lies a lasting savor. Its vigor is full and its expression fluent: include it.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The composition’s thought is closely and carefully structured.”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
至於光大人君莫大之休也臣子於此猶欲進
之悠久焉忠愛之情溢於言表矣旣醉之雅父
兄所以荅行葦也謂夫人君以一身而膺天下
之大任亦宜以一身而萃天下之大福我之祝
願於君者豈惟介以景福已哉自今觀之向離
出治天下仰文明之盛代天弘化四方荷光被
之休吾君之福固已極於昭明矣使不進之於
悠久亦非祝望之意也惟願簡在之命默隆夫
眷顧之心於萬斯年推之爲有秩之祜也寵綏
===
之仁陰隲於昭受之下萬有千歲引之爲永錫
之極也自其身而言之以令德則丕顯焉以志
氣則清明焉玄機雖泯於無形而元吉實顯於
有象自其國而言之以土宇則昄章焉以治教
則休明焉天心雖隱於至微而瑞慶實彰於莫
掩廣單厚之洪休有以培國家之元氣萬年此
君子萬年此昭明也福與時而俱積吾見其亹
亹之不厭矣衍多益之餘澤有以煥天子之耿
光萬年此昭明萬年此壽考也慶與日而竝茂
punctuated: 至於光大，人君莫大之休也。臣子於此猶欲進之悠久焉，忠愛之情溢於言表矣。《旣醉》之雅，父兄所以荅《行葦》也。謂夫人君以一身而膺天下之大任，亦宜以一身而萃天下之大福。我之祝願於君者，豈惟介以景福已哉？自今觀之，向離出治，天下仰文明之盛；代天弘化，四方荷光被之休。吾君之福固已極於昭明矣，使不進之於悠久，亦非祝望之意也。惟願簡在之命，默隆夫眷顧之心，於萬斯年，推之爲有秩之祜也；寵綏之仁，陰隲於昭受之下，萬有千歲，引之爲永錫之極也。自其身而言之，以令德則丕顯焉，以志氣則清明焉。玄機雖泯於無形，而元吉實顯於有象。自其國而言之，以土宇則昄章焉，以治教則休明焉。天心雖隱於至微，而瑞慶實彰於莫掩。廣單厚之洪休，有以培國家之元氣，萬年此君子，萬年此昭明也。福與時而俱積，吾見其亹亹之不厭矣。衍多益之餘澤，有以煥天子之耿光，萬年此昭明，萬年此壽考也。慶與日而竝茂
translation_en:
…to attain radiance and greatness is the greatest blessing a ruler can enjoy. Yet his servants and subjects would wish to extend it into perpetuity: their loyal affection overflows beyond their words. The ode “Already Drunk” (Ji zui) is the response of the elder kinsmen to “Reeds by the Path” (Xing wei). Its meaning is that, since the ruler alone bears the great responsibility for all under Heaven, he should also gather into his own person all the great blessings of the world. Could our wishes for our ruler amount merely to helping him obtain great blessings?

Looking at the present, he faces south to govern, and all under Heaven look up to the flourishing of his cultured brilliance; he spreads transforming influence on Heaven’s behalf, and the four quarters receive the blessing of his far-reaching radiance. Our ruler’s blessings have indeed reached the utmost in luminous splendor. Yet unless these are extended into perpetuity, the intent of our prayers and hopes remains unfulfilled. We wish only that Heaven’s mandate, which has singled him out, may silently deepen Heaven’s loving regard, extending it into enduring blessings for ten thousand years; and that Heaven’s benevolence in favoring and protecting him may work unseen beneath the blessings he manifestly receives, prolonging them for a thousand and ten thousand years into the fullest measure of bounty bestowed forever.

Speaking of his person, his excellent virtue is greatly illustrious, and his resolve and spirit are clear and bright. Though the mysterious workings remain concealed and formless, supreme good fortune appears in tangible signs. Speaking of his realm, its territories are vast and splendid, and its government and instruction are admirable and enlightened. Though Heaven’s intention lies hidden in the utmost subtlety, auspicious signs and blessings are so manifest that they cannot be concealed. By enlarging these abundant, generous blessings, the vital strength of the state is nurtured: ten thousand years for this lord, and ten thousand years for this luminous splendor! As blessings accumulate with time, I see his tireless diligence. By extending the overflowing bounty that ever increases, the brilliant glory of the Son of Heaven is made resplendent: ten thousand years for this luminous splendor, and ten thousand years for this longevity! As felicity flourishes with each passing day…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吾見其悠悠之不息矣非君有求於天一機之
交感自以一身而會其全光明俊偉之業殆與
天地相為無疆者乎非我有私於君一念之潛
孚自以一人而履其盛緝熈純嘏之福殆與日
月相為貞明者乎必如是而後吾君之福可底
於純全而吾人報答之心庶乎其少罄矣噫詩
人其善於祝頌者與愚於是而益知周臣愛君
之無已也蓋三代而上稱極治者莫堯舜若也
其光被四表格於上下濬哲文明溫恭允塞昭
===
===
明孰加焉周之臣子惓惓以昭明之福祝其君
是進其君以唐虞之隆愛之至也豈徒為私意
而已哉向非其君先之以行葦之咏感之者無
其機無疆惟休雖臣子之至願亦末由以舒其
誠也故曰上下交而其志同也說者謂太和在
成周宇宙間觀此益信
春秋
夏五月宋人及楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕
秋七月齊侯使國佐如師己酉及國佐
punctuated:
吾見其悠悠之不息矣。非君有求於天，一機之交感，自以一身而會其全，光明俊偉之業，殆與天地相為無疆者乎？非我有私於君，一念之潛孚，自以一人而履其盛，緝熈純嘏之福，殆與日月相為貞明者乎？必如是，而後吾君之福可底於純全，而吾人報答之心庶乎其少罄矣。噫！詩人其善於祝頌者與！愚於是而益知周臣愛君之無已也。蓋三代而上，稱極治者莫堯舜若也。其光被四表，格於上下，濬哲文明，溫恭允塞，昭明孰加焉？周之臣子惓惓以昭明之福祝其君，是進其君以唐虞之隆，愛之至也，豈徒為私意而已哉？向非其君先之以《行葦》之咏，感之者無其機，無疆惟休，雖臣子之至願，亦末由以舒其誠也。故曰：「上下交而其志同也。」說者謂太和在成周宇宙間，觀此益信。

春秋

夏五月，宋人及楚人平。〔宣公十有五年〕
秋七月，齊侯使國佐如師。己酉，及國佐
translation_en:
…I see that it endures on and on without ceasing. It is not that the ruler seeks anything from Heaven: through the reciprocal response of a single impulse, he gathers its fullness in his own person. Would not his radiant and magnificent achievements then endure without limit alongside Heaven and Earth? It is not that we show partiality toward our ruler: through the unspoken sincerity of a single thought, he alone comes to enjoy these blessings in their abundance. Would not the blessings of continuing brilliance and perfect good fortune then shine steadfastly alongside the sun and moon? Only thus can our ruler’s blessings attain complete perfection, and only then may our desire to repay him find some small measure of fulfillment. Ah! How skilled the poet was in offering blessings and praise! From this I understand still more deeply the unceasing love that the ministers of Zhou bore their ruler. In the Three Dynasties and earlier, none reputed to have attained the highest excellence in government equaled Yao and Shun. Their radiance reached the four outermost regions and extended above and below; they were profoundly wise, cultured and enlightened, gracious and reverent, trustworthy and sincere. Who could surpass them in manifest brilliance? When Zhou’s ministers and subjects earnestly wished their ruler the blessing of manifest brilliance, they were urging him toward the flourishing rule of Tang and Yu—that is, Yao and Shun. This was love at its utmost: how could it have been merely an expression of private sentiment? Had their ruler not first inspired them through the song “Thick-Growing Reeds” (Xing wei), there would have been no impulse to move them. Though boundless felicity was the deepest wish of his ministers and subjects, they would have had no means to express their sincerity. Thus it is said: “Those above and below communicate, and their purposes are one.” Commentators say that supreme harmony pervaded the universe in the age of Zhou’s perfected rule; this passage makes that claim still more convincing.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and the men of Chu made peace. 〔The fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
In autumn, in the seventh month, the Marquis of Qi sent Guo Zuo to the army. On the jiyou day, together with Guo Zuo…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
盟于袁婁成公二年癸丑公會晉侯
衞侯鄭伯曹伯宋世子成齊國佐邾人
同盟于戚成公十有五年吳子使札
來聘襄公二十有九年
王廷俊
同考試官教諭許批春秋忠節之士鮮有如四
子者子能約而言之末以夷患斷案最佳
考試官教諭蔡批四傳意難對待此作法度
森嚴老筆也
===
考試官教諭林批斷制謹嚴
聖人修經而深有取於効忠守節之臣焉此見
華元國佐忠於謀國而子臧季札節以立身皆
春秋之僅見者聖人安得不予之以垂訓歟且
忠臣國之衞也是故得其衞則國强此奔奏禦
侮所以見美於詩也春秋之臣知此者吾于宋
而得華元焉于齊而得國佐焉自夫憤起於投
袂而患啓自胥閭晉楚君臣所以處心積慮必
欲剪此然後甘心者使二臣無策以禦之辱國
punctuated:
盟于袁婁，成公二年。癸丑，公會晉侯、衞侯、鄭伯、曹伯、宋世子成、齊國佐、邾人，同盟于戚，成公十有五年。吳子使札來聘，襄公二十有九年。
王廷俊
同考試官教諭許批：春秋忠節之士，鮮有如四子者。子能約而言之，末以夷患斷案，最佳。
考試官教諭蔡批：四傳意難對待，此作法度森嚴，老筆也。
考試官教諭林批：斷制謹嚴。
聖人修經，而深有取於効忠守節之臣焉。此見華元、國佐忠於謀國，而子臧、季札節以立身，皆春秋之僅見者。聖人安得不予之以垂訓歟？且忠臣，國之衞也。是故得其衞則國强，此奔奏禦侮所以見美於詩也。春秋之臣知此者，吾于宋而得華元焉，于齊而得國佐焉。自夫憤起於投袂，而患啓自胥閭，晉楚君臣所以處心積慮，必欲剪此然後甘心者，使二臣無策以禦之，辱國
translation_en:
…made a covenant at Yuanlou. Second year of Duke Cheng. On the guichou day, the duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, Cheng, heir apparent of Song, Guo Zuo of Qi, and a representative of Zhu; together they made a covenant at Qi. Fifteenth year of Duke Cheng. The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit. Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.

Wang Tingjun

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Among the men of loyalty and integrity in the Spring and Autumn period, few equaled these four. You have discussed them concisely; best of all is your concluding judgment concerning the threat from the barbarians.

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: The meanings of the four accounts are difficult to treat in parallel. This composition is rigorously structured—the work of a seasoned writer.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Its judgments and organization are careful and rigorous.

In compiling the Classic, the Sage held in particular esteem ministers who rendered loyal service and upheld their integrity. Here we see Hua Yuan and Guo Zuo loyally planning for their states, and Zizang and Ji Zha establishing their conduct upon integrity—all rare examples in the Spring and Autumn Annals. How could the Sage fail to commend them and thereby transmit instruction to posterity? Loyal ministers are the defenses of a state. Thus, when a state obtains such defenses, it becomes strong. This is why those who hasten about on service and ward off aggression are praised in the Book of Odes. Among the ministers of the Spring and Autumn period who understood this, I find Hua Yuan in Song and Guo Zuo in Qi. When anger flared in a tossing of sleeves, and trouble arose from Xulü [?], the rulers and ministers of Jin and Chu bent their minds and exhausted their ingenuity, determined to crush these states before they would be satisfied. Had these two ministers possessed no strategy to resist them, the humiliation of their states…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
之禍其能免乎幸而元也登床數語啓以君子
善鄰之念佐也倍城固請申以先王德義之訓
卒使楚知愧而旋師晉服義而退舍壯矣哉干
城之衛也噫式微之風下矣孰有忠能强國如
二臣者乎昔下惠受展喜以卻齊君子以爲修
詞之功耳二臣之卻敵如此豈非聞下惠之風
而庶幾者乎聖人予之者其示天下以作忠之
道歟節義人之閑也是故踰其閑則身辱此介
石貞吉所以垂戒于易也春秋人臣知此者吾
===
于曹而得子臧焉于吳而得季札焉自夫逆構
於負芻而傳啓自壽夢父兄國人所以度德讓
賢必欲立此然後爲快者使二子偃然而居焉
失身之辱誰則原之幸而臧也先事奔宋堅以
拒乎諸侯之請札也遠處延陵終不狥乎父兄
之命是其力足以得國而不居智足以守身而
不亂偉矣哉烈丈夫之行也噫揖遜之風微矣
孰有守節敦讓如二子者乎昔伯夷舍孤竹而
不立君子以爲求仁之美耳而二子之辭國如
punctuated:
之禍，其能免乎？幸而元也登床數語，啓以君子善鄰之念；佐也倍城固請，申以先王德義之訓。卒使楚知愧而旋師，晉服義而退舍。壯矣哉，干城之衛也！噫！式微之風下矣，孰有忠能强國如二臣者乎？昔下惠受展喜以卻齊，君子以爲修詞之功耳。二臣之卻敵如此，豈非聞下惠之風而庶幾者乎？聖人予之者，其示天下以作忠之道歟？

節義，人之閑也。是故踰其閑則身辱，此介石貞吉所以垂戒于易也。春秋人臣知此者，吾于曹而得子臧焉，于吳而得季札焉。自夫逆構於負芻，而傳啓自壽夢，父兄國人所以度德讓賢，必欲立此然後爲快者，使二子偃然而居焉，失身之辱，誰則原之？幸而臧也先事奔宋，堅以拒乎諸侯之請；札也遠處延陵，終不狥乎父兄之命。是其力足以得國而不居，智足以守身而不亂。偉矣哉，烈丈夫之行也！噫！揖遜之風微矣，孰有守節敦讓如二子者乎？昔伯夷舍孤竹而不立，君子以爲求仁之美耳。而二子之辭國如
translation_en:
…could they have escaped the calamity of bringing disgrace upon their states? Fortunately, Hua Yuan climbed onto the bed and, with a few words, awakened the thought that a gentleman should maintain good relations with neighboring states. Guo Zuo, with his back to the city [?], pressed his plea firmly, reiterating the former kings’ teachings on virtue and righteousness. In the end, they made Chu feel shame and withdraw its army, and Jin submit to righteousness and pull back its encampment. How stalwart they were as their states’ shields and walls! Alas, the spirit of decline had spread throughout the age. Who possessed loyalty capable of strengthening a state as these two ministers did? Formerly, Liuxia Hui instructed Zhan Xi [?], enabling him to turn back Qi; gentlemen regarded this simply as an achievement of skillfully framed words. Since these two ministers repelled their enemies in this manner, were they not men who had heard of Liuxia Hui’s example and nearly matched it? In approving them, was the Sage not showing the world the way to inspire loyalty?

Integrity and righteousness are a person’s protective bounds. Thus, to cross those bounds is to disgrace oneself. This is why the Book of Changes bequeaths its admonition about being firm as a rock and obtaining good fortune through steadfast correctness. Among the ministers of the Spring and Autumn period who understood this, I find Zizang in Cao and Ji Zha in Wu. Rebellion was plotted by Fuchu, while the proposal to transmit the throne originated with Shoumeng. Fathers, elder brothers, and the people of the states weighed virtue and deferred to worthiness, determined to install these men before they would be satisfied. Had the two men complacently assumed those positions, who could have excused the disgrace of compromising themselves? Fortunately, Zizang fled to Song before matters came to a head and firmly rejected the requests of the feudal lords. Ji Zha withdrew far away to Yanling and never yielded to the commands of his father and elder brothers. Their strength sufficed to obtain a state, yet they would not occupy its throne; their wisdom sufficed to preserve their integrity and keep them from disorder. How magnificent was the conduct of these resolute men! Alas, the tradition of yielding courteously had faded. Who upheld integrity and practiced deference as earnestly as these two men? Formerly, Bo Yi relinquished Guzhu and declined to take the throne; gentlemen regarded this simply as the admirable pursuit of benevolence. Yet these two men’s relinquishment of their states was such…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
此豈非聞伯夷之風而興起者乎聖人美之者
其風天下以立節之道歟夫觀華元國佐之謀
國則夫貽城下之辱如季孫者寧非聖人之所
惡乎以子臧季札猶能辭位不立則夫不義如
鄭突者非王法所必誅乎玆聖人予奪之微意
矣雖然諸臣吾無責焉獨惜季札以出類之賢
竟不能成父兄之志以昌大其國卒釀王僚子
光之禍札實有以啓之也雖其才近乎伯夷而
德則愧乎泰伯矣聖人責備賢者之意蓋如此
===
六月齊侯來獻戎捷莊公三十有一年
楚人使宜申來獻捷僖公二十有一年
廖性之
同考試官敎諭許批行文有矩度用事有根據
此必究心經學者宜錄以式
考試官敎諭蔡批說齊魯事洞達嚴整且發
明胡傳中未備意
考試官敎諭林批典則老成
春秋兩紀獻捷有抑伯國之矜者有貶望國之
punctuated:
此，豈非聞伯夷之風而興起者乎？聖人美之者，其風天下以立節之道歟？夫觀華元、國佐之謀國，則夫貽城下之辱如季孫者，寧非聖人之所惡乎？以子臧、季札猶能辭位不立，則夫不義如鄭突者，非王法所必誅乎？玆聖人予奪之微意矣。雖然，諸臣吾無責焉，獨惜季札以出類之賢，竟不能成父兄之志，以昌大其國，卒釀王僚、子光之禍，札實有以啓之也。雖其才近乎伯夷，而德則愧乎泰伯矣。聖人責備賢者之意，蓋如此。

六月，齊侯來獻戎捷。莊公三十有一年。
楚人使宜申來獻捷。僖公二十有一年。
廖性之。

考試官敎諭林批：典則老成。

春秋兩紀獻捷，有抑伯國之矜者，有貶望國之
translation_en:
…like this, were they not men stirred to action by hearing of Boyi’s example? In praising them, was the Sage perhaps influencing all under Heaven to uphold moral integrity? Considering how Hua Yuan and Guo Zuo planned for their states, could someone like Jisun, who brought upon his state the humiliation of submission beneath its walls, fail to incur the Sage’s condemnation? Since even Zizang and Jizha could decline the throne and refuse enthronement, would someone as unrighteous as Tu of Zheng not necessarily be punished under kingly law? Such is the subtle intent behind the Sage’s approval and disapproval. Nevertheless, I have no reproach for the other ministers. I regret only that Jizha, despite his exceptional worthiness, ultimately failed to fulfill the wishes of his father and elder brothers and bring greatness and prosperity to his state. This finally brewed the calamity involving King Liao and Prince Guang, and Jizha indeed helped set it in motion. Although his abilities approached those of Boyi, his virtue fell short of Taibo’s. Such, it would seem, is the Sage’s intention in demanding perfection of the worthy.

“In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils of victory over the Rong.” Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.
“The men of Chu sent Yishen to present spoils of victory.” Twenty-first year of Duke Xi.
By Liao Xingzhi.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The composition observes proper rules, and its historical references are well grounded. This must be someone who has devoted himself to studying the Classics. It should be selected to serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The discussion of the affairs of Qi and Lu is penetrating, rigorous, and well ordered. It also elucidates ideas not fully developed in Hu’s Commentary.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Classically correct and mature.”
