title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
儒者此見齊以捷遺魯與魯之受於楚皆非也
春秋均貶之也宜哉戎捷之獻人固以善隣予
齊耳而胡以譏桓君子曰齊之捷也豈敵愾之
功乎略遠以勤民侈心肆矣使桓於戎之既獲
也能反而思曰武功之競文德之衰也引咎以
責躬修德以序成欲矜於一捷焉其何敢乃今
之來魯也凡以示威也以誇内也雖以伯主之
尊而躬親執馘不恤焉吾聞彤弓之錫諸侯所
以獻功天子者也魯匹敵之國也顧可遺歟噫
===
鞏朔獻齊捷于王單子猶責以奸先王之禮况
遺於友邦乎吾見戎之捷不足重而桓之辱則
已甚矣其何以主盟中夏哉故春秋特書曰獻
言若獻於王焉卑之者所以責之也宋捷之獻
人固以猾夏罪楚耳而胡以責魯君子曰楚之
獻也豈無故之遺乎志溢而氣驕是恐我矣使
魯當宜申之來也能奮而思曰夷狄之彊中國
之恥也馳詞以拒之聲罪以討之固却而不納
焉豈不可乃今偃然受之怵于勢而忘其辱劫
punctuated:
儒者。此見齊以捷遺魯與魯之受於楚，皆非也。《春秋》均貶之也，宜哉！戎捷之獻，人固以善隣予齊耳，而胡以譏桓。君子曰：「齊之捷也，豈敵愾之功乎？略遠以勤民，侈心肆矣。使桓於戎之既獲也，能反而思曰：『武功之競，文德之衰也。』引咎以責躬，修德以序成，欲矜於一捷焉，其何敢？乃今之來魯也，凡以示威也，以誇内也。雖以伯主之尊，而躬親執馘，不恤焉。吾聞彤弓之錫，諸侯所以獻功天子者也。魯，匹敵之國也，顧可遺歟？噫！鞏朔獻齊捷于王，單子猶責以奸先王之禮，况遺於友邦乎？吾見戎之捷不足重，而桓之辱則已甚矣，其何以主盟中夏哉？」故《春秋》特書曰「獻」，言若獻於王焉，卑之者所以責之也。

宋捷之獻，人固以猾夏罪楚耳，而胡以責魯。君子曰：「楚之獻也，豈無故之遺乎？志溢而氣驕，是恐我矣。使魯當宜申之來也，能奮而思曰：『夷狄之彊，中國之恥也。』馳詞以拒之，聲罪以討之，固却而不納焉，豈不可？乃今偃然受之，怵于勢而忘其辱，劫
translation_en:
…the weakness [?] of the eminent state. This shows that both Qi’s sending its spoils of victory to Lu and Lu’s accepting those from Chu were wrong. How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals censures both equally! As for the presentation of spoils from the Rong, people ordinarily praise Qi for being a good neighbor, but Hu uses it to criticize Duke Huan. The gentleman says: “Was Qi’s victory truly an achievement in combating the king’s enemies? He campaigned in distant lands and wearied his people, giving free rein to extravagant ambitions. Had Duke Huan, after taking captives from the Rong, reflected, ‘Competition in military achievements means the decline of civil virtue,’ acknowledged his faults and reproached himself, and cultivated virtue to bring about orderly accomplishment, how would he have dared boast of a single victory? Yet his coming to Lu was entirely to display his might and vaunt himself before the states within the realm. Despite his exalted standing as hegemon, he personally held the severed ears of the slain and thought nothing of it. I have heard that the bestowal of the vermilion bow concerns the feudal lords’ presentation of their achievements to the Son of Heaven. Lu was a state of equal standing: could such spoils properly be sent to it? Alas! When Gong Shuo presented spoils taken from Qi to the king, Viscount Shan still rebuked him for violating the rites of the former kings. How much more objectionable was sending them to a friendly state! I see nothing worthy of esteem in the victory over the Rong, but Duke Huan’s humiliation was already extreme. How could he preside over the covenants of the central states?” Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically writes “presented,” speaking as though he were presenting them to the king. By lowering his standing, it censures him.

As for the presentation of spoils from Song, people ordinarily condemn Chu for disturbing the Chinese states, but Hu uses it to censure Lu. The gentleman says: “Was Chu’s presentation a gift without an ulterior motive? Its ambition overflowed and its bearing was arrogant: this was meant to intimidate us. Had Lu, when Yishen arrived, roused itself and reflected, ‘The strength of the Yi and Di is the disgrace of the central states,’ sent a message rejecting him, proclaimed Chu’s offenses and called it to account, and firmly refused admission, would that not have been possible? Yet Lu now complacently accepted the offering, frightened by Chu’s power into forgetting its own humiliation, overawed …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
于厥而忘其義雖以上公之俘而甘心受命不
恥焉吾聞荆舒是懲周公所以示子若孫者也
魯周公之胄也顧不能歟噫公孫夏獻陳捷于
晉莊伯猶責以侵小之故况辱及伯主乎吾見
楚之彊日益横而魯之勢日益卑矣其何以宗
諸侯哉故春秋不言宋捷若不出於宋焉諱之
者所以貶之也吁罪桓則人知武功之不足尚
而徼功於外者知所戒矣責魯則人知夷狄之
不可縱而甘心從夷者知所懲矣兹聖人經世
===
之慮乎雖然戎捷不可獻也而陘亭之次何以
美之楚不能懲僖固有歉矣而在泮獻馘詩人
胡以頌之也蓋陘亭之次桓公所以成九合之
功僖公魯之賢君也建學興教於是乎成詩人
美而禱之非固以其却敵之功也是非美惡不
嫌於同□非聖人莫能脩也信夫
禮記
父則天天則神
高則益
punctuated:
于厥而忘其義，雖以上公之俘而甘心受命，不恥焉。吾聞「荆舒是懲」，周公所以示子若孫者也。魯，周公之胄也，顧不能歟？噫！公孫夏獻陳捷于晉，莊伯猶責以侵小之故，况辱及伯主乎？吾見楚之彊日益横，而魯之勢日益卑矣，其何以宗諸侯哉？故《春秋》不言宋捷，若不出於宋焉，諱之者所以貶之也。吁！罪桓，則人知武功之不足尚，而徼功於外者知所戒矣；責魯，則人知夷狄之不可縱，而甘心從夷者知所懲矣。兹聖人經世之慮乎？雖然，戎捷不可獻也，而陘亭之次何以美之？楚不能懲，僖固有歉矣，而在泮獻馘，詩人胡以頌之也？蓋陘亭之次，桓公所以成九合之功；僖公，魯之賢君也，建學興教，於是乎成。詩人美而禱之，非固以其却敵之功也。是非美惡，不嫌於同□，非聖人莫能脩也。信夫！

《禮記》
父則天，天則神。
高則益
translation_en:
…overawed by its power [?], he forgot his duty. Even when offered captives taken from a duke of the highest rank, he willingly accepted the command and felt no shame. I have heard the words, “Punish Jing and Shu”: this was the instruction the Duke of Zhou left to his sons and grandsons. The rulers of Lu were descendants of the Duke of Zhou—could they really not do this? Alas! When Gongsun Xia presented the spoils of victory over Chen to Jin, Zhuangbo still reproached him for attacking a small state [?]. How much worse when the humiliation extended to the overlord of the lords! I see Chu’s strength growing ever more overbearing, while Lu’s position grows ever more abject. How could Lu serve as a leader for the other lords? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals does not say “the spoils of victory over Song,” as though they had not come from Song. Its concealment is a means of censure.

Ah! By condemning Duke Huan, it teaches people that military achievements are insufficient grounds for esteem, and warns those who seek achievements abroad. By reproaching Lu, it teaches people that the peoples beyond the civilized realm must not be indulged, and admonishes those who willingly submit to them. Is this not the Sage’s concern for ordering the world?

Nevertheless, if spoils taken from the Rong ought not to have been presented, why praise the encampment at Xingting? Duke Xi certainly fell short in failing to chastise Chu; why, then, did the poet praise the presentation of severed ears at the Pan school? The encampment at Xingting was how Duke Huan brought to completion his achievement of assembling the lords nine times. Duke Xi was a worthy ruler of Lu, and the establishment of schools and promotion of instruction reached fulfillment under him. The poet praised him and prayed for him; the praise was not, in fact, for his achievement in repelling enemies. Judgments of right and wrong, praise and blame, may without objection share the same □ [?]. None but the Sage could have compiled this work. How true!

Record of Rites
“With endurance [?], one becomes like Heaven; like Heaven, one becomes numinous.” [The transcription has 父, “father,” apparently in place of 久, “endurance.”]
Gao Zeyi

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭汪批發明大樂治心妙用詞
意足燦然五色成文當是作手宜冠本房
考試官敎諭蔡批講天神處曲盡其妙佳士也
考試官敎諭林批充腴爽朗
惟善心有常而馴致於妙樂之治心者然也蓋
天且神者人心本然之妙也惟久能致之樂之
感化也如此哉記者之意若曰樂之在人也原
其所自固本於人心之生究其爲用實妙於人
心之感君子審於是而知樂之不可以已矣何
===
則易直慈良吾心固有之善也致樂以治之則
善心復生而樂安之妙固資樂以得之矣豈惟
是哉蓋安則必能久也和順之中積者純然罔
間而私僞不得以參之實理之內蘊者渾然無
息而始終不得以貳之蓋有理與心一而恒久
不已者矣夫心有息則滯而未融難以語天也
久則存之也熟而天機自涵無俟於矜持之功
養之也粹而性真自湛不涉於形迹之累知識
泯而帝則之默順也思慮忘而中道之從容也
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭汪批：發明大樂治心妙用，詞意足，燦然五色成文，當是作手，宜冠本房。
考試官敎諭蔡批：講天神處曲盡其妙，佳士也。
考試官敎諭林批：充腴爽朗。
惟善心有常，而馴致於妙，樂之治心者然也。蓋天且神者，人心本然之妙也；惟久能致之，樂之感化也如此哉！記者之意若曰：樂之在人也，原其所自，固本於人心之生；究其爲用，實妙於人心之感。君子審於是，而知樂之不可以已矣。何則？易直慈良，吾心固有之善也。致樂以治之，則善心復生，而樂安之妙，固資樂以得之矣。豈惟是哉？蓋安則必能久也。和順之中，積者純然罔間，而私僞不得以參之；實理之內，蘊者渾然無息，而始終不得以貳之。蓋有理與心一，而恒久不已者矣。夫心有息，則滯而未融，難以語天也。久則存之也熟，而天機自涵，無俟於矜持之功；養之也粹，而性真自湛，不涉於形迹之累。知識泯，而帝則之默順也；思慮忘，而中道之從容也，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “This elucidates the wondrous efficacy of great music in governing the heart. Its language and meaning are fully developed, forming a composition as brilliant as a five-colored pattern. This must be an accomplished writer; the essay should rank first in this examination section.”
Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The discussion of Heaven and spiritual efficacy brings out every subtlety to the fullest. A fine scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Rich and full, clear and vigorous.”
Only when the goodness of the heart remains constant does it gradually attain the wondrous: such is the effect of music in governing the heart. For being like Heaven and possessing spiritual efficacy are inherent wonders of the human heart. Only through enduring constancy can one attain them. Such, indeed, is music’s power to move and transform!
The compiler of the Record seems to mean this: as regards music in human life, if we trace its origin, it is fundamentally rooted in what arises in the human heart; if we investigate its operation, its subtle efficacy lies in the heart’s responsiveness. Understanding this, the gentleman knows that music cannot be dispensed with. Why? Simplicity, uprightness, kindness, and goodness are virtues inherent in our hearts. When we bring music to its fullest realization to govern the heart, its goodness comes to life again; the wondrous state of joyful repose is indeed attained through music. Yet is this all?
Repose necessarily makes endurance possible. Amid harmony and accord, what accumulates is pure and uninterrupted, so selfishness and falsity cannot intrude. Within true principle, what is stored is integral and unceasing, so there can be no divergence between beginning and end. Thus principle and the heart become one, enduring without cessation. If the heart’s activity lapses, it becomes obstructed and fails to achieve full integration; one can hardly speak of its being like Heaven. With endurance, preserving it becomes practiced and mature, and Heaven’s workings are naturally contained within it, without any need for the effort of deliberate restraint. Nurturing it becomes pure, and the truth of one’s nature is naturally clear and deep, unburdened by outward forms and traces. Discriminating knowledge fades away, and one silently accords with the Supreme Lord’s norms; deliberation is forgotten, and one follows the middle way with ease…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
卽吾心純一之天適得乎自然之本體矣非天
而何天非有外於心也心本天也唯善心旣久
則窮吾之本而得所以爲天耳夫心有迹則物
而不化難以語神也天則理契於淵微者渾淪
無迹有非心思之所能窺機深於靜密者變化
無方有非見聞之所能及其藏也幽而莫可測
也其發也微而不可象也卽吾心神明之奥實
通乎天載之妙運矣非神而何神非有加於天
也天故神也唯善心旣久自達天之故而卽所
以爲神耳要之曰久者由安而自得之者也治
心之功樂有以開其始曰天曰神者由久而馴
至之者也治心之驗樂有以成其終觀乎此而
樂之有益於人大矣君子可以斯須去身也哉
雖然至善雖妙於人心之微而寔通乎天地之
大則樂之感乎人心者而卽所以賛乎天地也
故以吾心之天而致位育之化以吾心之神而
成參兩之功配乎天地而行乎鬼神此皆吾人
之能事而君子之責所不容已者也致樂以治
punctuated: 卽吾心純一之天，適得乎自然之本體矣，非天而何？天非有外於心也，心本天也。唯善心旣久，則窮吾之本，而得所以爲天耳。夫心有迹，則物而不化，難以語神也。天則理契於淵微者，渾淪無迹，有非心思之所能窺；機深於靜密者，變化無方，有非見聞之所能及。其藏也幽而莫可測也，其發也微而不可象也。卽吾心神明之奥，實通乎天載之妙運矣，非神而何？神非有加於天也，天故神也。唯善心旣久，自達天之故，而卽所以爲神耳。要之，曰久者，由安而自得之者也，治心之功，樂有以開其始；曰天曰神者，由久而馴至之者也，治心之驗，樂有以成其終。觀乎此，而樂之有益於人大矣，君子可以斯須去身也哉？雖然，至善雖妙於人心之微，而寔通乎天地之大，則樂之感乎人心者，而卽所以賛乎天地也。故以吾心之天而致位育之化，以吾心之神而成參兩之功，配乎天地而行乎鬼神，此皆吾人之能事，而君子之責所不容已者也。致樂以治
translation_en:
…Thus the pure and undivided Heaven within my heart attains its spontaneous, original substance. What could this be but Heaven? Heaven is not something outside the heart: the heart is originally Heaven. Only when the good heart has endured does one fully fathom one’s own foundation and grasp what makes it Heaven. If the heart retains traces, it becomes a fixed thing incapable of transformation, and one can hardly speak of spiritual efficacy. When it attains Heaven, its principle accords with the profound and subtle, whole and without traces, beyond what thought can discern; its incipient workings lie deep in stillness and secrecy, transforming without fixed pattern, beyond what sight and hearing can reach. In concealment it is hidden and unfathomable; in manifestation it is subtle and cannot be represented in an image. Thus the depths of spiritual illumination within my heart truly communicate with the wondrous operation of Heaven’s workings. What could this be but spiritual efficacy? Spiritual efficacy adds nothing to Heaven: Heaven is inherently spiritually efficacious. Only when the good heart has endured does one naturally comprehend the basis of Heaven and thereby attain what makes it spiritually efficacious.

In sum, what is called endurance is attained of itself through being at ease; music initiates the work of governing the heart. What are called Heaven and spiritual efficacy are reached gradually through endurance; music brings the results of governing the heart to completion. Viewed in this light, great indeed is the benefit music brings to people! Could the gentleman allow it to depart from his person even for an instant? Yet although the highest goodness is wondrous in the subtle recesses of the human heart, it truly communicates with the vastness of Heaven and Earth. Thus music’s power to move the human heart is precisely how it assists Heaven and Earth. Through the Heaven within my heart, I therefore bring about the transforming work whereby Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things are nurtured; through the spiritual efficacy within my heart, I accomplish the work of the three and the two. To match Heaven and Earth and act in concert with ghosts and spirits: these are all within our powers, and are responsibilities from which the gentleman cannot desist. To bring music to its fullest realization in order to govern…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
心正唯有見於心之所養而化之所從以出耳
樂之所觀不旣深乎
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國君必報之以
爵祿故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功是
以國安而君寧
何慮
同考試官敎諭汪批人君崇德報功人臣感恩
思報是謂上下交而爲泰也此作能發明之必有志立功之士
考試官敎諭蔡批君臣相與之情溢於言表
===
考試官敎諭林批閎詞健氣非穉筆可到
人臣以君之報功而益勸焉其裨於君者大矣
夫不以爵祿立功者臣之職而必以是報功者
君之心也人臣體此心而益勸焉君不由是以
寧哉記燕禮者若曰義莫大乎君臣而禮莫重
乎燕飮故君有舉旅之爵有特賜之爵皆必再
拜以受之者燕所以明臣禮也而其禮則何以
哉蓋言人臣以君爲元首也竭吾股肱之力于
以左右厥辟期底績於邦家以君爲腹心也盡
punctuated:
心，正唯有見於心之所養，而化之所從以出耳。樂之所觀，不旣深乎？
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國，君必報之以爵祿，故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功，是以國安而君寧。
何慮
同考試官敎諭汪批：人君崇德報功，人臣感恩思報，是謂上下交而爲泰也。此作能發明之，必有志立功之士。
考試官敎諭蔡批：君臣相與之情，溢於言表。
考試官敎諭林批：閎詞健氣，非穉筆可到。
人臣以君之報功而益勸焉，其裨於君者大矣。夫不以爵祿立功者，臣之職；而必以是報功者，君之心也。人臣體此心而益勸焉，君不由是以寧哉？記燕禮者若曰：義莫大乎君臣，而禮莫重乎燕飮。故君有舉旅之爵，有特賜之爵，皆必再拜以受之者，燕所以明臣禮也。而其禮則何以哉？蓋言人臣以君爲元首也，竭吾股肱之力，于以左右厥辟，期底績於邦家；以君爲腹心也，盡
translation_en:
…the mind: this is precisely because one perceives what nourishes the mind and whence transformation proceeds. Is not the insight afforded by music profound indeed?
When ministers exert all their strength and ability to render service to the state, the ruler invariably rewards them with rank and emoluments. Thus all ministers strive to exert their full strength and ability to render service; consequently, the state is secure and the ruler at peace.
He Lü
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The ruler honors virtue and rewards achievement; his ministers feel gratitude for his kindness and seek to repay it. This is what is meant by intercourse between those above and those below bringing about peace. This composition elucidates that principle: its author must be a man intent on rendering meritorious service.
Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: The mutual affection between ruler and ministers overflows beyond the words.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Grand language and vigorous spirit—beyond the reach of an immature writer.
Ministers are further encouraged by their ruler’s rewarding merit, and the benefit they bring him is great indeed. To render meritorious service without seeking rank or emoluments is the minister’s duty; invariably to reward merit with these is the ruler’s heartfelt intention. When ministers appreciate this intention and are further encouraged, does not the ruler thereby attain peace? The recorder of the banquet ritual seems to say: No relationship of duty is greater than that between ruler and minister, and no ritual more important than the ceremonial banquet. Thus, whether the ruler offers a cup in the general round of toasts or bestows a cup as a special favor, the recipient must bow twice before receiving it. The banquet thereby makes clear the ritual obligations of ministers. How, then, are these obligations to be understood? A minister regards his ruler as the head: he exerts all his strength as the arms and legs, thereby assisting his sovereign and seeking to accomplish service for the state. He regards his ruler as the belly and heart: he exhausts…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吾謀猷之能于以勵翼一人期樹勳於社稷夫
志存立功非敢望其報也而爵賞之施君所以
詔其德者自隆焉事專報主非有冀於心也而
祿食之賜君所以顯其庸者自厚焉由是爲之
臣者莫不感知遇之甚殷而益殫其宣勞之力
務使功在邦家而必重吾之報禮也慶遭逢之
不偶而益效其贊襄之能務使功在社稷而無
負君之委任也夫然則臣者國之彊榦也竭力
而盡能則勞以定國才以經國而制治無虞所
===
以爲四國之楨矣其永底於奠安也耶國者君
之藏身也立功以安國則君心以豫君命以凝
而太平有象所以爲一人之慶矣其永綏於輯
寧也耶譬之元首在上而四肢衛焉譬之腹心
在中而百體從焉信乎其寧之至矣要其所以
致是者人臣安國之功也而燕禮有以明之禮
之不可以已也如是夫抑論古之君臣有堂陛
以秩其分而必有燕賜以洽其情此上下之交
孚而德業所由隆也雖然君猶天也臣猶地也
punctuated: 吾謀猷之能，于以勵翼一人，期樹勳於社稷。夫志存立功，非敢望其報也，而爵賞之施，君所以詔其德者自隆焉；事專報主，非有冀於心也，而祿食之賜，君所以顯其庸者自厚焉。由是爲之臣者，莫不感知遇之甚殷，而益殫其宣勞之力，務使功在邦家，而必重吾之報禮也；慶遭逢之不偶，而益效其贊襄之能，務使功在社稷，而無負君之委任也。夫然，則臣者國之彊榦也，竭力而盡能，則勞以定國，才以經國，而制治無虞，所以爲四國之楨矣，其永底於奠安也耶？國者君之藏身也，立功以安國，則君心以豫，君命以凝，而太平有象，所以爲一人之慶矣，其永綏於輯寧也耶？譬之元首在上，而四肢衛焉；譬之腹心在中，而百體從焉。信乎其寧之至矣！要其所以致是者，人臣安國之功也，而燕禮有以明之。禮之不可以已也，如是夫！抑論古之君臣，有堂陛以秩其分，而必有燕賜以洽其情，此上下之交孚，而德業所由隆也。雖然，君猶天也，臣猶地也。
translation_en:
…all my capacity for counsel and planning, thereby assisting and supporting the sovereign, in the hope of establishing meritorious service to the altars of soil and grain. A minister sets his heart on achieving merit, without daring to expect recompense; yet the ruler’s bestowal of rank and rewards, by which he makes that minister’s virtue known, is naturally generous. A minister devotes his service to repaying his lord, without harboring expectations; yet the ruler’s grant of emoluments, by which he makes that minister’s achievements manifest, is naturally ample. Thus all who serve him as ministers are deeply moved by the abundance of his recognition and favor, and devote still greater strength to his service. They strive to render meritorious service to the realm, taking their own duty of ritual reciprocation with utmost seriousness. Rejoicing in their exceptional good fortune in finding such a lord, they exert still more fully their ability to assist him. They strive to render meritorious service to the altars of soil and grain and not betray the ruler’s trust.
In this way ministers are the sturdy trunk of the state. When they exert all their strength and ability, their labors stabilize the state and their talents order it; government is well regulated and free from anxiety. They thereby become the pillars of the lands in all four directions: will they not bring them to lasting security? The state is the ruler’s shelter. When ministers achieve merit in securing it, the ruler’s heart is at ease, his mandate is firmly established, and signs of great peace appear. This brings felicity to the sovereign: will it not preserve him forever in concord and tranquility? It is like the head above, guarded by the four limbs, or the vital organs within, obeyed by every part of the body. Truly, this is tranquility at its utmost! Ultimately, what brings this about is the ministers’ meritorious work in securing the state, and the ceremonial banquet serves to make this clear. Such is the indispensability of ritual!
Consider, moreover, the rulers and ministers of antiquity. The hall and its steps marked the ordered distinctions between their stations, yet there were necessarily also banquets and gifts to bring their feelings into harmony. Through these, those above and below trusted one another, and virtue and achievement flourished. Nevertheless, the ruler is like Heaven, and the minister like Earth…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
□君逸而臣勞賜必再拜不辭勞也君尊而臣
卑拜必降階不辭卑也人臣明於此而敬事之
義先勞之責凡可以尊上而逸其君者當無弗
至矣爵祿之報其在於君者何容心哉
第貳塲
論
天之所以爲天
黃文煒
同考試官教諭許批天命之精人所難言作此
題者不失之泛則失之晦獨此篇發揮瑩徹足占所養之純粹矣佳士佳士
===
同考試官教諭朱批說造化流行之妙探本窮源
活潑潑地是學究天人之蘊者高薦允宜
考試官教諭蔡批一氣渾成自然中度當是作手
考試官教諭林批理到詞瑩論之佳者
論曰善言天者不于其流行之迹而探其立命
之原則造化之妙可識矣夫造化流行於兩間
其屈伸相感往來相禪終始相生凡有迹而可
見者莫非天也而所以爲天者則不在是惟夫
punctuated:
□君逸而臣勞，賜必再拜，不辭勞也；君尊而臣卑，拜必降階，不辭卑也。人臣明於此，而敬事之義、先勞之責，凡可以尊上而逸其君者，當無弗至矣。爵祿之報，其在於君者，何容心哉？

第貳塲
論
天之所以爲天
黃文煒

同考試官教諭許批：天命之精，人所難言。作此題者，不失之泛，則失之晦。獨此篇發揮瑩徹，足占所養之純粹矣。佳士！佳士！

同考試官教諭朱批：說造化流行之妙，探本窮源，活潑潑地，是學究天人之蘊者，高薦允宜。

考試官教諭蔡批：一氣渾成，自然中度，當是作手。

考試官教諭林批：理到詞瑩，論之佳者。

論曰：善言天者，不于其流行之迹，而探其立命之原，則造化之妙可識矣。夫造化流行於兩間，其屈伸相感，往來相禪，終始相生，凡有迹而可見者，莫非天也。而所以爲天者，則不在是。惟夫
translation_en:
…[illegible character] The ruler enjoys ease while his ministers toil. On receiving a gift, they invariably bow twice, not shrinking from exertion; the ruler is exalted while his ministers are lowly. When bowing, they invariably descend the steps, not shrinking from their lowly position. Once a minister understands this, he should leave nothing undone in fulfilling his duty to serve reverently and his responsibility to take the lead in toil—doing whatever will honor his sovereign and allow him ease. As for rewards of rank and emolument, these lie with the ruler: why should the minister set his mind on them?

Second Session
Discourse
“What Makes Heaven Heaven”
Huang Wenwei

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: The subtle essence of Heaven’s mandate is difficult to express. Those who write on this topic fall into either vagueness or obscurity. This essay alone expounds it with luminous clarity, enough to reveal the purity of the author’s cultivation. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: In explaining the marvelous workings of creation’s ceaseless flow, he probes its foundation and traces it to its source, making it vividly alive. Here is someone whose learning penetrates the profundities of Heaven and humanity. A high recommendation is entirely fitting.

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: The whole is seamlessly formed in a single flow of vital energy, naturally meeting the proper measure. Surely the work of an accomplished writer.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: The reasoning reaches its mark and the language is lucid: an excellent discourse.

The discourse reads: Those who speak well of Heaven do not look to the traces of its ceaseless operation, but probe the source from which its mandate is established. Thus the marvelous workings of creation can be understood. Creation flows between Heaven and Earth: contraction and expansion respond to one another, departure and arrival alternate, and endings and beginnings give rise to one another. Whatever has perceptible traces is a manifestation of Heaven. Yet what makes Heaven Heaven does not lie in these things. It is only…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
本然之實理根柢乎造化而貫徹於流行之表
本無聲臭之可即而實不離乎屈伸往來之間
是乃所以爲立命之原而造化之妙統於是矣
故其大用顯行無往不在而變化不測之盛有
莫知其所以然而然者是則所以爲天也知天
之所以爲天則聖之所以爲聖者不亦可類見
乎夫古今之言天者多矣其説莫辯乎易伏羲
作易以乾象天文王繫之辭曰元亨利貞夫元
以始之亨以通之利以遂之貞以成之終而復
===
始如環無端是則天道之不已也而必本之乎
乾者乾即天之性情所以立乎命者也夫子有
見於此故於文言賛之曰大哉乾乎剛健中正
純粹精也剛健中正蓋直指其性情言之而純
粹精也者其天道之至妙至妙者歟自今觀之
日月之運行寒暑之推遷人物之代謝其屈伸
往來於宇宙之間者無窮也於此而無以爲之
綱維則聚爲有象者散入於無形寢微寢滅乾
坤亦幾乎息矣其何以爲天道耶噫是必有所
punctuated: 本然之實理，根柢乎造化，而貫徹於流行之表，本無聲臭之可即，而實不離乎屈伸往來之間，是乃所以爲立命之原，而造化之妙統於是矣。故其大用顯行，無往不在，而變化不測之盛，有莫知其所以然而然者，是則所以爲天也。知天之所以爲天，則聖之所以爲聖者，不亦可類見乎？夫古今之言天者多矣，其説莫辯乎《易》。伏羲作《易》，以乾象天。文王繫之辭曰：「元亨利貞。」夫元以始之，亨以通之，利以遂之，貞以成之，終而復始，如環無端，是則天道之不已也。而必本之乎乾者，乾即天之性情，所以立乎命者也。夫子有見於此，故於《文言》賛之曰：「大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。」剛健中正，蓋直指其性情言之；而純粹精也者，其天道之至妙至妙者歟！自今觀之，日月之運行，寒暑之推遷，人物之代謝，其屈伸往來於宇宙之間者無窮也。於此而無以爲之綱維，則聚爲有象者，散入於無形，寢微寢滅，乾坤亦幾乎息矣，其何以爲天道耶？噫！是必有所
translation_en:
…the inherent, true principle takes root in creation and transformation and permeates their outward workings. In itself it has neither sound nor scent by which it might be apprehended, yet in reality it never departs from the processes of contraction and expansion, coming and going. This is the source through which the heavenly mandate is established, and in it the mysteries of creation and transformation are united. Thus its great operation manifests itself everywhere, and amid the fullness of its unfathomable transformations, things occur without anyone knowing why they do so. This is what makes Heaven what it is. If we understand what makes Heaven Heaven, may we not also understand by analogy what makes a sage a sage?
Many, past and present, have spoken of Heaven, but no account elucidates it more fully than the Book of Changes. When Fu Xi composed the Changes, he used Qian to symbolize Heaven. King Wen attached to it the words: “Origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.” Origination begins things; flourishing brings them through; benefit brings them to fulfillment; constancy completes them. Ending and beginning anew, like a ring without an endpoint: this is the ceaselessness of Heaven’s Way. That it must be rooted in Qian is because Qian is Heaven’s very nature and disposition, that through which its mandate is established. The Master perceived this, and therefore praised it in the Commentary on the Words of the Text: “Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure, unalloyed, and refined.” “Firm and vigorous, central and correct” directly describes its nature and disposition. As for “pure, unalloyed, and refined,” does this not express the utmost, utmost subtlety of Heaven’s Way?
Consider it now: the movements of sun and moon, the succession of cold and heat, and the passing and replacement of people and things—their contraction and expansion, coming and going within the universe are inexhaustible. If there were nothing to hold all this together, what gathers into visible form would disperse into the formless, gradually dwindling and vanishing; even Qian and Kun—Heaven and Earth—would nearly cease. How could this constitute Heaven’s Way? Ah! There must surely be something that …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
以為之立命者矣吾嘗求之於未有物之先一
理渾然機緘莫測而千變萬化咸於是乎包括
所謂大哉乾元萬物資始為日月之樞四時之
柄人物之命者此也及夫氣機流行分散布濩
而本然之妙未始有一物之或遺是謂乾道變
化各正性命而凡成形成象舉燦然其各足蓋
二曜異行四時異氣人與物異性而皆不能外
乎陰陽陰陽異位動靜異時而皆不能外乎太
極太極者渾然之實理夫子所謂純粹以精所
===
以立天之命者也惟其有是實理故能有是實
氣是故日月之運行寒暑之推遷人物之代謝
莫非是實理以為之綱維實則無長無妄故不
息而屈伸相感往來相禪終始相生固其機之
所不容已耳使無是實理則天亦一物耳未有
物久而不敝者天且不能以自成又何有於日
月寒暑耶是可見分而言之則為萬象之森然
合而言之無非實理之貫徹大哉誠乎其天之
所以立命者乎世之言天者不求其立命之原
punctuated: 以為之立命者矣。吾嘗求之於未有物之先，一理渾然，機緘莫測，而千變萬化咸於是乎包括。所謂「大哉乾元，萬物資始」，為日月之樞、四時之柄、人物之命者，此也。及夫氣機流行，分散布濩，而本然之妙未始有一物之或遺，是謂「乾道變化，各正性命」，而凡成形成象，舉燦然其各足。蓋二曜異行，四時異氣，人與物異性，而皆不能外乎陰陽；陰陽異位，動靜異時，而皆不能外乎太極。太極者，渾然之實理，夫子所謂純粹以精，所以立天之命者也。惟其有是實理，故能有是實氣。是故日月之運行、寒暑之推遷、人物之代謝，莫非是實理以為之綱維。實則無長無妄，故不息，而屈伸相感，往來相禪，終始相生，固其機之所不容已耳。使無是實理，則天亦一物耳。未有物久而不敝者，天且不能以自成，又何有於日月寒暑耶？是可見，分而言之，則為萬象之森然；合而言之，無非實理之貫徹。大哉誠乎！其天之所以立命者乎！世之言天者，不求其立命之原
translation_en: …by which its mandate is established. I have sought this in the time before things existed: a single principle formed an undivided whole, its workings unfathomable, yet encompassing every transformation. This is what is meant by “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian; all things draw upon it for their beginning.” It is the pivot of sun and moon, the governing power of the four seasons, and the mandate of human beings and other things. When the workings of material force flow forth, dispersing and spreading everywhere, the subtle efficacy of this original principle leaves no thing untouched. This is what is meant by “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, and each thing attains its proper nature and mandate.” Everything that takes shape or manifests an image thus possesses its own full endowment in splendid clarity. The two luminaries follow different courses; the four seasons have different material forces; human beings and other things have different natures. Yet none can lie outside yin and yang. Yin and yang occupy different positions, and movement and stillness occur at different times; yet none can lie outside the Supreme Ultimate. The Supreme Ultimate is the real principle in its undivided wholeness—what the Master called pure, unadulterated, and refined—and is that by which Heaven’s mandate is established. Only because this real principle exists can this real material force exist. Thus the movements of sun and moon, the succession of cold and heat, and the passing and replacement of human beings and other things all have this real principle as their ordering framework. Being real, it has neither growth [?] nor falsity, and therefore never ceases. Contraction and expansion respond to one another; departure and arrival succeed one another; endings and beginnings generate one another. Its workings inherently cannot stop. If this real principle did not exist, Heaven too would be merely a thing. No thing endures long without deteriorating. If Heaven could not even sustain its own constitution, how could there be sun and moon, cold and heat? From this we can see that, considered separately, these constitute the myriad phenomena in their profusion; considered together, they are nothing other than the real principle running through all. Great indeed is sincerity! Is it not that by which Heaven establishes its mandate? Those in the world who speak of Heaven do not seek the source by which its mandate is established…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而徒泥乎法象之末有見於日月若是其運行
寒暑若是其推遷人物若是其代謝消息盈虛
舉無所忒遂以爲天之所以爲天者在是矣而
其所以運行推遷盈虛消息者莫得其故焉是
無惑乎以神化爲糟粕以萬物爲芻狗岐天人
而二之也不有聖人者盡道於其間則繼天以
立極者將誰屬耶蓋聖人定之以中正仁義而
與乾道之剛健中正者均一至誠無息之體是
故巍然而爲成功煥然而爲文章與廣大高明
===
者同其運用而合一不測之神自渾融而無間
矣故曰天道不已聖人純於天道則亦不已聖
同天不其深乎未至聖人者其必戒懼於不睹
不聞以致其中愼獨於莫見莫顯以致其和則
靜焉誠之復也動焉誠之通也大本立而達道
行盛德大業一以貫之聖人天道之極致由此
可以馴入矣否則徒以徇生執有之見而妄擬
乎天道之精微則離道益遠而與天不相肖矣
此固子思子之所深憂是書之所由以作也謹
punctuated: 而徒泥乎法象之末，有見於日月若是其運行，寒暑若是其推遷，人物若是其代謝，消息盈虛，舉無所忒，遂以爲天之所以爲天者在是矣。而其所以運行推遷、盈虛消息者，莫得其故焉。是無惑乎以神化爲糟粕，以萬物爲芻狗，岐天人而二之也。不有聖人者盡道於其間，則繼天以立極者將誰屬耶？蓋聖人定之以中正仁義，而與乾道之剛健中正者，均一至誠無息之體。是故巍然而爲成功，煥然而爲文章，與廣大高明者同其運用，而合一不測之神，自渾融而無間矣。故曰：「天道不已。」聖人純於天道，則亦不已。聖同天，不其深乎？未至聖人者，其必戒懼於不睹不聞，以致其中；愼獨於莫見莫顯，以致其和。則靜焉，誠之復也；動焉，誠之通也。大本立而達道行，盛德大業一以貫之，聖人天道之極致，由此可以馴入矣。否則徒以徇生執有之見，而妄擬乎天道之精微，則離道益遠，而與天不相肖矣。此固子思子之所深憂，是書之所由以作也。謹
translation_en:
…but merely cling to the superficial details of its patterns and manifestations. They observe how the sun and moon move, how cold and heat succeed one another, and how people and other beings pass away and are replaced; waning and waxing, fullness and emptiness all proceed without deviation. They therefore suppose that these are what make Heaven Heaven. Yet they cannot discover the reason behind these movements and successions, this fullness and emptiness, this waning and waxing. It is thus no wonder that they treat numinous transformation as dregs, regard the myriad things as straw dogs, and divide Heaven and humanity into two separate realms. If there were no sage to realize the Way fully within this realm, to whom would the task of carrying on Heaven’s work and establishing the ultimate standard belong?

The sage establishes this standard through centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness, sharing with the strength, vigor, centrality, and correctness of the Way of Qian—the Creative—the same substance of utmost sincerity that never ceases. Thus his accomplishments are lofty and his cultural achievements radiant. He shares in the workings of Heaven’s breadth, greatness, height, and brightness, and unites with its unfathomable numinous power, naturally merging into an undivided whole. Hence it is said: “The Way of Heaven never ceases.” The sage is wholly attuned to the Way of Heaven and therefore likewise never ceases. How profound is this unity of the sage with Heaven!

Those who have not yet attained sagehood must remain vigilant and apprehensive concerning what they neither see nor hear, so as to bring their equilibrium to its fullest realization; they must be watchful over themselves when alone, where nothing is more visible or manifest than what is hidden, so as to bring their harmony to its fullest realization. In stillness, sincerity returns to its source; in activity, sincerity flows forth. The great foundation is established and the universally prevailing Way is put into practice; flourishing virtue and great achievements are linked by a single thread. Through this, one may gradually enter the ultimate attainment of the sage and the Way of Heaven. Otherwise, if one merely adheres to views that pursue life and cling to existence, and presumptuously conjectures about the subtle profundities of Heaven’s Way, one will depart ever farther from the Way and cease to resemble Heaven. This was precisely Master Zisi’s profound concern, and the reason this book was written. Respectfully…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
論
同前
魯如衢
同考試官教諭汪批〔識全體乎無极皆本神之實〕
〔發明造化流行妙用闔闢繼動如環無端與易大傳擅場文也錄之以式〕
同考試官教諭金批〔圓融周匝自是說理之文〕
〔可取〕
考試官教諭蔡批〔是窮本知化之論〕
考試官教諭林批〔義深詞暢斐然成章〕
===
論曰天之所以成位於上者必有神焉以運之
善言天者不于其成位之大而于其一理默運
之神則天之爲天可以窮其原矣何者天之所
以成位者其迹也以迹論天徒得其穹窿廣大
之體而說天之不詳天之所以爲天不與存也
天之爲言理也凝然主宰之不易者太極之精
也萬化之樞紐也冲然混闢於無窮者太極之
分也實理之推行也實理即誠也誠即神也以
定一元之極而樞紐立焉以妙不已之化而推
punctuated:
論。
同前。
魯如衢。
同考試官教諭汪批〔識全體乎無极，皆本神之實。〕〔發明造化流行妙用，闔闢繼動，如環無端，與易大傳擅場文也。錄之以式。〕
同考試官教諭金批〔圓融周匝，自是說理之文。〕〔可取。〕
考試官教諭蔡批〔是窮本知化之論。〕
考試官教諭林批〔義深詞暢，斐然成章。〕
論曰：天之所以成位於上者，必有神焉以運之。善言天者，不于其成位之大，而于其一理默運之神，則天之爲天，可以窮其原矣。何者？天之所以成位者，其迹也。以迹論天，徒得其穹窿廣大之體，而說天之不詳，天之所以爲天不與存也。天之爲言，理也。凝然主宰之不易者，太極之精也，萬化之樞紐也；冲然混闢於無窮者，太極之分也，實理之推行也。實理即誠也，誠即神也。以定一元之極，而樞紐立焉；以妙不已之化，而推
translation_en:
…discourse.
On the same topic as above.
By Lu Ruqu (魯如衢).
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔It apprehends the whole in the Limitless; all is grounded in the reality of spiritual efficacy [?].〕〔It elucidates the wondrous workings of the ongoing transformations of creation: closing and opening, succession and movement [?], like a ring without an end. This is an outstanding composition alongside the Great Commentary on the Book of Changes. It is recorded here to serve as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Jin, Instructor, comments: 〔Fully integrated and comprehensive, this is indeed a composition that expounds principle.〕〔Worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: 〔This is a discourse that fathoms the root and understands transformation.〕
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Its meaning is profound and its language fluent; it forms an accomplished literary composition.〕
The discourse says: For Heaven to occupy its position above, there must be spiritual efficacy that sets it in motion. Those who speak well of Heaven attend not to the grandeur of its established position, but to the spiritual efficacy through which its single principle operates silently. Thus they can fathom the source of what makes Heaven Heaven. Why is this? Heaven’s occupying its position is its manifest trace. To discuss Heaven in terms of its traces is merely to apprehend its vast, overarching form. Such an account of Heaven is incomplete: what makes Heaven Heaven is absent from it. What is meant by Heaven is principle. That which remains steadfast and unchanging in its governance is the essence of the Supreme Ultimate, the pivot of all transformations. That which, empty and undifferentiated, opens forth without limit [?] is the differentiation of the Supreme Ultimate, the unfolding of real principle. Real principle is sincerity, and sincerity is spiritual efficacy. Through establishing the ultimate standard of the primal unity, the pivot is set in place; through making ceaseless transformation wondrous, the unfolding…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
行出焉一一此天也一日此不已之實理在也
萬古此天也萬古此不已之實理在也天以不
已而成天行之健吾於不已而窮天命之奧說
天莫辨于此矣嘗讀詩曰上天之載無聲無臭
夫聲臭且無烏有所謂命哉命不可得而見又
何以謂之誠耶易不云乎天命流行物與无妄
无妄者實理也蓋由天之賦予於物也有命之
名由物各得乎无妄之理也有誠之名然則誠
也者其命之原乎命也者其物之所資以生者
===
乎人惟以己私與之始與天不相似矣惟聖人
也清明在躬而一物無所雜一私無所容故能
與天合德純乎其不息者一天之運也煥乎其
被之功業者一天之化也巍乎其爲博厚高明
而悠久者一天之運而不積也觀聖人而天道
從可知已觀天道而聖人益可知已今夫天以
輕清之氣而成其象指成象以言天足以盡其
覆冒之體矣而非所以語貞觀之常也天以廣
運之德而大其生指大生以言天足以盡其功
punctuated:
行出焉。一一此天也，一日此不已之實理在也；萬古此天也，萬古此不已之實理在也。天以不已而成天行之健，吾於不已而窮天命之奧，說天莫辨于此矣。嘗讀詩曰：「上天之載，無聲無臭。」夫聲臭且無，烏有所謂命哉？命不可得而見，又何以謂之誠耶？易不云乎：「天命流行，物與无妄。」无妄者，實理也。蓋由天之賦予於物也，有命之名；由物各得乎无妄之理也，有誠之名。然則誠也者，其命之原乎？命也者，其物之所資以生者乎？
人惟以己私與之，始與天不相似矣。惟聖人也，清明在躬，而一物無所雜，一私無所容，故能與天合德。純乎其不息者，一天之運也；煥乎其被之功業者，一天之化也；巍乎其爲博厚高明而悠久者，一天之運而不積也。觀聖人而天道從可知已，觀天道而聖人益可知已。
今夫天以輕清之氣而成其象，指成象以言天，足以盡其覆冒之體矣，而非所以語貞觀之常也。天以廣運之德而大其生，指大生以言天，足以盡其功
translation_en:
…its operation emerges. In each instance [?], it is this same Heaven; for a single day, this unceasing, real principle is present. Throughout all ages, it is this same Heaven; throughout all ages, this unceasing, real principle is present. Through never ceasing, Heaven achieves the vigor of its movement; through this ceaselessness, I fathom the mysteries of Heaven’s mandate. No explanation of Heaven is more discerning than this. I once read in the Book of Poetry: “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” If there is not even sound or smell, where is this so-called mandate? If the mandate cannot be seen, how can it be called sincerity? Does not the Book of Changes say: “Heaven’s mandate flows forth, and things are endowed with freedom from falsity”? Freedom from falsity is real principle. Because Heaven bestows it upon things, it bears the name “mandate”; because things each receive the principle free from falsity, it bears the name “sincerity.” Is sincerity, then, the source of the mandate? And is the mandate that upon which things depend for their birth?
Only when people introduce their own selfishness into this do they begin to differ from Heaven. The sage alone embodies clarity and illumination, admitting neither the admixture of a single thing nor the intrusion of a single selfish thought, and thus can unite his virtue with Heaven’s. His pure ceaselessness is wholly Heaven’s operation; the brilliance manifested in his achievements is wholly Heaven’s transforming activity; his towering breadth and depth, loftiness and illumination, and enduring constancy are wholly Heaven’s operation without accumulation [?]. By observing the sage, one can consequently understand the Way of Heaven; by observing the Way of Heaven, one can understand the sage still better.
Now Heaven forms its visible appearance from light, clear vital energy. To speak of Heaven by pointing to this formed appearance suffices to describe fully its substance as that which covers all things, but does not explain the constancy of its steadfast manifestation. Through its virtue of expansive operation, Heaven makes its generation of life vast. To speak of Heaven by pointing to this vast generation suffices to describe fully its efficacy …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
用之盛矣而非所以語貞一之運也貞一理之
運而確然不貳粹然不雜者天之精也卽天之
所以存之而神達之而化也蘊之於寂而天命
本然之眞涵焉機之流而不息者所以藏諸用
也順之於動而陰陽互根之義行焉機之合同
而化者所以顯諸仁也用之藏者天也非天之
自握其樞也一實理之斂於無也仁之顯者天
也非天之自洩其秘也一實理之彰於有也有
無合一顯微無間以通晝夜之道而一闔一闢
===
與時消息以貫古今之運而往屈來伸相生不
窮所以生生不窮者化也一天之神主之也知
神則知天矣是故神之發而爲昭明之象則日
月星辰皆其所斡旋所以麗乎天而經緯之有
章者神也莫非實理之不已爲之也誠也神之
衍而爲順布之序則弦晦寒燠皆其所節宣所
以循乎天而錯行不紊者神也莫非實理之不
已爲之也誠也神之達而爲動撓潤說之仁則
雨露風霆皆其所敷施所以承乎天而昭布之
punctuated:
用之盛矣，而非所以語貞一之運也。貞一理之運，而確然不貳、粹然不雜者，天之精也，卽天之所以存之而神、達之而化也。蘊之於寂，而天命本然之眞涵焉，機之流而不息者，所以藏諸用也；順之於動，而陰陽互根之義行焉，機之合同而化者，所以顯諸仁也。用之藏者，天也，非天之自握其樞也，一實理之斂於無也；仁之顯者，天也，非天之自洩其秘也，一實理之彰於有也。有無合一，顯微無間，以通晝夜之道，而一闔一闢，與時消息，以貫古今之運，而往屈來伸，相生不窮。所以生生不窮者，化也，一天之神主之也。知神則知天矣。
是故神之發而爲昭明之象，則日月星辰皆其所斡旋，所以麗乎天而經緯之有章者，神也，莫非實理之不已爲之也，誠也。神之衍而爲順布之序，則弦晦寒燠皆其所節宣，所以循乎天而錯行不紊者，神也，莫非實理之不已爲之也，誠也。神之達而爲動撓潤說之仁，則雨露風霆皆其所敷施，所以承乎天而昭布之
translation_en:
…the fullness of its functioning, yet this does not explain its steadfast and unitary operation. The operation of this steadfast, unitary principle, unfailingly without duality and purely without admixture, is Heaven’s essence. It is precisely that by which Heaven preserves it as spiritual efficacy and brings it forth as transformation. Stored in stillness, it contains the original truth of Heaven’s mandate; the ceaseless flow of its incipient activity is how it is concealed in functioning. Following its course in movement, it puts into effect the principle that yin and yang are rooted in one another; the convergence and transformation of its incipient activity is how it becomes manifest in benevolence. What is concealed in functioning is Heaven—not because Heaven itself grasps its pivot, but because the one real principle contracts into nonbeing. What becomes manifest in benevolence is Heaven—not because Heaven itself divulges its secret, but because the one real principle appears in being. Being and nonbeing form a unity; the manifest and the subtle admit no separation. Thus the Way of day and night is carried through, with alternate closing and opening, waning and waxing with the seasons; thus the operation extending through past and present is sustained, with what departs contracting and what comes extending, each generating the other without end. What makes this endless generation possible is transformation, presided over by the spiritual efficacy of the one Heaven. To understand spiritual efficacy is therefore to understand Heaven.
Thus, when spiritual efficacy issues forth as luminous images, the sun, moon, and stars are all moved by it. That by which they are attached to Heaven and form an ordered pattern in its warp and weft is spiritual efficacy. All this is brought about by the unceasing activity of real principle: it is sincerity. When spiritual efficacy extends into an orderly sequence, the quarter moons and the moon’s dark phase, cold and warmth, are all regulated and distributed by it. That by which they follow Heaven and proceed in interwoven courses without disorder is spiritual efficacy. All this is brought about by the unceasing activity of real principle: it is sincerity. When spiritual efficacy reaches outward as the benevolence that sets things in motion, stirs, moistens, and gladdens them, rain, dew, wind, and thunder are all dispensed by it. That by which they accord with Heaven and spread it manifestly…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
不可測者神也莫非實理之不已爲之也誠也
神之廓而爲王始成終之化則形色象貌皆其
所發育所以本乎天而潔齊之不可遏者神也
莫非實理之不已爲之也誠也何也理之貞一
而不雜者天之主宰無極之眞也萬象之森列
無盡萬物之雜揉不齊者天之運用有漸之化
也化以達之理以基之其機淵然以深其體渾
然以穆其流行之妙則盈虛如彼而卒莫消長
推之千萬世之上其旣往者猶夫其將來天之
===
所以爲天者一也固理也引之千萬世之後其
將來者猶夫其旣往天之所以爲天者一也亦
理也理不變而天亦不變理貞一而有常天則
貞觀而不遷由之三光順軌四氣以和雨暘時
若品彙咸亨在大之化不言而成者此也吁化
以達天之神神以立天之命即維天於穆不已
之命而天之所以爲天其原可知矣不然指輕
清之象以名天是緣迹而窺天之秘也指大生
之德以名天是因物而觀天之蘊也豈所以語
punctuated: 不可測者，神也。莫非實理之不已爲之也，誠也。神之廓而爲王始成終之化，則形色象貌皆其所發育，所以本乎天而潔齊之不可遏者，神也。莫非實理之不已爲之也，誠也。何也？理之貞一而不雜者，天之主宰，無極之眞也；萬象之森列無盡、萬物之雜揉不齊者，天之運用，有漸之化也。化以達之，理以基之，其機淵然以深，其體渾然以穆。其流行之妙，則盈虛如彼，而卒莫消長。推之千萬世之上，其旣往者猶夫其將來，天之所以爲天者一也，固理也；引之千萬世之後，其將來者猶夫其旣往，天之所以爲天者一也，亦理也。理不變而天亦不變，理貞一而有常，天則貞觀而不遷。由之三光順軌，四氣以和，雨暘時若，品彙咸亨。在大之化，不言而成者，此也。吁！化以達天之神，神以立天之命，即維天於穆不已之命，而天之所以爲天，其原可知矣。不然，指輕清之象以名天，是緣迹而窺天之秘也；指大生之德以名天，是因物而觀天之蘊也。豈所以語
translation_en:
…what is unfathomable is spiritual potency. All this is the work of unceasing, substantive principle: it is sincerity. When spiritual potency expands into the transformation that governs beginnings [?] and brings endings to completion, all forms, colors, images, and appearances are nurtured by it. What takes its basis in Heaven and irresistibly brings them to purity and harmonious order is spiritual potency. All this is the work of unceasing, substantive principle: it is sincerity.

Why is this so? Principle, steadfastly one and unmixed, is the governing power of Heaven, the reality of the Ultimate of Nonbeing. The myriad phenomena arrayed without end, and the myriad things mingled in their diversity, are Heaven’s functioning, its gradual transformation. Transformation gives it expression; principle provides its foundation. Its workings are profound as an abyss; its substance is an undivided, solemn whole. Such is the subtlety of its circulation that, despite all those instances of fullness and emptiness, ultimately it neither diminishes nor grows. Trace it back through countless generations: what has passed is just like what is yet to come. That by which Heaven is Heaven is one; it is assuredly principle. Extend it forward through countless generations: what is yet to come is just like what has passed. That by which Heaven is Heaven is one; it too is principle. Principle does not change, and Heaven likewise does not change. Principle is steadfastly one and constant; Heaven thus displays its constancy without alteration. Through this, the three luminaries follow their courses, the vital energies of the four seasons remain harmonious, rain and sunshine arrive in due season, and all kinds of beings flourish. This is the transformation of greatness [?], accomplished without speech.

Ah! Transformation manifests Heaven’s spiritual potency, and spiritual potency establishes Heaven’s mandate. This is precisely the mandate expressed in the words, “Heaven, how profound and unceasing!” Thus the source of that by which Heaven is Heaven can be known. Otherwise, to point to the image of the light and clear and call it Heaven is to follow its traces in order to glimpse Heaven’s mysteries. To point to its virtue of bringing forth life on a grand scale and call it Heaven is to observe Heaven’s hidden riches through things. How could this be the way to speak of …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
窮神知化之學哉雖然天一神也神非外理而
爲言也神即理之兩在不測也神一理也理非
外誠而爲言也理即誠之爲物不貳也不貳故
不息不息則天道在是矣然要之天非幽深玄
遠而別爲一道也即吾心帝降之良一而不雜
之秘也孔子之賛堯亦曰巍巍乎惟天爲大惟
堯則之及稽其事功光被四表格于上下可謂
盛矣而其所以爲之本者精一執中而已精也
者言乎其不雜也一也者言乎其不二也中與
===
誠又豈有二道哉此詩之於文王又曰於乎不
顯文王之德之純夫純亦不已同乎天矣子思
之所以賛文王者夫有所受之也蓋天惟不已
故有以普無心之化聖人惟不已故有以成無
疆之功要之皆誠之所爲也未至于誠者苟能
去其有妄之私以復于无妄而聖人天道之神
可幾矣故曰聖人之神惟天
表
擬宋以文彥博平章軍國重事謝表〔元祐〕
punctuated:
窮神知化之學哉？雖然，天一神也，神非外理而爲言也，神即理之兩在不測也。神一理也，理非外誠而爲言也，理即誠之爲物不貳也。不貳故不息，不息則天道在是矣。然要之，天非幽深玄遠而別爲一道也，即吾心帝降之良、一而不雜之秘也。孔子之賛堯亦曰：「巍巍乎！惟天爲大，惟堯則之。」及稽其事功，光被四表，格于上下，可謂盛矣。而其所以爲之本者，精一執中而已。精也者，言乎其不雜也；一也者，言乎其不二也。中與誠又豈有二道哉？此詩之於文王又曰：「於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」夫純亦不已，同乎天矣。子思之所以賛文王者，夫有所受之也。蓋天惟不已，故有以普無心之化；聖人惟不已，故有以成無疆之功。要之，皆誠之所爲也。未至于誠者，苟能去其有妄之私，以復于无妄，而聖人天道之神可幾矣。故曰：「聖人之神惟天。」

表

擬宋以文彥博平章軍國重事謝表〔元祐〕
translation_en:
…could this be the learning that fathoms the spiritual and understands transformation? Nevertheless, Heaven is one spiritual efficacy. This efficacy is not spoken of apart from principle: it is principle’s unfathomable presence in both aspects. Spiritual efficacy is one principle. Principle is not spoken of apart from sincerity: it is sincerity’s being without doubleness. Having no doubleness, it never ceases; in this ceaselessness lies the Way of Heaven. Ultimately, Heaven is not something hidden, profound, mysterious, and remote that constitutes a separate Way. It is the goodness bestowed upon our hearts by the Lord on High, the mystery of being one and unmixed.

In praising Yao, Confucius likewise said: “How majestic! Heaven alone is great, and Yao alone took it as his model.” When we examine his achievements, their radiance extended to the four quarters and reached above and below: they may indeed be called magnificent. Yet their foundation was simply refinement and oneness, and holding fast to the Mean. Refinement means being unmixed; oneness means being undivided. Could the Mean and sincerity, then, be two different Ways? Thus the Book of Odes also says of King Wen: “Oh, how illustrious was the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” Purity, too, is unceasing, and thus like Heaven. Zisi’s praise of King Wen had a teaching handed down behind it. Because Heaven never ceases, it can extend everywhere its transformation without deliberate intent; because the sage never ceases, he can accomplish works without limit. Ultimately, all this is the work of sincerity. Those who have not yet attained sincerity, if they can remove the selfishness of their falsity and return to freedom from falsity, may approach the spiritual efficacy of the sage and the Way of Heaven. Hence it is said: “The sage’s spiritual efficacy is Heaven itself.”

Memorial

A model memorial of thanks, composed as if under the Song, for Wen Yanbo’s appointment as Deliberator on Important Military and State Affairs. 〔Yuanyou reign …〕

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
元年
胡子霖
同考試官教諭張批發揮有宋君臣相與情誼
真篤可以占他日大用之具矣
同考試官教諭周批叙事詳而不泛行文贍而
有體四六之佳者
同考試官教諭許批豐蔚溫厚得感謝體
考試官教諭蔡批人主優待臣下之意宛然
在目
===
考試官教諭林批駢麗中有典則
元祐元年某月某日具官臣文彥博伏蒙
聖恩以臣平章軍國重事臣誠惶誠恐稽首頓
首上言稱
謝者伏以
台鼎崇階獨冠端揆之寄
鈞衡鉅任兼承總轄之司蓋將密贊
皇猷豈止參知
朝政
punctuated:
元年。
胡子霖。
同考試官教諭張批：發揮有宋君臣相與情誼真篤，可以占他日大用之具矣。
同考試官教諭周批：叙事詳而不泛，行文贍而有體，四六之佳者。
同考試官教諭許批：豐蔚溫厚，得感謝體。
考試官教諭蔡批：人主優待臣下之意，宛然在目。
考試官教諭林批：駢麗中有典則。
元祐元年某月某日，具官臣文彥博伏蒙聖恩，以臣平章軍國重事。臣誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首，上言稱謝者。伏以：台鼎崇階，獨冠端揆之寄；鈞衡鉅任，兼承總轄之司。蓋將密贊皇猷，豈止參知朝政？
translation_en:
…the first year.

Hu Zilin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The exposition conveys the truly deep affection between the Song ruler and his minister. From this one may discern the writer’s capacity for important service in the future.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The narration is detailed without being diffuse; the writing is ample and observes the proper form. An excellent example of four-and-six-character parallel prose.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Rich and flourishing, warm and generous: it captures the proper manner of an expression of gratitude.”

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The sovereign’s intention to treat his minister with special favor appears vividly before our eyes.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Within its elegant parallelism there are classical standards and orderly form.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the first year of Yuanyou, your servant Wen Yanbo, holding the duly specified offices, has humbly received your sagely grace appointing me Deliberator on Important Military and State Affairs. In utmost awe and trepidation, bowing my head to the ground and repeatedly kowtowing, I submit this memorial to express my thanks. I humbly reflect:

The exalted rank among the highest ministers places me uniquely foremost in the charge entrusted to the chief councilor; the weighty responsibility of balancing the affairs of state also entrusts me with comprehensive oversight. This is surely intended for close assistance in Your Majesty’s grand designs—how could it be merely participation in the administration of the court? …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗所以尊隆勳德
聖主因之優待老成自非有名震四夷之功難
以居禮絕百僚之地如臣朴直何補咨疇
歷考前聞無如
今日蕭何之在漢室徒聞劔履之榮子儀之在
唐家惟稱甲館之盛
異數無誇於先代嘉名有待於
聖朝天禧以來于今三見宰相而上未及四人
必須齒與德均乃謂名能實副冒榮逾分
===
揣已難堪聞
命自天措躬無地茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
聖由
天縱
德與性成纘
一祖
五宗之洪業大振
乾綱當
punctuated: 祖宗所以尊隆勳德，聖主因之優待老成。自非有名震四夷之功，難以居禮絕百僚之地。如臣朴直，何補咨疇？歷考前聞，無如今日。蕭何之在漢室，徒聞劔履之榮；子儀之在唐家，惟稱甲館之盛。異數無誇於先代，嘉名有待於聖朝。天禧以來，于今三見；宰相而上，未及四人。必須齒與德均，乃謂名能實副。冒榮逾分，揣已難堪；聞命自天，措躬無地。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，聖由天縱，德與性成，纘一祖五宗之洪業，大振乾綱，當
translation_en:
…This was how the imperial ancestors exalted merit and virtue; the sagely sovereign follows their example in treating experienced elders with special favor. Unless one has achieved deeds whose fame resounds among the peoples of the four quarters, it is difficult to occupy a position accorded honors surpassing those of all other officials. What contribution can someone as plain and straightforward as your servant make to deliberations and the selection of worthy men? Surveying all that has been recorded of the past, I find nothing comparable to today. Of Xiao He in the Han court, we hear only of the honor of entering court wearing his sword and shoes; of Guo Ziyi in the Tang, only the splendor of his magnificent residence is celebrated. Earlier dynasties could boast no such extraordinary distinction; this fine title awaited our sagely dynasty. Since the Tianxi reign period, it has appeared only three times down to the present; fewer than four men have held this rank above that of chief councilor. Only when age and virtue are commensurate can the title be said to accord with the reality. Having presumptuously accepted an honor beyond my station, I judge myself [?] unable to bear it. Hearing this command from Heaven, I find nowhere to place myself.

This is surely because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇: text unclear], whose sagacity is Heaven-endowed and whose virtue developed together with your innate nature. You have carried forward the vast imperial enterprise of the one founding ancestor and five ancestral emperors, greatly invigorating the sovereign’s governing authority, at a time when…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
重熙累洽之
昌期丕隆治化
恩先黎庶
賜賑艱食之民禮被儒臣
詔舉館閣之士修通鑑之編
留神載籍重說書之職加意
典章肆人心之和豫致
帝貺之庥祥五色卿雲丕顯文明之象並穗嘉
穀於昭豐穰之年真大有為之
===
君不世出之
主也臣彥博一介章縫
三朝仕版汾陽夜雨少蒙史炤之知翼邑花封
漸起潘安之譽自蘭臺而荐登政府積以
歲年由館閣而濫與樞階深蒙
恩造薦賢為國矢心慕山濤之忠儲粟備邊雅
意嗣先臣之緒北使過褒敢當異人之號
西羌何識誤承名馬之頒實非有威望可
震懾外夷皆由仗
punctuated:
重熙累洽之昌期，丕隆治化。恩先黎庶，賜賑艱食之民；禮被儒臣，詔舉館閣之士。修通鑑之編，留神載籍；重說書之職，加意典章。肆人心之和豫，致帝貺之庥祥。五色卿雲，丕顯文明之象；並穗嘉穀，於昭豐穰之年。真大有為之君、不世出之主也！
臣彥博，一介章縫，三朝仕版。汾陽夜雨，少蒙史炤之知；翼邑花封，漸起潘安之譽。自蘭臺而荐登政府，積以歲年；由館閣而濫與樞階，深蒙恩造。薦賢為國，矢心慕山濤之忠；儲粟備邊，雅意嗣先臣之緒。北使過褒，敢當異人之號？西羌何識，誤承名馬之頒。實非有威望可震懾外夷，皆由仗
translation_en:
…in this flourishing age of successive splendor and enduring peace, you have greatly advanced orderly government and moral transformation. Your grace reaches the common people first, granting relief to those suffering from food shortages; your courtesy extends to Confucian officials, commanding the recommendation of scholars from the imperial libraries and literary institutions. You commissioned the compilation of the Comprehensive Mirror and devoted your attention to historical writings; you esteemed the office of Expositor and gave particular attention to institutions and precedents. Thus the people's hearts are harmonious and joyful, bringing auspicious blessings bestowed by Heaven. Five-colored auspicious clouds grandly manifest the signs of civilized rule; excellent grain bearing paired ears brilliantly proclaims a year of abundant harvests. Truly, you are a ruler of great accomplishment, a sovereign rarely seen in any age!
Your servant Yanbo, a mere scholar in Confucian attire, has served on the official rolls through three reigns. Amid the night rain at Fenyang, I received Shi Zhao's recognition while still young; in the flower-filled county of Yi [?], I gradually acquired a reputation like Pan An's. From the Censorate I rose successively to the chief offices of government over many years; from the imperial libraries and literary institutions I was undeservedly admitted to the ranks of the Bureau of Military Affairs, deeply benefiting from your nurturing grace. In recommending worthy men for the state, I pledged myself to emulate Shan Tao's loyalty; in storing grain to defend the frontier, I have long aspired to carry on the work of my late father, your servant. The northern envoy praised me excessively: how could I presume to accept the designation of an extraordinary man? What could the Western Qiang know of me? I undeservedly received the bestowal of a famous horse. In truth, I possess no authority or prestige capable of overawing foreign peoples; all has depended upon relying on…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
神武以布昭中夏方求遂退歸之願結社洛陽
豈期荷
寵命之臨復登樞府六日一趨
丹陛兩月一赴
經筵念臣筋力之衰不欲煩以細務亮臣經
歷之久或可效乎愚衷不分駘駑之技取
其諳道雖及桑榆之景責以後功臣敢不
思求舊之
恩勉圖報稱畢此生之力矢竭涓埃入贊
===
廟謨嘉謀嘉猷之必盡外參
廷議邊機戎政之必詳庶以仰答乎
天地之仁而俯罄乎臣子之分伏願
緝熙益懋宏
大業以迓
天庥
撫綏謐寧攘夷狄以安華夏凝承
帝眷萬年引
寶曆之長克享
punctuated: 神武以布昭中夏。方求遂退歸之願，結社洛陽，豈期荷寵命之臨，復登樞府！六日一趨丹陛，兩月一赴經筵。念臣筋力之衰，不欲煩以細務；亮臣經歷之久，或可效乎愚衷。不分駘駑之技，取其諳道；雖及桑榆之景，責以後功。臣敢不思求舊之恩，勉圖報稱，畢此生之力，矢竭涓埃！入贊廟謨，嘉謀嘉猷之必盡；外參廷議，邊機戎政之必詳。庶以仰答乎天地之仁，而俯罄乎臣子之分。伏願緝熙益懋，宏大業以迓天庥；撫綏謐寧，攘夷狄以安華夏；凝承帝眷，萬年引寶曆之長；克享
translation_en: …Your Majesty’s divine martial might, whose brilliance spreads throughout the central realm. I was just seeking to fulfill my wish to retire and return home, forming a fellowship in Luoyang. How could I have expected to receive your gracious command and once more enter the Bureau of Military Affairs! Once every six days I approach the vermilion steps of the throne, and once every two months I attend the Classics Colloquium. Mindful of my declining physical strength, you do not wish to burden me with minor duties; recognizing my long experience, you think that my humble devotion may yet be of service. You do not disdain the abilities of this worn-out nag [?], but value its familiarity with the road. Though I have reached the evening of my life, you charge me with further achievements. How could I fail to remember your graciousness in seeking out an old servant and strive to repay it fittingly, expending all the strength remaining in my life and pledging to contribute every last drop and speck! Within, assisting in plans for the dynasty, I shall offer every sound counsel and worthy proposal; without, participating in court deliberations, I shall thoroughly examine frontier strategy and military administration. Thus may I repay, looking upward, your benevolence as vast as Heaven and Earth, and fully discharge, in my humble station, the duties of a subject. I reverently pray that you will strive ever further in the cultivation of luminous virtue, enlarging your great enterprise to welcome Heaven’s blessings; that you will bring peace and tranquility, repelling the barbarians to secure the Chinese realm; that you will firmly receive the favor of the Lord on High, extending your precious imperial reign for ten thousand years; and that you may fully enjoy…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
天心億載鞏
鴻圖之永臣無任瞻
天仰
聖感激踴躍之至謹奉

聞

黃文煒
同考試官教諭金批我
二祖

聖化而有得者
同考試官教諭劉批人臣讀此作當知自勗

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇
敬天之誠超越前古此篇能揄揚之足徵忠愛之蘊可錄以式
考試官教諭蔡批善揄揚
聖德之盛
考試官教諭林批典則忠實
帝王有
敬天之盛德而后有格天之大業蘊之於心淵
微而莫測恒久而不已所以為祈
天永命之本者盛德之存也發之於政渙頒其
===
誥令敷著為
典謨所以為祈
天永命之實者大業之徵也是惟我
二祖與我
皇上為能超越前代與二帝三王媲美匹休而
豈漢唐宋之君所能及哉在詩有之維天
之命於穆不已於乎不顯文王之德之純
言盛德之存諸心也在書有之有典有則
貽厥子孫又曰皇極之敷言是彛是訓言
punctuated:
皇敬天之誠超越前古，此篇能揄揚之，足徵忠愛之蘊，可錄以式。
考試官教諭蔡批：善揄揚聖德之盛。
考試官教諭林批：典則忠實。
帝王有敬天之盛德，而后有格天之大業。蘊之於心，淵微而莫測，恒久而不已，所以為祈天永命之本者，盛德之存也。發之於政，渙頒其誥令，敷著為典謨，所以為祈天永命之實者，大業之徵也。是惟我二祖與我皇上為能超越前代，與二帝三王媲美匹休，而豈漢唐宋之君所能及哉！在詩有之：「維天之命，於穆不已。於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」言盛德之存諸心也。在書有之：「有典有則，貽厥子孫。」又曰：「皇極之敷言，是彛是訓。」言
translation_en:
…our sovereign’s sincerity in revering Heaven surpasses that of antiquity. This essay aptly celebrates it, sufficiently demonstrating the loyalty and affection within its author. It merits inclusion as a model.
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: It aptly celebrates the fullness of His Majesty’s sagely virtue.
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: Classical and well regulated, loyal and sincere.
Only when emperors and kings possess the abundant virtue of revering Heaven can they accomplish the great work of moving Heaven. Stored within the heart, this virtue is profound, subtle, and unfathomable, enduring without cessation. The presence of this abundant virtue constitutes the foundation for praying to Heaven for an everlasting mandate. Expressed in government, it takes form in proclamations and commands generously promulgated, set forth and recorded as canons and counsels. These manifestations of great achievement constitute the practical substance of praying to Heaven for an everlasting mandate. Only our Two Founding Ancestors and our reigning Emperor have been able to surpass previous ages and equal the Two Emperors and Three Kings in excellence and glory. How could the rulers of the Han, Tang, or Song have attained this!
The Book of Odes says: “Heaven’s mandate—ah, how profound and unceasing! Ah, how illustrious was the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” This speaks of abundant virtue residing in the heart. The Book of Documents says: “There are statutes and rules, bequeathed to their descendants.” It also says: “The Sovereign’s Ultimate, expounded in words, constitutes constant norms and instruction.” This speaks of …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
大業之發諸政也執事策諸生以我
太祖高皇帝
成祖文皇帝我
皇上之
敬天
敬神
恤民為問且欲敷揚
皇德之盛愚生承學顧非其人也雖然生乎
聖人之世與百姓日用而不知者等焉非愚生
===
所以自待也請詳繹其義而諦言之粤自
欽若昊天一語見之堯典而言帝王之盛
德者必歸焉然而欽天者事天之總名也
以是心而事神則為敬神以是心而勤民
則為恤民何則百神者天之靈也詩所謂
昊天曰明及爾出王昊天曰旦及爾游衍
人君動靜起居孰非
天地
祖宗所默相哉萬民者天之眾子也書所謂天
punctuated:
大業之發諸政也。執事策諸生，以我太祖高皇帝、成祖文皇帝、我皇上之敬天、敬神、恤民為問，且欲敷揚皇德之盛。愚生承學，顧非其人也。雖然，生乎聖人之世，與百姓日用而不知者等焉，非愚生所以自待也。請詳繹其義而諦言之。
粤自「欽若昊天」一語見之《堯典》，而言帝王之盛德者必歸焉。然而欽天者，事天之總名也。以是心而事神，則為敬神；以是心而勤民，則為恤民。何則？百神者，天之靈也。《詩》所謂「昊天曰明，及爾出王；昊天曰旦，及爾游衍」。人君動靜起居，孰非天地、祖宗所默相哉？萬民者，天之眾子也。《書》所謂「天
translation_en:
…the manifestation of great achievements in government. You, honored examiners, have posed a policy question to us candidates concerning how our Emperor Taizu Gao, Emperor Chengzu Wen, and our reigning Emperor revere Heaven, revere the spirits, and care for the people; you also wish to proclaim the fullness of imperial virtue. Though I, your humble student, have received instruction, I am hardly equal to this task. Nevertheless, to live in the age of a sage and remain like the common people, who use the Way daily without understanding it, is not what I expect of myself. Allow me to unfold its meaning in detail and speak of it with care.
Ever since the phrase “reverently accord with August Heaven” appeared in the Canon of Yao, those who discuss the abundant virtue of emperors and kings have invariably returned to it. Revering Heaven, however, is the general designation for serving Heaven. To serve the spirits with this same disposition is to revere the spirits; to labor for the people with this same disposition is to care for the people. Why is this so? The many spirits are the spiritual powers of Heaven. As the Book of Odes says: “August Heaven is bright, accompanying you when you go forth; August Heaven is radiant, accompanying you as you roam.” In a ruler’s activity and repose, rising and resting, when do Heaven and Earth and his ancestors fail to aid him unseen? The myriad people are all Heaven’s children. As the Book of Documents says: “Heaven …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
視自我民視天聽自我民聽
人君發號施令孰非海宇蒼生所仰戴哉是故
求之唐虞則堯舜之爲聖也在夏商周則
禹湯文武之爲烈也今觀典謨訓誥之所
載史官之所紀若曰夙夜惟寅直哉惟清
若曰至誠感神若曰宗廟社稷罔不祗肅
若曰肇稱殷禮咸秩無文又若曰欽哉欽
哉惟刑之恤哉又若曰民爲邦本本固邦
寧又若曰子惠困窮又若曰顧畏民嵒若
===
是者何莫非數聖人者事神之敬勤民之
恤要之則皆敬天實事也是以其在當時
大禮大樂五刑八政燦然明備天地相爲
昭焉治化之隆亘古莫加太和之氣洋溢
於宇宙諸福之物畢見乎嘉祥遐乎邈乎
弗可尚已自時厥后歷漢唐宋雖有英君
誼辟然其心或駁而弗純其政或龐而靡
實所以治不古若安足爲執事陳哉洪惟
我
punctuated: 視自我民視，天聽自我民聽。」人君發號施令，孰非海宇蒼生所仰戴哉？是故求之唐虞，則堯舜之爲聖也；在夏商周，則禹湯文武之爲烈也。今觀典謨訓誥之所載，史官之所紀，若曰：「夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」若曰：「至誠感神。」若曰：「宗廟社稷，罔不祗肅。」若曰：「肇稱殷禮，咸秩無文。」又若曰：「欽哉，欽哉，惟刑之恤哉！」又若曰：「民爲邦本，本固邦寧。」又若曰：「子惠困窮。」又若曰：「顧畏民嵒。」若是者，何莫非數聖人者事神之敬、勤民之恤？要之，則皆敬天實事也。是以其在當時，大禮大樂，五刑八政，燦然明備，天地相爲昭焉。治化之隆，亘古莫加；太和之氣，洋溢於宇宙；諸福之物，畢見乎嘉祥。遐乎，邈乎，弗可尚已！自時厥后，歷漢唐宋，雖有英君誼辟，然其心或駁而弗純，其政或龐而靡實，所以治不古若，安足爲執事陳哉？洪惟我
translation_en:
…sees as our people see; Heaven hears as our people hear.” When a ruler issues commands and promulgates orders, which of these is not looked up to and upheld by the common people throughout the realm? Thus, if we seek examples in the ages of Tang and Yu, we find the sagehood of Yao and Shun; in Xia, Shang, and Zhou, we find the achievements of Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Now consider what is recorded in the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents, and what the court historians have chronicled. One passage says: “Be reverent morning and night; be upright and pure.” Another says: “Utmost sincerity moves the spirits.” Another says: “At the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, none failed to be reverent and solemn.” Another says: “He first performed the grand rites, duly ordering even those not prescribed in writing.” Again: “Be reverent! Be reverent! Be solicitous in applying punishments!” Again: “The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is at peace.” Again: “Care as for your children for those in distress and poverty.” Again: “Heed and fear the people, as a perilous cliff.” Which of these does not express those sages’ reverence in serving the spirits and their solicitude in working for the people? In essence, all were concrete acts of revering Heaven.

Thus, in their day, the great rites and great music, the Five Punishments and Eight Affairs of Government were splendidly manifest and complete, and Heaven and Earth shone in mutual illumination. The flourishing of government and moral transformation was unsurpassed in all antiquity; the vital energy of supreme harmony overflowed throughout the universe; and every manifestation of blessing appeared in auspicious signs. How lofty, how far-reaching—nothing could surpass it! Thereafter, through the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, although there were outstanding sovereigns and righteous rulers, their hearts were sometimes mixed rather than pure, and their government sometimes cumbersome and lacking substance. Hence their rule did not equal that of antiquity. How could it merit recounting to you, honored examiners? We reverently reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝
聖神文武開
天立極掃除胡元之僭亂以正中夏之統
即位之初作
祖訓一書垂示
聖子
神孫其目曰
祖訓首章曰持守曰嚴祭祀曰謹出入曰慎國
政曰禮儀曰律法曰內令曰內官曰職制曰
===
兵衛曰營繕曰供用其嚴祭祀章有曰
精誠則感格怠慢則禍生故祭祀之時皆當
極其精誠不可少有怠慢是
聖祖之
敬神即虞廷惟寅惟清之旨也其慎國政章曰
凡廣耳目不必偏觀聽所以防壅蔽而通下
情也今後大小官員并百工技藝之人應有
可言之事許直至
御前奏
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝，聖神文武，開天立極，掃除胡元之僭亂，以正中夏之統。即位之初，作《祖訓》一書，垂示聖子神孫。其目曰「祖訓首章」，曰「持守」，曰「嚴祭祀」，曰「謹出入」，曰「慎國政」，曰「禮儀」，曰「律法」，曰「內令」，曰「內官」，曰「職制」，曰「兵衛」，曰「營繕」，曰「供用」。其嚴祭祀章有曰：「精誠則感格，怠慢則禍生。故祭祀之時，皆當極其精誠，不可少有怠慢。」是聖祖之敬神，即虞廷惟寅惟清之旨也。其慎國政章曰：「凡廣耳目，不必偏觀聽，所以防壅蔽而通下情也。今後大小官員并百工技藝之人，應有可言之事，許直至御前奏
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao, sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and military affairs, opened a new age and established the supreme standard. He swept away the usurpation and disorder of the non-Han Yuan dynasty, thereby restoring the rightful succession in the central realm. At the beginning of his reign, he composed a book, Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun), to hand down to his sagely sons and divine grandsons. Its chapter headings are “Opening Chapter of the Ancestral Instructions,” “Maintaining What Has Been Established,” “Showing Reverence in Sacrifices,” “Exercising Care When Going Out and Coming In,” “Exercising Caution in Affairs of State,” “Ritual and Ceremony,” “Statutes and Laws,” “Palace Ordinances,” “Palace Officials,” “The System of Offices,” “Military Guards,” “Construction and Repairs,” and “Provisions and Expenditures.”

The chapter on showing reverence in sacrifices says: “Perfect sincerity elicits a response from the spirits; negligence brings calamity. Thus, whenever sacrifices are performed, all must exert their utmost sincerity and must not be negligent in the slightest.” The reverence for the spirits shown by our sagely ancestor embodies the very purport of “being reverent and pure” at the court of Shun.

The chapter on exercising caution in affairs of state says: “In broadening what one hears and sees, one need not confine oneself to partial sources of observation and report. This is how to prevent obstruction and concealment and to learn the circumstances of those below. Henceforth, officials of every rank, together with artisans and practitioners of skilled occupations, who have matters they ought to speak of shall be permitted to come directly before the throne and report …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
聞其言當理卽付所司施行是
聖祖之恤民卽虞廷明目達聰之旨也他如
諭中書以
大祀禮成
命使齎帛祭歷代
先聖
命禮部諭天下有司謹祭祀何莫非事神之
敬
勅諭中書免浙西秋糧
===
勅諭中書罪過期賑濟
勅諭羣臣務公去私何莫非恤民之
仁是我
皇祖之所以
敬天者
精誠懇惻其叮嚀告戒之旨眞與典謨訓誥
如出一揆矣我
成祖文皇帝
英明濬哲
punctuated:
聞，其言當理，卽付所司施行。是聖祖之恤民，卽虞廷明目達聰之旨也。他如諭中書以大祀禮成，命使齎帛祭歷代先聖，命禮部諭天下有司謹祭祀，何莫非事神之敬？勅諭中書免浙西秋糧，勅諭中書罪過期賑濟，勅諭羣臣務公去私，何莫非恤民之仁？是我皇祖之所以敬天者，精誠懇惻，其叮嚀告戒之旨，眞與典謨訓誥如出一揆矣。
我成祖文皇帝，英明濬哲，
translation_en:
…reported to the throne. If their words accorded with reason, the matter was immediately referred to the responsible office for implementation. Such was the Sagely Progenitor’s concern for the people, embodying the intent of the injunction at Shun’s court to make one’s sight clear and one’s hearing far-reaching. Other examples include his informing the Central Secretariat that the rites of the great sacrifice had been completed; commanding envoys to carry silk offerings to sacrifice to the sages of past dynasties; and ordering the Ministry of Rites to instruct the responsible officials throughout the realm to conduct sacrifices with care. Were these not all expressions of reverence in serving the spirits? He issued edicts instructing the Central Secretariat to remit the autumn grain tax in western Zhejiang and to punish delays in distributing relief, and instructed his assembled ministers to devote themselves to the public good and put aside private interests. Were these not all expressions of benevolence in caring for the people? Thus did our imperial ancestor revere Heaven with utmost sincerity and heartfelt compassion. The purport of his repeated admonitions truly followed the same principles as the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents.
Our Emperor Wen, Chengzu, was brilliant and discerning, profound in wisdom…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
纘基紹緒驅匪茹之醜虜以定
燕京之鼎
卽位之初作
聖學心法一書闡揚
皇祖謨訓其綱揭而爲四曰
君道臣道父道子道其目分而爲二有統言之
者有專言之者在
君道有
祀神章首採易之萃卦終以心學之言其論
===
事神之理明矣
仁政章首採易之坤卦終以眞德秀之言其
論勤民之事詳矣至于
御製序有云
天之主宰謂之帝陰陽不測謂之神海岳川瀆
皆有攸司凡饗
帝祀
神尊
祖配
punctuated:
纘基紹緒，驅匪茹之醜虜，以定燕京之鼎。卽位之初，作《聖學心法》一書，闡揚皇祖謨訓。其綱揭而爲四，曰君道、臣道、父道、子道；其目分而爲二，有統言之者，有專言之者。在君道，有祀神章，首採《易》之萃卦，終以心學之言，其論事神之理明矣。仁政章，首採《易》之坤卦，終以眞德秀之言，其論勤民之事詳矣。
至于御製序，有云：「天之主宰謂之帝，陰陽不測謂之神，海岳川瀆皆有攸司。凡饗帝祀神，尊祖配
translation_en:
…continued the imperial foundation and inherited the dynastic succession, driving out the hostile barbarian foes [?] to establish the seat of sovereignty at Yanjing. At the beginning of his reign, he composed Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), expounding the Imperial Progenitor’s counsels and instructions. Its guiding principles were set out under four headings: the way of the ruler, the way of the minister, the way of the father, and the way of the son. Its entries were divided into two kinds: general discussions and discussions of particular matters. Under the way of the ruler is a chapter on sacrificing to spirits. It begins with selections concerning the Cui hexagram of the Book of Changes and ends with statements on the learning of the mind; its discussion of the principles of serving spirits is clear indeed. The chapter on benevolent government begins with selections concerning the Kun hexagram of the Book of Changes and ends with statements by Zhen Dexiu; its discussion of diligently caring for the people is detailed indeed.
The imperially composed preface states: “The sovereign power of Heaven is called the Lord on High; the unfathomable workings of yin and yang are called spirits. The seas, sacred peaks, rivers, and waterways each have their presiding powers. In all offerings to the Lord on High and sacrifices to spirits, in honoring the ancestors and associating them with …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
天所以報本反始也必端愨以盡其誠齋莊以
致其敬專精其德以達明薦則鬼神享之祭
必受福又何莫非事神之
敬乎又云
民者
國之根本也根本欲其安固不可使之凋敝
是故
聖王之於百姓也恒保之如赤子未食則先思
其饑也未衣則先思其寒也民情欲生也我
===
===
則有以遂之民情惡勞也我則有以逸之教
之樹藝而使之不失其時薄其稅斂而使之
必有其節如此則教化行而風俗美天下順
而民心歸又何莫非恤民之
仁是我
成祖之所以
敬天者精神懇惻其叮嚀告戒之旨又與我
皇祖如出一轍矣肆我
皇上
punctuated: 天，所以報本反始也。必端愨以盡其誠，齋莊以致其敬，專精其德以達明薦，則鬼神享之，祭必受福。」又何莫非事神之敬乎？又云：「民者，國之根本也。根本欲其安固，不可使之凋敝。是故聖王之於百姓也，恒保之如赤子。未食則先思其饑也，未衣則先思其寒也。民情欲生也，我則有以遂之；民情惡勞也，我則有以逸之。教之樹藝而使之不失其時，薄其稅斂而使之必有其節。如此則教化行而風俗美，天下順而民心歸。」又何莫非恤民之仁？是我成祖之所以敬天者，精神懇惻，其叮嚀告戒之旨，又與我皇祖如出一轍矣。肆我皇上
translation_en: …Heaven: these are the means of repaying the source and returning to the beginning. One must be upright and sincere to give full expression to one's sincerity, purified and solemn to manifest one's reverence, and single-minded in perfecting one's virtue to present luminous offerings. Then the spirits will partake of them, and sacrifice will assuredly bring blessings.” How is any of this other than reverence in serving the spirits? It also says: “The people are the foundation of the state. This foundation must be kept secure and firm; it must not be allowed to wither and decline. Thus, in their dealings with the common people, sage kings always protect them like newborn children. Before the people have eaten, they first consider their hunger; before they are clothed, they first consider their cold. The people desire to sustain their lives, and I therefore provide the means to fulfill that desire; the people dislike toil, and I therefore provide the means to give them rest. Teach them planting and cultivation, ensuring that they do not miss the proper seasons; lighten their taxes and levies, ensuring that these remain within due limits. In this way, moral instruction will prevail and customs will improve; all under Heaven will be obedient, and the people's hearts will turn in allegiance.” How is any of this other than benevolence in caring for the people? Thus, the reverence for Heaven shown by our Chengzu was imbued with earnest solicitude, and the purport of his repeated admonitions followed precisely the same course as that of our imperial ancestor. Hence our present Emperor…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
中正當乾
文明御世本堯舜之心傳法
二祖之身教以事
神言之
郊丘正分祀之典而饗
帝之禮明
明堂定配享之儀而尊
親之義著祀
先聖
===
先師於
文華東室而崇儒之
制備其見于
宸章奎翰如
欽天記頌有云
上荷
簡在答
貺無由銘心欽戴有云
上荷
punctuated: 中正當乾，文明御世，本堯舜之心傳，法二祖之身教。以事神言之，郊丘正分祀之典，而饗帝之禮明；明堂定配享之儀，而尊親之義著；祀先聖先師於文華東室，而崇儒之制備。其見于宸章奎翰，如《欽天記頌》有云：「上荷簡在，答貺無由，銘心欽戴。」有云：「上荷
translation_en: …with centrality and rectitude occupies the position of Heaven and governs the world with enlightened virtue, taking as his foundation the transmission of the Way through the minds of Yao and Shun and emulating the personal example of the two ancestral emperors. As regards service to the spirits, at the suburban altars he has rectified the regulations for separate sacrifices, thereby clarifying the rites for offering to the Supreme Lord. In the Hall of Enlightenment, he has established the rites of associated worship, thereby making manifest the principle of honoring one's parents. He sacrifices to the Former Sage and Former Teacher in the eastern chamber of Wenhua Hall, thereby completing the institutions for honoring Confucian learning. These things also appear in his imperial compositions and august calligraphy. For example, the Record and Eulogy on Revering Heaven (Qintian ji song) says: “I have received Heaven's favor in being chosen; unable to repay its gifts, I engrave them upon my heart and reverently cherish them.” It also says: “I have received from above…”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
眷殊報
德無由罔敢自娛有云
蕩蕩
昊極
元樞不息斡運四時惟
帝之力有云
曰雨曰暘亶賴
穹蒼
嘉貺眇昧家國平康有云
===
稼穡盈塍來牟亦登兆民其綏五福是徴有
云
感
恩曷已敢爾恣悛夙夜勉脩以拜
帝祉述感格之誠也又如
明堂或問折羣議以孔子之言見降
祖為親之非本秋時成物之義見
父配為正之是明周武君臣之分而準
宗祀之典別
punctuated:
眷殊，報德無由，罔敢自娛。」有云：「蕩蕩昊極，元樞不息，斡運四時，惟帝之力。」有云：「曰雨曰暘，亶賴穹蒼，嘉貺眇昧，家國平康。」有云：「稼穡盈塍，來牟亦登，兆民其綏，五福是徴。」有云：「感恩曷已，敢爾恣悛？夙夜勉脩，以拜帝祉。」述感格之誠也。
又如《明堂或問》，折羣議以孔子之言，見降祖為親之非；本秋時成物之義，見父配為正之是；明周武君臣之分而準宗祀之典，別
translation_en:
…such exceptional favor; I have no means of repaying this benevolence and dare not indulge in personal enjoyment.” Another passage reads: “Vast is highest Heaven; its primal pivot never rests. It turns and orders the four seasons: this is the power of the Lord on High alone.” Another reads: “Rain and sunshine alike depend truly upon the azure Heaven. Its gracious gifts reach one so insignificant and benighted; family and state enjoy peace and well-being.” Another reads: “Grain fills the fields to their boundaries; wheat and barley too ripen abundantly. May the myriad people enjoy tranquility: these are signs of the five blessings.” Another reads: “How could gratitude ever end? Would I dare thus indulge myself [?]? Morning and night I strive to cultivate myself, reverently receiving the blessings of the Lord on High.” These passages express the sincerity that moves and reaches the divine.
Likewise, Questions and Answers on the Hall of Light (Mingtang huowen) refutes the various opinions through the words of Confucius, showing the error of lowering an ancestor to the status of a parent. Drawing upon the principle that autumn brings things to completion, it shows the correctness of making one’s father the associated recipient of sacrifice. It clarifies the distinction between ruler and subject in the relationship of the Duke of Zhou and King Wu, thereby establishing the standard for the rites of ancestral sacrifice, and distinguishes…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖功
宗德之異以定
宗祧之法昭大順之極也我
皇上所以祗肅神祗者何如其至哉以
恤民言之如念民生衣食之艱也而躬
親農蠶于
內苑念民生疾厄之苦也而
親施藥餌于
京師慮賑濟之不時也而發
===
帑輸粟
畿甸赤子賴以全活慮盜賊之爲患也而
命官置將東南黔首賴以謐寧並見于
綸音
大誥
訓吏部以評品之眞
訓戶部以度支之策夙夜惟寅之敬以
訓典禮之臣安內攘外之忠以
訓本兵之長秋卿
punctuated: 祖功、宗德之異，以定宗祧之法，昭大順之極也。我皇上所以祗肅神祗者，何如其至哉！以恤民言之，如念民生衣食之艱也，而躬親農蠶于內苑；念民生疾厄之苦也，而親施藥餌于京師；慮賑濟之不時也，而發帑輸粟，畿甸赤子賴以全活；慮盜賊之爲患也，而命官置將，東南黔首賴以謐寧。並見于綸音大誥。訓吏部以評品之眞，訓戶部以度支之策，夙夜惟寅之敬以訓典禮之臣，安內攘外之忠以訓本兵之長。秋卿
translation_en:
…the distinction between the achievements of founding ancestors and the virtue of succeeding ancestors, thereby establishing the rules governing ancestral temples and displaying the utmost perfection of proper order. How consummate is the reverence with which Our Emperor honors the spirits of Heaven and Earth!

As for his compassion for the people: mindful of their difficulties in obtaining clothing and food, he personally undertakes agriculture and sericulture in the inner imperial gardens. Mindful of their suffering from illness and distress, he personally dispenses medicines in the capital. Concerned that relief might not arrive in time, he releases treasury funds and sends grain, enabling his beloved subjects in the metropolitan region to survive. Concerned about the harm caused by bandits, he appoints officials and installs commanders, enabling the common people of the southeast to enjoy peace. All these things are recorded in his imperial pronouncements and grand proclamations.

He instructs the Ministry of Personnel to be truthful in its assessments and rankings, and the Ministry of Revenue in plans for managing expenditure. He instructs the officials responsible for ritual to maintain reverent attentiveness day and night, and the head of military affairs to show loyalty in securing peace within and repelling threats from without. The Minister of Justice…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
訓以欽恤冬官
訓以節省無非以安民也脩建
殿堂工程浩大矣
皇上則深恤民瘼不許加派北地旱蝗饑饉荐
臻矣
皇上則深恤流離許以移粟因
覲考而用言官之議申明黜陟之條因風霾而
感
上天之警爰舉陳察之例亦無非以安民也我
===
皇上之所勤恤民隱者又何如其至哉蓋自
龍飛四十年以來兢業之懷益虔于
宵旰儆戒之念愈篤于無虞是以
誠敬流通格于上下
精意孚感達乎幽明由
輦轂之下以極海宇之遠含生之類莫不濡首
跂足以霑
麻澤呻吟疾苦之民以及含哺鼓腹之老罔不
舉手加額以戴
punctuated:
訓以欽恤，冬官訓以節省，無非以安民也。脩建殿堂，工程浩大矣，皇上則深恤民瘼，不許加派；北地旱蝗，饑饉荐臻矣，皇上則深恤流離，許以移粟。因覲考而用言官之議，申明黜陟之條；因風霾而感上天之警，爰舉陳察之例，亦無非以安民也。我皇上之所勤恤民隱者，又何如其至哉！
蓋自龍飛四十年以來，兢業之懷益虔于宵旰，儆戒之念愈篤于無虞。是以誠敬流通，格于上下；精意孚感，達乎幽明。由輦轂之下，以極海宇之遠，含生之類莫不濡首跂足，以霑麻澤；呻吟疾苦之民，以及含哺鼓腹之老，罔不舉手加額以戴
translation_en:
…is instructed to exercise reverent care and compassion in administering punishments, and the Minister of Works is instructed to practice economy—all to bring peace to the people. The construction and repair of palace halls entail immense works, yet His Majesty, deeply concerned for the people’s suffering, forbids additional levies. Drought and locusts in the north have brought repeated famine, yet His Majesty, deeply concerned for those displaced, authorizes the transfer of grain. On the occasion of the evaluations accompanying officials’ court audiences, he adopts the proposals of the censorial officials and reiterates the rules for dismissal and promotion. Moved by Heaven’s warning in winds and dust haze, he invokes the procedure of “chencha” scrutiny [?]. These measures, too, are all intended to bring peace to the people. How utterly devoted is our emperor in his diligent concern for the people’s hidden hardships!
In the forty years since his accession, his vigilant diligence has grown ever more reverent as he works before dawn and eats late; his resolve to remain watchful has grown still firmer even when no danger threatens. Thus his sincerity and reverence circulate freely, reaching above and below; his wholehearted intent inspires trust and response, penetrating both the unseen and the visible realms. From the capital to the farthest reaches of the empire, all living beings steep their heads and rise on tiptoe [?] to receive his beneficent bounty [?]. From people groaning in sickness and hardship to elders with food in their mouths and bellies full, all raise their hands to their foreheads in grateful reverence for…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
上仁和氣翔洽
明德馨香
上帝降祥
玄穹默佑是以甘露降于
玄宮嘉禾生於梁鄭白鹿陳於東越芝草發於
名山休禎疊見上瑞競呈以昭孚佑之徵
以明昌祚之應而我
皇上寔敬承之夫天人之理至微而感應之機
甚速神民之分雖隔而幽明之道不殊商
===
===
書云皇天無親惟德是輔民罔常懷懷于
有仁鬼神無常享享于克誠正謂此也愚
生生際
明聖之世目睹治化之盛涵濡德教之中與不
識不知者相忘於擊壤之外譬之頌
天地摸日月難以盡其覆載之蘊而形容其久
照之明將何以爲
聖德頌哉雖然唐韓愈有言臣者行君之令而
致之民者也宋胡寅有言臣之事君以行
punctuated:
上仁，和氣翔洽，明德馨香，上帝降祥，玄穹默佑。是以甘露降于玄宮，嘉禾生於梁鄭，白鹿陳於東越，芝草發於名山，休禎疊見，上瑞競呈，以昭孚佑之徵，以明昌祚之應，而我皇上寔敬承之。夫天人之理至微，而感應之機甚速；神民之分雖隔，而幽明之道不殊。《商書》云：「皇天無親，惟德是輔；民罔常懷，懷于有仁；鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」正謂此也。
愚生生際明聖之世，目睹治化之盛，涵濡德教之中，與不識不知者相忘於擊壤之外。譬之頌天地，摸日月，難以盡其覆載之蘊，而形容其久照之明，將何以爲聖德頌哉？雖然，唐韓愈有言：「臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。」宋胡寅有言：「臣之事君，以行
translation_en:
…the sovereign’s benevolence. Harmonious influences spread everywhere; his luminous virtue gives forth its fragrance. The Lord on High sends down auspicious signs, and lofty Heaven silently grants protection. Thus sweet dew descends upon the Mysterious Palace, auspicious grain grows in Liang and Zheng, white deer are presented from eastern Yue, and numinous mushrooms spring up on renowned mountains. Favorable portents appear repeatedly, and supreme auspicious signs vie in their manifestation, displaying evidence of Heaven’s faithful protection and responses foretelling a flourishing imperial destiny. Our August Sovereign receives these with true reverence. The principles connecting Heaven and humanity are exceedingly subtle, yet the workings of stimulus and response are exceedingly swift. Although spirits and people occupy separate realms, the Way governing the unseen and the visible is no different. The Documents of Shang states: “August Heaven shows no partiality; it supports only virtue. The people have no constant attachment; they attach themselves to those who possess benevolence. Spirits have no constant recipients of their favor; they accept offerings from those capable of sincerity.” This is precisely what those words mean.
I, a humble scholar, was born into an age of enlightened and sagely rule. I have witnessed the flourishing of its civilizing governance and been steeped in its moral instruction. Together with those who live without conscious knowledge or understanding, I lose all awareness of distinctions amid the peace evoked by the game of striking the earth. To praise this would be like praising Heaven and Earth or portraying [?] the sun and moon: it is difficult to exhaust the meaning of their sheltering and sustaining all things, or to describe the brilliance of their enduring illumination. How, then, could I compose a eulogy of the sage sovereign’s virtue?
