Nevertheless, Han Yu of the Tang said: “A minister is one who carries out his ruler’s commands and conveys them to the people.” Hu Yin of the Song said: “A minister serves his ruler by putting into practice…”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
安民之術也今
聖人在上
建極敷錫爲臣子者正宜精白一心以承
明德寅恭一念以答
君恩使四境之內神罔怨恫民無夭厲災害不
生寇盜不作以廣我
皇上如天之仁教化大行風俗醇美享祀以時
徵科不擾以昭我
皇上如神之智是在百執事有位者矣詩不云
===
乎靖共爾位好是正直神之聽之介爾景
福又云百辟卿士媚于
天子不解于位民之攸墍敢以是爲臣子勗焉
第二問
高則益
同考試官教諭周批以公明歸薦賢以養重望
賢者此必有志自樹之士真足以當高薦矣
同考試官教諭郭批論薦賢者與賢者自待處
讀之痛快足占所養
punctuated:
安民之術也。今聖人在上，建極敷錫，爲臣子者正宜精白一心以承明德，寅恭一念以答君恩，使四境之內神罔怨恫，民無夭厲，災害不生，寇盜不作，以廣我皇上如天之仁；教化大行，風俗醇美，享祀以時，徵科不擾，以昭我皇上如神之智。是在百執事有位者矣。《詩》不云乎：「靖共爾位，好是正直，神之聽之，介爾景福。」又云：「百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸墍。」敢以是爲臣子勗焉。

第二問
高則益

同考試官教諭周批：以公明歸薦賢，以養重望賢者，此必有志自樹之士，真足以當高薦矣。

同考試官教諭郭批：論薦賢者與賢者自待處，讀之痛快，足占所養。
translation_en:
…the art of bringing peace to the people. Now that the sage occupies the throne, establishing the supreme standard and bestowing blessings broadly, we who serve as his subjects should purify our hearts with single-minded devotion to uphold his luminous virtue, and maintain reverent respect in every thought to repay our sovereign’s grace. Within the realm’s four borders, let the spirits have neither resentment nor distress, and the people suffer neither premature death nor pestilence; let disasters never arise and bandits never stir. Thus may we extend our Emperor’s Heaven-like benevolence. Let moral instruction spread widely, customs become sincere and fine, sacrifices be offered at their proper times, and tax collection cause no disturbance. Thus may we manifest our Emperor’s spirit-like wisdom. This rests with all those who hold office. Does not the Book of Odes say: “Attend reverently to your office; cherish what is upright. The spirits will hear you and grant you great blessings”? It also says: “The many lords and high officers cherish the Son of Heaven. Unremitting in their offices, they give the people a place of rest.” I venture to offer these words as an exhortation to those who serve as subjects.

Second Policy Question
Gao Zeyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “He makes impartiality and discernment the responsibility of those who recommend worthy men, and expects worthy men to cultivate dignity. This must be a man resolved to establish his own character, truly deserving of a high recommendation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Guo, Instructor: “He discusses those who recommend worthy men and the standards worthy men set for themselves. Reading this is thoroughly satisfying; it amply reveals his cultivation.”

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭蔡批條答無遺議論允當
考試官教諭林批精確有見
嘗謂藎臣之薦賢譬操衡鑑然衡以權人
物之重輕而低昂乎其間微公則衡倚而
取舍之極曷以定也鑑以別人物之臧否
而是非乎其間微明則鑑鉊而美惡之品
曷以辯也雖然此自薦賢者言之然耳乃
若賢者自處若木之遇大匠然其飽雨露
歷霜雪一也其在名山大藪匠者得而用
===
之為榱桷為棟梁匠無心也木亦無心也
其在深山幽谷匠者過而不視林莽蓊蔚
而不得效堂搆之末匠無心也木亦無心
也知此則藎臣之所以薦賢與賢者之自
處各有道焉已執事發策秋闈惓惓以昔
之薦賢者為問豈以諸生中亦有圭璋特
達如昔之賢者乎愚非其人也顧執事之
問不可虛也粤稽唐虞之世百僚師師九
官濟濟相讓同寅協恭賛襄帝治斯時也
punctuated:
考試官教諭蔡批：條答無遺，議論允當。
考試官教諭林批：精確有見。
嘗謂藎臣之薦賢，譬操衡鑑然。衡以權人物之重輕，而低昂乎其間，微公則衡倚，而取舍之極曷以定也？鑑以別人物之臧否，而是非乎其間，微明則鑑鉊，而美惡之品曷以辯也？雖然，此自薦賢者言之然耳。乃若賢者自處，若木之遇大匠然。其飽雨露、歷霜雪，一也。其在名山大藪，匠者得而用之，為榱桷，為棟梁，匠無心也，木亦無心也。其在深山幽谷，匠者過而不視，林莽蓊蔚，而不得效堂搆之末，匠無心也，木亦無心也。知此，則藎臣之所以薦賢，與賢者之自處，各有道焉已。
執事發策秋闈，惓惓以昔之薦賢者為問，豈以諸生中亦有圭璋特達如昔之賢者乎？愚非其人也，顧執事之問不可虛也。粤稽唐虞之世，百僚師師，九官濟濟，相讓，同寅協恭，賛襄帝治。斯時也，
translation_en:
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The points are answered in order, with nothing omitted; the arguments are sound and appropriate.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Precise and insightful.”
I have long maintained that a loyal minister’s recommendation of worthy men resembles the use of scales and a mirror. Scales weigh the relative weight of people and things, rising and falling between them. Without impartiality, the scales tilt: how, then, can a standard for acceptance and rejection be established? A mirror distinguishes the good and bad in people and things, determining right and wrong between them. Without discernment, the mirror becomes clouded [?]: how, then, can degrees of beauty and ugliness be distinguished? Yet this holds only from the standpoint of those who recommend worthy men. As for how worthy men should conduct themselves, their situation resembles that of timber encountering a master carpenter. All timber alike drinks its fill of rain and dew and endures frost and snow. When it stands on renowned mountains or in great thickets, a carpenter finds and uses it, making rafters, ridgepoles, or beams. The carpenter has no calculating intent, and neither does the timber. When it stands in remote mountains and secluded valleys, a carpenter passes without looking; the woods and undergrowth flourish, yet the timber cannot serve even the humblest purpose in constructing a hall. The carpenter has no calculating intent, and neither does the timber. Understanding this, we see that loyal ministers have their proper way of recommending worthy men, and worthy men their proper way of conducting themselves.
You, honored examiners, have set policy questions at the autumn Provincial Examination, earnestly asking about those who recommended worthy men in former times. Can it be that you believe there are among us students men of such outstanding worth—like gui and zhang jade tablets—as the worthy men of old? I am not such a man, yet I cannot leave your question unanswered. Looking back to the age of Tang and Yu, the hundred officials learned from one another, and the holders of the nine offices, dignified and accomplished, yielded to one another. Sharing reverence and joining in respectful service, they assisted the emperors’ governance. At that time…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
有薦賢之實無薦賢之名迨至成周成王
訓迪百官乃曰舉能其官惟爾之能稱匪
其人惟爾不任而后舉賢之名始昉于此
舉即薦之義當時自三事大夫以及長伯
莫非藹藹吉人雖由鄉舉里選之法而周
召畢榮之徒延引獎進乎其間其力顧豈
少哉玆不暇多及即以明問所條而槩言
之百里奚虞之賢者也禽息薦於穆公而
擊車以諫陸機所謂禽息碎首豈要先茅
===
之田嘉其志之壯也若息者可不謂明乎
公仲連以牛畜不用稱疾不出而肅侯止
歌者之田感悟何其速也匪其心之公君
且疑之矣祁午晉之才子也晉侯問于祁
奚而舉午以對秦觀所謂薦其子不爲黨
取其心之忠也若奚者可不謂公乎薛簡
肅之在蜀而載范景仁以歸自謂得一偉
人所見何其卓也匪其知之明人且負之
矣知人三難自劉毅始發之似是矣然以
punctuated: 有薦賢之實，無薦賢之名。迨至成周，成王訓迪百官，乃曰：「舉能其官，惟爾之能；稱匪其人，惟爾不任。」而后舉賢之名始昉于此。舉即薦之義。當時自三事大夫以及長伯，莫非藹藹吉人。雖由鄉舉里選之法，而周召畢榮之徒延引獎進乎其間，其力顧豈少哉？玆不暇多及，即以明問所條而槩言之。百里奚，虞之賢者也。禽息薦於穆公，而擊車以諫。陸機所謂「禽息碎首，豈要先茅之田」，嘉其志之壯也。若息者，可不謂明乎？公仲連以牛畜不用，稱疾不出，而肅侯止歌者之田，感悟何其速也！匪其心之公，君且疑之矣。祁午，晉之才子也。晉侯問于祁奚，而舉午以對。秦觀所謂「薦其子不爲黨」，取其心之忠也。若奚者，可不謂公乎？薛簡肅之在蜀，而載范景仁以歸，自謂得一偉人，所見何其卓也！匪其知之明，人且負之矣。知人三難，自劉毅始發之，似是矣。然以
translation_en:
…there was the substance of recommending worthy men, but no name for the practice. Only with the Zhou dynasty, when King Cheng instructed the officials, did he say: “If you recommend someone capable of fulfilling his office, that is your own capability; if you commend an unsuitable man, you yourself are unfit for your charge.” It was here that the designation “advancing the worthy” first arose. “Advancing” means recommending. At that time, from the Three Dukes and grand masters down to the heads of offices, there was a multitude of good men. Although this resulted from the system of recommendation through districts and villages, men such as the Dukes of Zhou, Shao, Bi, and Rong also brought men forward and encouraged their advancement. Could their contribution have been small? There is no time here to discuss this at length; I shall instead speak in general terms about the examples listed in your discerning question.

Baili Xi was a worthy man of Yu. Qin Xi recommended him to Duke Mu and struck his head against the duke’s carriage in remonstrance. Lu Ji’s words, “Qin Xi shattered his head—could he have been seeking Xian Mao’s lands?” praise the strength of his resolve. Can someone like Qin Xi fail to be called discerning? Because Niu Xu was not employed, Gongzhong Lian pleaded illness and stayed away from court; Marquis Su then halted the grant of land to a singer. How swiftly he was moved to understanding! Had Gongzhong Lian’s intentions not been impartial, his lord would have suspected him.

Qi Wu was a talented man of Jin. When the Marquis of Jin consulted Qi Xi, he responded by recommending Wu. Qin Guan’s statement, “He recommended his son without being partisan,” commends the loyalty of his intentions. Can someone like Qi Xi fail to be called impartial? While Xue Jiansu was in Shu, he brought Fan Jingren back with him, saying that he had found an outstanding man. How exceptional his discernment was! Had his judgment not been clear, the man he chose might have failed him.

The three difficulties of judging men were first articulated by Liu Yi, and his account seems correct. Yet by…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
一言而識然明於堂下又何難焉愚以爲
有叔向之明而后可以免劉毅之論駱生
謂一言合道接然明於鄭階其殆有所感
乎用人五阻自甯戚始發之似然矣然以
邂逅而封辛甲於長子又何阻焉愚以爲
有召公之公而后可以釋甯戚之疑劉歆
謂驚駟馬而觀風慶辛甲於長子其殆有
所激乎此數子者執事所謂或以知遇而
致身於青雲若木之遇大匠者也賈誼通
===
達國體漢之才誠無如誼者吳公薦之誠
是也何長沙之行致有旱雲之賦誼洛陽
年少未免才有餘而識不足其來絳灌之
忌宜矣實誼之不能自用其才也於薦人
者何尤哉仲舒學貫天人漢之儒誠莫如
舒者公孫弘薦之誠是也何膠東之命致
有不遇之賦舒縱閉陰陽未免言則是而
術則疎以致呂步舒之誚宜矣實舒之不
能自用其學也於薦人者何過哉渭川曰
punctuated:
一言而識然明於堂下，又何難焉？愚以爲，有叔向之明，而后可以免劉毅之論。駱生謂：「一言合道，接然明於鄭階。」其殆有所感乎？用人五阻，自甯戚始發之，似然矣。然以邂逅而封辛甲於長子，又何阻焉？愚以爲，有召公之公，而后可以釋甯戚之疑。劉歆謂：「驚駟馬而觀風，慶辛甲於長子。」其殆有所激乎？此數子者，執事所謂或以知遇而致身於青雲，若木之遇大匠者也。
賈誼通達國體，漢之才誠無如誼者，吳公薦之誠是也。何長沙之行，致有旱雲之賦？誼洛陽年少，未免才有餘而識不足，其來絳灌之忌宜矣，實誼之不能自用其才也，於薦人者何尤哉？仲舒學貫天人，漢之儒誠莫如舒者，公孫弘薦之誠是也。何膠東之命，致有不遇之賦？舒縱閉陰陽，未免言則是而術則疎，以致呂步舒之誚宜矣，實舒之不能自用其學也，於薦人者何過哉？渭川曰
translation_en:
…Yet when Ran Ming was recognized beneath the hall on the strength of a single remark, what difficulty was there? In my humble opinion, only with Shu Xiang’s discernment can one escape Liu Yi’s criticism. Master Luo said, “A single remark accorded with the Way, and Ran Ming was received upon the steps in Zheng.” Was he perhaps moved by some particular experience? The five obstacles to employing men were first articulated by Ning Qi, and his account seems plausible. Yet when a chance encounter led to Xin Jia’s enfeoffment at Zhangzi, what obstacle was there? In my humble opinion, only with the Duke of Shao’s impartiality can one resolve Ning Qi’s doubts. Liu Xin said, “Startling the four-horse team and observing local customs, he bestowed favor upon Xin Jia at Zhangzi” [?]. Was he perhaps stirred by some particular grievance? These men are those whom you describe as having risen to lofty station through recognition and patronage, like timber that encounters a master craftsman.
Jia Yi thoroughly understood the principles of government. Among the talented men of the Han, truly none equaled him, and Lord Wu was certainly right to recommend him. Why, then, did his journey to Changsha give rise to the Rhapsody on Drought Clouds [?]? Jia Yi was a young man from Luoyang; inevitably, his talent exceeded his judgment. It was only to be expected that he should incur the jealousy of Jiang and Guan. In truth, Jia Yi failed to put his own talent to proper use. What blame could attach to the man who recommended him? Zhongshu’s learning encompassed Heaven and humanity. Among the Confucian scholars of the Han, truly none equaled him, and Gongsun Hong was certainly right to recommend him. Why, then, did his appointment to Jiaodong give rise to the Rhapsody on Not Meeting with Recognition? Zhongshu manipulated the opening and closing of yin and yang [?]; although his pronouncements were correct, his methods were wanting. It was only to be expected that he should incur Lü Bushu’s reproach. In truth, Zhongshu failed to put his own learning to proper use. What fault could attach to the man who recommended him? “The Wei River,” it says [?] …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
久有玉關人老之句察挺似自薦矣視嘉
遯不出如宋纖者為何如馬岌稱纖為人
中之龍斯足以見挺之不善自待也錦他
未得有明河龍門之篇之問似求進矣視
避名不起如法真者為何如郭正稱真為
百世之師斯足以見之問之不善自養也
執事所謂或以偃蹇而委身於丘壑若宋
纖法真者即木之不遇大匠者也是故薦
賢者存至公之心秉至明之識則雖擊車
===
也而不為激雖稱疾也而不為矯及其予
也而不為私一言之合不為驟邂逅之遇
不為易載之后車不為昵薦賢賢乎哉賢
人者厲介石之守樂丘園之賁則雖謫也
而不為傷雖遠也而不為戚雖久于外也
而不為勞雖莫我知也而不為躁若宋纖
之嘉遯也而不為孤高若法真之逃名也
而不為絕物賢者賢乎哉若然則遭逢其
盛而際明良之會投魚藻之歡知遇者固
punctuated: 久，有玉關人老之句，察挺似自薦矣。視嘉遯不出如宋纖者，為何如？馬岌稱纖為人中之龍，斯足以見挺之不善自待也。錦他未得，有明河龍門之篇，之問似求進矣。視避名不起如法真者，為何如？郭正稱真為百世之師，斯足以見之問之不善自養也。執事所謂或以偃蹇而委身於丘壑，若宋纖、法真者，即木之不遇大匠者也。是故薦賢者，存至公之心，秉至明之識，則雖擊車也而不為激，雖稱疾也而不為矯，及其予也而不為私，一言之合不為驟，邂逅之遇不為易，載之后車不為昵。薦賢，賢乎哉！賢人者，厲介石之守，樂丘園之賁，則雖謫也而不為傷，雖遠也而不為戚，雖久于外也而不為勞，雖莫我知也而不為躁。若宋纖之嘉遯也而不為孤高，若法真之逃名也而不為絕物。賢者，賢乎哉！若然，則遭逢其盛，而際明良之會，投魚藻之歡，知遇者固
translation_en:
…long [?], with a line about a man growing old at the Jade Gate: Cha Ting 察挺 [?] seems to have been recommending himself. How does he compare with someone like Song Xian, who withdrew honorably and would not come forth? Ma Ji called Song Xian a dragon among men; this is sufficient to show that Ting did not know how to maintain his own dignity. With “the brocade … not yet obtained” [?], and poems on the Bright River and Dragon Gate, Zhiwen seems to have been seeking advancement. How does he compare with someone like Fa Zhen, who shunned fame and would not take office? Guo Zheng called Fa Zhen a teacher for a hundred generations; this is sufficient to show that Zhiwen did not know how to cultivate himself. Those whom you describe as proudly aloof, committing themselves to life among hills and ravines—men like Song Xian and Fa Zhen—are precisely timber that has never encountered a master carpenter.
Thus, if those who recommend worthy men preserve a heart of utmost impartiality and exercise the clearest discernment, even striking a carriage need not be impetuous, and even pleading illness need not be a pretense. When their recommendations extend to their own sons [?], this need not be favoritism. Agreement upon a single utterance need not make a recommendation hasty; a chance encounter need not make it careless; carrying a man in an attendant carriage need not be undue familiarity. How worthy is such recommending of the worthy! As for worthy men themselves, if they strengthen their rock-firm resolve and delight in the adornment of a life among hills and gardens, then even demotion will not wound them, distance will not distress them, long service away from court will not weary them, and lack of recognition will not make them impatient. They may withdraw honorably like Song Xian without being haughtily aloof, or flee fame like Fa Zhen without severing relations with the world. How worthy are such worthy men! If this is so, then, encountering a flourishing age and a meeting of an enlightened ruler with worthy ministers, and sharing the joy celebrated in Fish among the Pondweed, those who receive recognition and employment assuredly …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲榮退處其閒而自甘林壑養晦衡門偃
蹇者不爲辱夫固貞於所遇耳雖然士之
不遇養素自重以待在上者之知其分也
夫何後世恬退者少競進者多雖以昌黎
之賢而不免於三上書士風之偷也如是
所以作而起之者不賴於上之人乎故獎
恬退抑奔競操人物衡鑑者不可不益辨
矣蓋臣薦賢至公至明以食賢者之報其
分也夫何賢者志隳於官之成節墮於利
===
之誘未能一一如謝玄之才不負所舉士
行之薄也如是所以砥而礪之者又不有
賴於上之人乎故稽名實慎考課操人物
衡鑑者不可不益嚴矣方今
聖人在上懋隆唐虞之治闢四門以來賢俊任
九德以亮天工登明選公已無遺賢之嘆
往者因南北多事
朝廷復
詔舉才望之臣不分廢棄咸在錄用至於才略
punctuated:
爲榮；退處其閒，而自甘林壑，養晦衡門，偃蹇者不爲辱。夫固貞於所遇耳。雖然，士之不遇，養素自重，以待在上者之知，其分也。夫何後世恬退者少，競進者多？雖以昌黎之賢，而不免於三上書。士風之偷也如是，所以作而起之者，不賴於上之人乎？故獎恬退，抑奔競，操人物衡鑑者不可不益辨矣。蓋臣薦賢，至公至明，以食賢者之報，其分也。夫何賢者志隳於官之成，節墮於利之誘，未能一一如謝玄之才，不負所舉？士行之薄也如是，所以砥而礪之者，又不有賴於上之人乎？故稽名實，慎考課，操人物衡鑑者不可不益嚴矣。
方今聖人在上，懋隆唐虞之治，闢四門以來賢俊，任九德以亮天工，登明選公，已無遺賢之嘆。往者因南北多事，朝廷復詔舉才望之臣，不分廢棄，咸在錄用。至於才略
translation_en:
…regard it as an honor; those who withdraw into retirement, content among woods and ravines, nurturing their virtue in obscurity behind humble gates, do not regard their proud seclusion as disgrace. They simply remain steadfast in whatever circumstances they encounter. Nevertheless, when a scholar finds no opportunity for service, it is his duty to cultivate his unadorned integrity and maintain his self-respect, awaiting recognition by those above. Why, then, in later ages have so few been content to withdraw, and so many competed for advancement? Even someone as worthy as Han Yu of Changli could not refrain from submitting three letters. When the ethos of scholars has become so debased, does not its revival depend upon those above? Thus, those who weigh and assess men must exercise still greater discernment, rewarding quiet retirement and restraining the scramble for advancement. It is a minister’s duty to recommend worthy men with the utmost impartiality and discernment, and thereby receive the return their service provides. Why, then, do worthy men’s aspirations crumble once they attain office, and their integrity collapse before the lure of profit, so that they cannot all match Xie Xuan’s ability and vindicate their recommendation? When scholars’ conduct has become so deficient, does not its tempering and refinement likewise depend upon those above? Thus, those who weigh and assess men must be still more exacting, checking reputation against actual performance and conducting official evaluations with care.
Now that the sage sovereign reigns above, he assiduously advances the governance of Tang and Yu, opening the four gates to attract worthy and talented men, and employing those endowed with the nine virtues to assist in Heaven’s work. He promotes the discerning and selects the impartial; already there is no cause to lament that worthy men have been overlooked. Previously, because of troubles in both north and south, the court again issued an edict calling for the recommendation of officials of talent and reputation. All were to be considered for employment, including those dismissed or set aside. As for those whose ability and strategic judgment…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
超軼者又皆不次推擢
皇上以
天地之心覆冒於上
日月之明照臨乎下百僚師師莫不推賢而進
達之斯物覩之
昌期而彙征之
泰運也士生其時者固不患乎有才而不知
知之而不舉顧所以自獻成信以亮天工
而凝庶績者何如耳若脩之於家而易節
===
於
天子之庭以賢進而不以賢遂則上負
明時下負所學者不旣多乎此愚之所不敢也
不識執事以為何如
第三問
王廷俊
同考試官敎諭古批彌盜之方不止一端要之
守令為急子能援古徵今辯博明悉蓋素有志於經國者
同考試官敎諭張批發明守令所係之重讀之
punctuated:
超軼者，又皆不次推擢。皇上以天地之心覆冒於上，日月之明照臨乎下，百僚師師，莫不推賢而進達之。斯物覩之昌期，而彙征之泰運也。士生其時者，固不患乎有才而不知，知之而不舉，顧所以自獻成信，以亮天工而凝庶績者何如耳。若脩之於家，而易節於天子之庭，以賢進而不以賢遂，則上負明時，下負所學者，不旣多乎？此愚之所不敢也。不識執事以為何如？
第三問
王廷俊
同考試官敎諭古批：彌盜之方，不止一端，要之守令為急。子能援古徵今，辯博明悉，蓋素有志於經國者。
同考試官敎諭張批：發明守令所係之重，讀之
translation_en:
…those of outstanding ability were also all promoted without regard to the normal order of advancement. His Majesty shelters all from above with the heart of Heaven and Earth, and shines upon all below with the brilliance of the sun and moon. The hundred officials emulate one another, all recommending worthy men and bringing them forward. This is a flourishing age in which all beings behold their sovereign, a time of peace and prosperity in which worthy men advance together. Scholars born into such an age surely need not fear that their talents will go unrecognized, or that, once recognized, they will not be recommended. The question is simply how they will offer their services and establish their trustworthiness, assist in Heaven’s work, and bring the many undertakings of government to fruition. If they cultivate themselves at home but abandon their principles at the Son of Heaven’s court, advancing through their worthiness but failing to sustain it thereafter, would they not gravely betray both this enlightened age above and their own learning below? This is what I, in my ignorance, dare not do. I wonder what you, sir, think of this.
Third Policy Question
Wang Tingjun
Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Instructor: There is more than one way to quell banditry; the essential and urgent matter concerns prefects and county magistrates. You draw upon antiquity and adduce evidence from the present; your argument is wide-ranging, clear, and thorough. Evidently you have long aspired to order the affairs of the state.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: You elucidate the weighty responsibilities resting upon prefects and county magistrates. Reading this …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
令人惕然
考試官教諭蔡批議論的確
考試官教諭林批邃古之文
圖安民之術者務求所以牧民者而已矣
何者民猶赤子也守令猶慈母也赤子之
愁苦痛癢必號呼慈母以保護之然後足
以安其軀民之愁苦痛癢其所以調護而
安全之非於守令之賴而誰賴哉守令之
匪人則赤子失所依矣而况又從而虐之
===
乎如之何民不窮且盜也民窮至於為盜
返指而罪之曰是非吾民也嗚呼夫民豈
有離父母舍妻子而樂於為盜者哉其必
有以致之者矣此探本之論非臆說也執
事憤閩廣之盜蔓延而入我江右迺追論
所以致盜之由而歸咎於守令嗟夫此足
以仰窺執事憂民之心矣粵稽臯陶之謨
曰在安民在知人又曰惇德允元而難壬
人蠻夷率服夫以安民而必先曰知人所
punctuated:
令人惕然。
考試官教諭蔡批：議論的確。
考試官教諭林批：邃古之文。
圖安民之術者，務求所以牧民者而已矣。何者？民猶赤子也，守令猶慈母也。赤子之愁苦痛癢，必號呼慈母以保護之，然後足以安其軀。民之愁苦痛癢，其所以調護而安全之，非於守令之賴而誰賴哉？守令之匪人，則赤子失所依矣，而况又從而虐之乎？如之何民不窮且盜也？民窮至於為盜，返指而罪之曰：「是非吾民也。」嗚呼！夫民豈有離父母、舍妻子而樂於為盜者哉？其必有以致之者矣。此探本之論，非臆說也。執事憤閩廣之盜蔓延而入我江右，迺追論所以致盜之由，而歸咎於守令。嗟夫！此足以仰窺執事憂民之心矣。粵稽臯陶之謨，曰：「在安民，在知人。」又曰：「惇德允元，而難壬人，蠻夷率服。」夫以安民而必先曰知人，所
translation_en:
… makes the reader apprehensive.
Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The argument is sound and precise.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Writing of profound antiquity.”
Those who devise means of bringing peace to the people need only seek out those fit to shepherd them. Why is this? The people are like infants, and prefects and magistrates are like loving mothers. When infants suffer distress, pain, or discomfort, they invariably cry out to their loving mothers to protect them; only then can their bodies be at ease. When the people suffer distress, pain, or discomfort, upon whom can they depend to tend them and keep them safe, if not their prefects and magistrates? If prefects and magistrates are unworthy men, these infants lose those upon whom they depend. How much worse if these officials then abuse them! How could the people fail to become destitute and turn to banditry? Yet when poverty drives the people to become bandits, the officials turn around, point at them, and condemn them, saying: “These are not my people.” Alas! Would any among the people gladly leave their parents, abandon their wives and children, and become bandits? There must be something that drives them to it. This argument probes the root of the matter; it is no conjecture.
You, sir, are indignant that banditry in Min and Guang has spread into our Jiangyou. You therefore trace the causes that give rise to banditry and lay the blame upon prefects and magistrates. Ah! This affords a respectful glimpse of your concern for the people. Now, examining the Counsels of Gao Yao, we find: “It lies in bringing peace to the people; it lies in knowing men.” It also says: “Honor the virtuous, trust the good, and keep flatterers at a distance; then the Man and Yi will all submit.” Thus, to bring peace to the people, one must first speak of knowing men. What is meant by …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
謂知人者非所謂擇人而寄之以子民之
責乎以蠻夷之率服由於惇德允元而難
壬人況其邇者乎由此則圖安民之術信
無出於擇守令之賢者矣是故董生有言
郡邑守令民之師帥夫謂之師者非教之
而復其性乎謂之帥者非治之而遂其生
乎若宣帝愼二千石之選明帝不私求郎
而寧賜錢者非以其所繫之重乎愚生楚
產也固未詳閩廣之事然其所以致盜者
===
則亦有聞矣夫閩廣海邦也地饒而民富
且多珍貨故爲長吏者日朘月削瘠民以
自封
京師遼邈雖有奸慝不及聞也爲之監司者
縱欲按舉之亦不過去其太甚者耳嗚呼
民如之何不窮且盜也夫江右文獻之地
矣而郡邑守令固多賢豪之選也而執事
猶舉昔之宦於玆土者而欲以風之夫豪
傑之士不待教而興者也雖然言及之而
punctuated:
謂知人者，非所謂擇人而寄之以子民之責乎？以蠻夷之率服，由於惇德允元而難壬人，況其邇者乎？由此則圖安民之術，信無出於擇守令之賢者矣。是故董生有言：「郡邑守令，民之師帥。」夫謂之師者，非教之而復其性乎？謂之帥者，非治之而遂其生乎？若宣帝愼二千石之選，明帝不私求郎而寧賜錢者，非以其所繫之重乎？愚生楚產也，固未詳閩廣之事，然其所以致盜者，則亦有聞矣。
夫閩廣海邦也，地饒而民富，且多珍貨，故爲長吏者日朘月削，瘠民以自封。京師遼邈，雖有奸慝，不及聞也。爲之監司者，縱欲按舉之，亦不過去其太甚者耳。嗚呼！民如之何不窮且盜也？夫江右文獻之地矣，而郡邑守令固多賢豪之選也，而執事猶舉昔之宦於玆土者而欲以風之。夫豪傑之士，不待教而興者也。雖然，言及之而
translation_en:
…what is meant by knowing men—is it not choosing men and entrusting them with the responsibility of caring for the people as their children? If the submission of the Man and Yi peoples results from honoring the virtuous, trusting the good, and keeping deceitful men at a distance, how much more must this apply to those nearby? Thus, among methods of securing the people's peace, surely none surpasses selecting worthy prefects and magistrates. Hence Master Dong said: “Prefects and magistrates are the people's teachers and leaders.” To call them teachers—is this not to say that they instruct the people and restore their original nature? To call them leaders—is this not to say that they govern the people and enable them to sustain their lives? Emperor Xuan carefully selected officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank, while Emperor Ming refused to grant a personal request for appointment as a Gentleman, preferring to bestow money instead. Was this not because so much depended upon these appointments? I, an unworthy student, am a native of Chu. Although I do not know the affairs of Min and Guang in detail, I have nevertheless heard something of what has brought about banditry there.
Min and Guang are coastal regions, with fertile land, wealthy inhabitants, and abundant precious merchandise. Consequently, their senior local officials fleece the people day after day and month after month, impoverishing them to enrich themselves. The capital is far away; even when wrongdoing occurs, word of it does not reach there. Even if the regional surveillance officials wish to investigate and impeach the offenders, they do no more than remove the worst among them. Alas! How could the people fail to become impoverished and turn to banditry? Jiangyou is a land of cultural traditions and learned men, and many of its prefects and magistrates have indeed been chosen from among the worthy and outstanding. Yet you, Sir, still cite those who formerly served in this land, wishing thereby to inspire its present officials. Men of exceptional ability rise to action without waiting for instruction. Nevertheless, having touched upon this matter, …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
不言可乎自今觀之令鄱陽而號番君非
吳芮乎下榻而禮高士則陳蕃之高致矣
令建昌而歌何父非何易于乎建陂而立
生祠則顏真卿之偉蹟也計傭而贖男女
韓愈善於賑饑矣若趙抃戒諸縣而自相
為治非弭盜之良圖乎興學賑饑范仲淹
實心愛民矣若楊萬里俸外一無所取者
非守身之大節乎至於孜孜愛民之林弼
正直廉潔之周鐸是皆良吏之選也求其
===
可為師法者其惟周濂溪朱晦菴先生乎
濂溪甞知南昌矣而富室黠吏皆恥其非
又知南康軍矣而興學善俗能成其化至
若陳北山之知贛州張南軒之知袁州則
皆庶幾於濂溪者焉朱晦菴之守南康也
興利除害講社倉之政而民無轉徙勸學
造士新鹿洞之規而士皆向方至若黃勉
齋之知臨川真西山之知隆興則皆庶幾
於晦菴者焉雖其學術有淺深事功有小
punctuated: 不言可乎？自今觀之，令鄱陽而號番君，非吳芮乎？下榻而禮高士，則陳蕃之高致矣。令建昌而歌何父，非何易于乎？建陂而立生祠，則顏真卿之偉蹟也。計傭而贖男女，韓愈善於賑饑矣。若趙抃戒諸縣而自相為治，非弭盜之良圖乎？興學賑饑，范仲淹實心愛民矣。若楊萬里俸外一無所取者，非守身之大節乎？至於孜孜愛民之林弼、正直廉潔之周鐸，是皆良吏之選也。求其可為師法者，其惟周濂溪、朱晦菴先生乎？濂溪甞知南昌矣，而富室黠吏皆恥其非；又知南康軍矣，而興學善俗，能成其化。至若陳北山之知贛州、張南軒之知袁州，則皆庶幾於濂溪者焉。朱晦菴之守南康也，興利除害，講社倉之政，而民無轉徙；勸學造士，新鹿洞之規，而士皆向方。至若黃勉齋之知臨川、真西山之知隆興，則皆庶幾於晦菴者焉。雖其學術有淺深，事功有小
translation_en:
…can one refrain from speaking of them? Looking back from the present, was it not Wu Rui who served as magistrate of Poyang and was called the Lord of Poyang? Lowering a couch to honor a lofty scholar exemplified Chen Fan’s noble bearing. Was it not He Yiyu who served as magistrate of Jianchang and was celebrated in songs as “Father He”? Building a reservoir and having a shrine erected to him while still alive marked Yan Zhenqing’s great achievements. By reckoning the wages for their labor and redeeming men and women from bondage, Han Yu showed his skill in famine relief. As for Zhao Bian’s admonishing the counties to cooperate in maintaining order, was this not an excellent plan for suppressing banditry? By promoting learning and relieving famine, Fan Zhongyan showed his heartfelt love for the people. As for Yang Wanli’s taking nothing beyond his official salary, was this not an outstanding example of preserving one’s integrity? Then there were Lin Bi, tireless in caring for the people, and Zhou Duo, upright, honest, and incorruptible: all were outstanding choices as good officials. Yet if we seek those who can serve as models to emulate, would they not be Masters Zhou Lianxi and Zhu Hui’an?

Lianxi once served as magistrate of Nanchang, where wealthy households and crafty clerks alike became ashamed of their wrongdoing. He also served as prefect of Nankang Military Prefecture, where he promoted learning and improved customs, successfully bringing about moral transformation. As for Chen Beishan’s administration of Ganzhou and Zhang Nanxuan’s administration of Yuanzhou, both approached Lianxi’s example. When Zhu Hui’an served as prefect of Nankang, he promoted beneficial measures, eliminated abuses, and gave careful attention to community granary administration, so that the people did not have to leave their homes. He encouraged learning, cultivated scholars, and renewed the regulations of White Deer Grotto Academy, so that scholars all turned toward the proper way. As for Huang Mianzhai’s administration of Linchuan and Zhen Xishan’s administration of Longxing, both approached Hui’an’s example. Although their learning varied in depth and their achievements in government were small…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
大而學道愛人豈非西江良牧之表率者
乎今
皇帝仁聖嘉惠元元海內欣欣焉見
德化之成顧所以宣布
上澤使其淪浹宇內覃被羣生者非在守令乎
邇因言官建白
特命憲臣申儆吏治簡其尤不肖者斥譴之海
內尤欣欣焉若甦生小大吏莫不惕惕焉
精白一心詢民瘼而霈
===
皇仁矣而執事猶以風厲之方下詢承學者豈
亦以人之智愚賢不肖相越也其豪傑之
士能自樹立如古循吏者固無待於振揚
惕厲矣而中材之士恒多也非多方以鼓
舞之其孰思自效耶迹今吏於茲土者豈
敢謂無豪傑之士哉一錢選受三異化行
者比比有之而號乳虎名蒼鷹者或未必
其盡無也夫守令不能以皆賢而欲民之
無愁苦嘆息難矣斯民不免於愁嘆而欲
punctuated: 大，而學道愛人，豈非西江良牧之表率者乎？今皇帝仁聖，嘉惠元元，海內欣欣焉見德化之成。顧所以宣布上澤，使其淪浹宇內、覃被羣生者，非在守令乎？邇因言官建白，特命憲臣申儆吏治，簡其尤不肖者斥譴之。海內尤欣欣焉若甦生，小大吏莫不惕惕焉，精白一心，詢民瘼而霈皇仁矣。而執事猶以風厲之方下詢承學者，豈亦以人之智愚賢不肖相越也？其豪傑之士能自樹立如古循吏者，固無待於振揚惕厲矣，而中材之士恒多也。非多方以鼓舞之，其孰思自效耶？迹今吏於茲土者，豈敢謂無豪傑之士哉？一錢選受、三異化行者，比比有之；而號乳虎、名蒼鷹者，或未必其盡無也。夫守令不能以皆賢，而欲民之無愁苦嘆息，難矣。斯民不免於愁嘆，而欲
translation_en:
…great; yet in studying the Way and loving the people, were they not exemplars of good governors in Jiangxi?

Now the Emperor, humane and sagely, bestows gracious benefits upon the common people, and all within the seas rejoice to witness the success of his moral transformation. Yet does not responsibility for spreading imperial beneficence, so that it thoroughly permeates the realm and reaches all living people, rest with prefects and magistrates? Recently, following a proposal submitted by a censorial official, the Emperor specially commanded the surveillance officials to renew their admonitions concerning local administration, selecting the most unworthy officials for dismissal and punishment. All within the seas rejoiced still more, as though restored to life. Officials high and low alike became vigilant, purifying their hearts with single-minded resolve, inquiring into the people’s sufferings, and showering imperial benevolence upon them.

Yet you, honored examiners, still condescend to ask us students how officials might be encouraged and admonished. Is this also because people differ so greatly in wisdom and folly, worthiness and unworthiness? Outstanding men who can establish themselves as the exemplary officials of antiquity did surely need no encouragement or admonition. But men of middling ability are always numerous. Unless various means are used to inspire them, who among them will think to render worthy service? Looking at those now serving as officials in this region, how could I dare say there are no outstanding men? Those associated with ‘a single coin’ in what they accept [?], and whose transforming influence brings forth ‘three wonders,’ are found everywhere. Yet it may not be the case that we are entirely free of those called ‘tigresses with young’ or known as ‘goshawks’ for their ferocity. When prefects and magistrates cannot all be worthy, it is difficult indeed to expect the people to be free from sorrow, hardship, and lamentation. While these people still suffer sorrow and lamentation, to wish that…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
盜寇屏息胡可得也風厲之方愚也草茅
有懷耿耿久矣執事復勉之曰無諱是以
敢有言焉昔人有言曰吏數變則民不安
業久於其事則民服敎化言任之當久也
故漢文之世爲吏者長子孫宣帝時守宰
卓異者輒以璽書慰勉增秩賜金不即遷
也吏稱其職民安其業有由然矣今長吏
率未三年即遷即一考亦不及矧復有再
三考者其不肖者曰是傳舍耳非無所事
===
事則亦爲一切苟且之政冀旦夕徙去其
誰加志於民哉即有賢者能加志於民然
不久於其官亦無以自見欲其厎有成績
也不亦難乎
國初內外官咸以九年通考課其功過而黜
陟之不如是驟也則久任之法顧不可行
乎漢制二千石異等者得入爲御史大夫
是故卓茂自密令召爲太傅則又罔資格
拘也夫能以非常待人則必以非常自待
punctuated:
盜寇屏息，胡可得也？風厲之方，愚也草茅，有懷耿耿久矣。執事復勉之曰：「無諱。」是以敢有言焉。昔人有言曰：「吏數變，則民不安業；久於其事，則民服敎化。」言任之當久也。故漢文之世，爲吏者長子孫；宣帝時，守宰卓異者，輒以璽書慰勉，增秩賜金，不即遷也。吏稱其職，民安其業，有由然矣。今長吏率未三年即遷，即一考亦不及，矧復有再三考者？其不肖者曰：「是傳舍耳。」非無所事事，則亦爲一切苟且之政，冀旦夕徙去，其誰加志於民哉？即有賢者能加志於民，然不久於其官，亦無以自見，欲其厎有成績也，不亦難乎？
國初，內外官咸以九年通考，課其功過而黜陟之，不如是驟也。則久任之法，顧不可行乎？漢制，二千石異等者得入爲御史大夫。是故卓茂自密令召爲太傅，則又罔資格拘也。夫能以非常待人，則必以非常自待。
translation_en:
…how could one hope to make bandits and marauders cease their activities? As for ways to exhort and spur officials onward, I, an unworthy man outside official service, have long harbored earnest concerns. You gentlemen have further encouraged me, saying, “Hold nothing back.” Thus I venture to speak. A man of old said: “When officials are frequently changed, the people cannot pursue their livelihoods in peace; when officials remain long at their duties, the people submit to their teaching and transforming influence.” This means that appointments should be lengthy. Thus, under Emperor Wen of Han, officials remained in office long enough to raise children and grandchildren. Under Emperor Xuan, outstanding prefects and magistrates were regularly comforted and encouraged by letters bearing the imperial seal, given increases in rank and gifts of gold, and not immediately transferred. There was good reason why officials fulfilled their duties and the people pursued their livelihoods in peace. Today, senior local officials are generally transferred before three years have elapsed: they do not even reach their first performance evaluation, much less a second or third. The unworthy among them say, “This is merely a posting station.” If they do anything at all, they carry out only makeshift measures, hoping to be transferred away at any moment. Who among them will devote himself to the people? Even when worthy men do devote themselves to the people, if they do not remain long in office, they have no means to demonstrate their abilities. Is it not difficult to expect them to achieve lasting results?
At the founding of our dynasty, officials both at court and in the provinces all underwent a comprehensive evaluation after nine years. Their merits and faults were assessed, and they were demoted or promoted accordingly; changes were not so hasty as they are now. Could the practice of lengthy appointments not be implemented again? Under the Han system, exceptional officials of the two-thousand-bushel salary grade could enter the central administration as Censor-in-chief. Thus Zhuo Mao was summoned from his post as Magistrate of Mi to become Grand Preceptor, without being constrained by formal qualifications. If one treats men with extraordinary regard, they will surely hold themselves to extraordinary standards.

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
今循良者未能表其殊絕而待以不次之
位欲使闒茸委瑣之流革舊樹新焉亦難
矣舉殊擢之典以作循良之風又獨不可
以舉行乎漢宣有言安靜之吏悃幅無華
日計不足歲計有餘而今監司所取於守
令者不然程之於簿書期會之間稽之於
將迎應酬之際夫實心愛民者則於節目
也必疎今以其節目之疎而略其實心之
政又誰勸於為善哉為今之計曷亦令監
===
司者務崇實効如實心惠政則必略其節
目之疎而直以循良待之則粉飾求知者
知所戒矣此又不可舉而行之乎周官以
六計弊群吏之治而貪殘之弊漢法尤嚴
也今為吏以贓敗若殺人不忌而惟止削
籍愚懼無以為之隄防矣按法之外獨不
可籍其贓以為養兵之費乎漢制刺史以
六條檢察非法行部駐節至有望風解印
綬者由其人賢而是非明且公耳今之監
punctuated: 今循良者未能表其殊絕，而待以不次之位，欲使闒茸委瑣之流革舊樹新焉，亦難矣。舉殊擢之典，以作循良之風，又獨不可以舉行乎？漢宣有言：「安靜之吏，悃幅無華，日計不足，歲計有餘。」而今監司所取於守令者不然，程之於簿書期會之間，稽之於將迎應酬之際。夫實心愛民者，則於節目也必疎。今以其節目之疎，而略其實心之政，又誰勸於為善哉？為今之計，曷亦令監司者務崇實効？如實心惠政，則必略其節目之疎，而直以循良待之，則粉飾求知者知所戒矣。此又不可舉而行之乎？周官以六計弊群吏之治，而貪殘之弊，漢法尤嚴也。今為吏以贓敗，若殺人不忌，而惟止削籍，愚懼無以為之隄防矣。按法之外，獨不可籍其贓，以為養兵之費乎？漢制刺史以六條檢察非法，行部駐節，至有望風解印綬者，由其人賢而是非明且公耳。今之監
translation_en:
Today, when conscientious and benevolent officials are not singled out for their exceptional merit and rewarded with appointments beyond the normal order of promotion, it is difficult to expect the base and petty to abandon their old ways and establish themselves anew. Could the practice of exceptional promotion not be implemented to encourage conscientious and benevolent administration? Emperor Xuan of the Han said: “Quiet and unassuming officials are sincere and plain, without ornament [?]; measured by the day, their achievements seem insufficient, but measured by the year, they are more than ample.” Yet this is not what today’s surveillance officials seek in prefects and magistrates. They assess them by paperwork and deadlines, and scrutinize their conduct in receiving and seeing off visitors and attending to social obligations. Those who sincerely care for the people will inevitably be lax in procedural details. If their sincere administration is disregarded because of such laxity, who will be encouraged to do good? As a remedy for the present, why not require surveillance officials to give priority to practical results? Where there is sincere and beneficent administration, they should overlook lapses in procedural details and simply treat the official as conscientious and benevolent. Those who seek recognition through embellishment will then know what to guard against. Could this too not be put into practice?

The Offices of Zhou used six criteria to judge the administration of officials, while Han law was especially strict concerning corruption and cruelty. Today, when officials are exposed for illicit gains, or kill without restraint, they suffer only removal from the official rolls. I fear this provides no effective restraint. In addition to imposing the prescribed legal penalties, could their illicit gains not be confiscated to cover the expense of maintaining troops? Under the Han system, regional inspectors investigated unlawful conduct according to six articles. When they toured their jurisdictions and halted at a place, some officials would even surrender their seals and insignia of office at the mere news of their approach. This was simply because the inspectors were worthy men whose judgments of right and wrong were clear and impartial. Today’s surveillance officials…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
司果能必其皆若人耶其所薦列者非盡
無良也而謂其皆良則未矣其所論剌者
非盡無不良也而謂其皆不良則未矣以
喜怒爲愛憎以警鈍爲賢否銓曹因之撫
按撫按因之藩臬其可否去留非必皆人
人當也是非混淆則賢者不行其志而不
肖者倖位矣欲守令之皆賢而民安也其
可得乎今唯使監司薦列必懸明秉公謬
進者罰其舉主如是則監司亦惕惕焉奉
===
法而守令之賢否得以
上聞矣噫守令者民之父母也郡邑則其家也
苟治郡邑皆如其家視民皆如其子殫智
竭力皇皇焉以圖之則生無不遂性無不
復民其有不安者哉又孰肯舍父母捐妻
子而甘心於盜賊之歸也哉此弭盜安民
誠無出於擇良吏之術矣狂瞽之言不識
時務惟執事試採擇焉
第四問
punctuated:
司果能必其皆若人耶？其所薦列者，非盡無良也，而謂其皆良則未矣。其所論剌者，非盡無不良也，而謂其皆不良則未矣。以喜怒爲愛憎，以警鈍爲賢否。銓曹因之撫按，撫按因之藩臬，其可否去留，非必皆人人當也。是非混淆，則賢者不行其志，而不肖者倖位矣。欲守令之皆賢而民安也，其可得乎？今唯使監司薦列必懸明秉公，謬進者罰其舉主。如是，則監司亦惕惕焉奉法，而守令之賢否得以上聞矣。噫！守令者，民之父母也；郡邑則其家也。苟治郡邑皆如其家，視民皆如其子，殫智竭力，皇皇焉以圖之，則生無不遂，性無不復，民其有不安者哉？又孰肯舍父母、捐妻子，而甘心於盜賊之歸也哉？此弭盜安民，誠無出於擇良吏之術矣。狂瞽之言，不識時務，惟執事試採擇焉。

第四問
translation_en:
…supervisory officials: can we truly be certain that they are all such men? Those they recommend are not all unworthy, but to call them all worthy would be unwarranted. Among those they impeach, there are indeed some who are unworthy [?], but to call them all unworthy would likewise be unwarranted. They let their pleasure and anger determine whom they favor or dislike, and judge worthiness by quickness or dullness of wit. The personnel authorities rely upon the grand coordinators and regional inspectors, who in turn rely upon the provincial administration and surveillance commissioners [?]. Their decisions to approve or reject, dismiss or retain, do not necessarily do justice to every individual. When right and wrong become confused, worthy men cannot carry out their aims, while the unworthy obtain office through undeserved good fortune. Can one then hope that prefects and magistrates will all be worthy and the people at peace? We need only require supervisory officials to exercise clear judgment and impartiality in making recommendations, and punish the recommending official whenever someone is wrongly advanced. Then supervisory officials will also observe the law with vigilant care, and the worthiness or unworthiness of prefects and magistrates can be made known to the throne.

Ah! Prefects and magistrates are the fathers and mothers of the people, and their prefectures and counties are their households. If they all governed their prefectures and counties as their own households, regarded the people as their own children, exhausted their intelligence and strength, and worked anxiously for their welfare, then every life would flourish and every person's original nature would be restored. How could any of the people fail to live in peace? Who would willingly leave his parents, abandon his wife and children, and gladly turn to banditry? Truly, for suppressing banditry and bringing peace to the people, no method surpasses choosing good officials. These rash and benighted words betray my ignorance of the needs of the times. I ask only that you, honored examiners, consider and select whatever may be useful.

Fourth Question

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吳國賓
同考試官教諭許批虛名初爲士累具實以底
補入國子能據理折衷讀者可以興起矣
同考試官教諭朱批好名非士之過惟失實則可
懼耳此作歸重採實而不專斥好名是必名實相符之士也
考試官教諭蔡批名實之辨此作盡之
考試官教諭林批敦本黜浮有裨風教
古之聖王樹聲教於天下而不可眩以名
實者握其機而已古之賢士以德業爲已
===
任而不以名實自眩者行其志而已機者
何也天下之勢不可使極重而不可反也
故名所以表實者也崇名太甚則浮競之
士將寘力焉抑名太過則晏安之人兀奔
走之聖王斟酌於二者之間而折衷之以
勵世設教故聖王雖取人以名未嘗不責
人以實非徒徇乎其名已也此之謂握其
機古之賢士何獨爲不然篤其道德才藝
之實德業樹於已則聲名加於人固不以
punctuated:
吳國賓

同考試官教諭許批：「虛名初爲士累，具實以底補入國子，能據理折衷，讀者可以興起矣。」

同考試官教諭朱批：「好名非士之過，惟失實則可懼耳。此作歸重採實，而不專斥好名，是必名實相符之士也。」

考試官教諭蔡批：「名實之辨，此作盡之。」

考試官教諭林批：「敦本黜浮，有裨風教。」

古之聖王樹聲教於天下，而不可眩以名實者，握其機而已。古之賢士以德業爲已任，而不以名實自眩者，行其志而已。機者何也？天下之勢，不可使極重而不可反也。故名所以表實者也，崇名太甚，則浮競之士將寘力焉；抑名太過，則晏安之人兀奔走之。聖王斟酌於二者之間，而折衷之，以勵世設教。故聖王雖取人以名，未嘗不責人以實，非徒徇乎其名已也。此之謂握其機。古之賢士何獨爲不然？篤其道德才藝之實，德業樹於已，則聲名加於人，固不以
translation_en:
Wu Guobin

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Empty reputation initially burdens scholars. Possessing substance so as to … gain admission to the Directorate of Education [?]. The author can weigh the matter judiciously on the basis of principle; readers may be inspired by this.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “Loving reputation is no fault in a scholar; only a lack of substance is to be feared. This essay places the emphasis on seeking substance, rather than exclusively condemning the love of reputation. Its author must surely be a scholar whose reputation matches his substance.”

Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “This essay exhaustively treats the distinction between reputation and substance.”

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “It strengthens the foundations and rejects superficiality, contributing to moral instruction and the improvement of customs.”

The sage kings of antiquity established their civilizing influence throughout the realm and could not be deceived by reputation and substance, simply because they grasped the crucial point. The worthy scholars of antiquity took virtue and achievement as their own responsibility and did not let reputation and substance cloud their judgment, simply because they carried out their aspirations. What is this crucial point? The tendencies prevailing in the realm must not be allowed to become so heavily weighted in one direction that they cannot be reversed. Reputation serves to make substance manifest. If reputation is exalted excessively, superficial, competitive scholars will devote their efforts to it; if reputation is disparaged excessively, those content with ease will … rush about in pursuit of it [?]. The sage kings weighed these two extremes and struck a balance between them, thereby encouraging the world and establishing moral instruction. Thus, although the sage kings selected men by reputation, they invariably demanded substance of them; they did not merely follow their reputations. This is what is meant by grasping the crucial point. How could the worthy scholars of antiquity alone have acted otherwise? They cultivated the substance of their moral character, abilities, and accomplishments. Once virtue and achievement were established within themselves, renown was bestowed upon them by others. They certainly did not take …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
名為事亦不以名為諱也此之謂行其志
此名實之大較也執事發策而以名實之
辨下詢末學何足以知之雖然竊嘗聞之
矣昔者聖王以名實設教旌別淑慝昭示
好惡於天下故佑賢輔德而天下之為德
義者勸矣式閭封墓而天下之為忠讓者
慕矣聖王所以勵世興行者恒必由之若
抑而不用則好惡不彰而為善者怠故紫
磨之金而與瓦礫同價則鬻金者稀矣千
===
里之足而與果下同售則鬻驥者稀矣有
國家者亦奚利於此而為之乎若夫士之
所以自處者則孳孳為善知為之在我者
當如是而已人苟不知焉實至而名不孚
不計也人苟知焉雖涉於好名不恤也夫
慕名而為善者為之不已則性之矣避好
名之嫌而不敢為者是善終無時可為也
又奚必以名為諱乎然而古今之議者每
不取於好名之士而論治者恒以抑浮名
punctuated: 名為事，亦不以名為諱也。此之謂行其志。此名實之大較也。執事發策，而以名實之辨下詢，末學何足以知之？雖然，竊嘗聞之矣。昔者聖王以名實設教，旌別淑慝，昭示好惡於天下，故佑賢輔德，而天下之為德義者勸矣；式閭封墓，而天下之為忠讓者慕矣。聖王所以勵世興行者，恒必由之。若抑而不用，則好惡不彰，而為善者怠。故紫磨之金而與瓦礫同價，則鬻金者稀矣；千里之足而與果下同售，則鬻驥者稀矣。有國家者亦奚利於此而為之乎？若夫士之所以自處者，則孳孳為善，知為之在我者當如是而已。人苟不知焉，實至而名不孚，不計也；人苟知焉，雖涉於好名，不恤也。夫慕名而為善者，為之不已，則性之矣；避好名之嫌而不敢為者，是善終無時可為也。又奚必以名為諱乎？然而古今之議者，每不取於好名之士，而論治者恒以抑浮名
translation_en:
…make reputation their pursuit, nor do they treat reputation as something to shun. This is what is meant by carrying out one’s aspirations. Such is the broad outline of the relationship between reputation and substance. You, honored Examiner, have issued a policy question, deigning to ask about the distinction between reputation and substance. How could a student of such meager learning as myself understand it adequately? Nevertheless, I have heard something of the matter.

In antiquity, the sage kings used reputation and substance to establish moral instruction, distinguishing the good from the wicked and making their approval and disapproval manifest throughout the realm. Thus, by supporting the worthy and assisting the virtuous, they encouraged all those in the realm who practiced virtue and righteousness. By bowing at the gates of worthy men’s neighborhoods and raising mounds over their graves, they inspired admiration among those devoted to loyalty and deference. The sage kings invariably relied upon these means to encourage the world and promote virtuous conduct. If such recognition were suppressed and left unused, approval and disapproval would not be manifest, and those doing good would grow remiss. Thus, if highly refined gold fetched the same price as broken tiles and pebbles, few would offer gold for sale; if a horse capable of traveling a thousand li sold for the same price as a pony small enough to pass beneath fruit trees, few would offer fine steeds for sale. What advantage could rulers of states find in doing this?

As for how a scholar should conduct himself, he should diligently do good, knowing only that this is how he ought to act in matters within his own control. If others do not recognize him, and his substance is fully developed but his reputation has not gained credence, he does not reckon it a concern. If others do recognize him, he does not worry even if this exposes him to the charge of seeking reputation. For one who does good out of a desire for reputation will, by persisting without cease, make goodness his nature. But one who dares not act for fear of being suspected of seeking reputation will never find a time when he can do good. Why, then, must reputation be treated as something to shun? Yet commentators, ancient and modern, frequently disapprove of scholars who seek reputation, while those who discuss government constantly advocate suppressing empty reputation…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
屏虚僞爲言者何也蓋所惡於好名者非
惡其好名也惡好其名而不務其實者也
夫畫脂鏤氷之無裨於實用無其質而學
其文者也兔絲燕麥之不救於饑寒有其
名而無其實者也此誠僞之辨不可以不
察也善乎昔人之言名實也宋之薛季宣
謂人主爲社稷計惟恐士之不好名陳塤
謂求士於三代之上惟恐其好名求士於
三代之下惟恐其不好名而司馬光則獨
===
以采名不采實爲國家之患合三子之言
而觀之而後名實之義備焉雖然薛季宣
謂人主惟恐士之不好名似矣又以好名
爲臣子學問之累則抑揚太過而未盡於
義也夫以孔子之聖也而疾没世之不稱
屈子之賢也而懼脩名之不立士之好名
果可盡非乎使好名果爲臣子學問之累
則人君奚取焉若曰上之取士與士之自
處不以名爲諱必以實爲先則善矣陳塤
punctuated:
屏虚僞爲言者，何也？蓋所惡於好名者，非惡其好名也，惡好其名而不務其實者也。夫畫脂鏤氷之無裨於實用，無其質而學其文者也；兔絲燕麥之不救於饑寒，有其名而無其實者也。此誠僞之辨，不可以不察也。
善乎昔人之言名實也！宋之薛季宣謂人主爲社稷計，惟恐士之不好名；陳塤謂求士於三代之上，惟恐其好名，求士於三代之下，惟恐其不好名；而司馬光則獨以采名不采實爲國家之患。合三子之言而觀之，而後名實之義備焉。
雖然，薛季宣謂人主惟恐士之不好名，似矣；又以好名爲臣子學問之累，則抑揚太過，而未盡於義也。夫以孔子之聖也，而疾没世之不稱；屈子之賢也，而懼脩名之不立。士之好名，果可盡非乎？使好名果爲臣子學問之累，則人君奚取焉？若曰上之取士與士之自處，不以名爲諱，必以實爲先，則善矣。陳塤
translation_en:
…and speak of banishing falsehood—why is this? What they dislike in those who seek reputation is not their desire for reputation itself, but their desire for the name without attending to the substance. Drawing on grease and carving ice contribute nothing to practical use: this is to imitate outward refinement without possessing its underlying substance. Dodder and wild oats cannot relieve hunger and cold: they possess the names of useful things but lack their substance. This distinction between sincerity and falsehood must be carefully examined.
How well earlier thinkers spoke of reputation and substance! Xue Jixuan of the Song said that a ruler, in planning for the state, fears only that scholars will not care for reputation. Chen Xun said that, in seeking scholars from the Three Dynasties and earlier, one fears only that they care for reputation; in seeking scholars from after the Three Dynasties, one fears only that they do not. Sima Guang, however, singled out choosing men for reputation rather than substance as a danger to the state. Only by considering these three thinkers’ statements together can we fully understand the relationship between reputation and substance.
Nevertheless, Xue Jixuan’s statement that a ruler fears only that scholars will not care for reputation seems right. Yet when he also regards concern for reputation as an impediment to the learning of subjects and sons, his praise and blame go too far, and his account does not fully capture what is right. Even Confucius, with all his sageliness, deplored the prospect of dying without his name being celebrated; even Master Qu, with all his worthiness, feared that an enduring reputation would not be established. Can scholars’ desire for reputation really be condemned outright? If that desire truly impedes the learning of subjects and sons, why would a ruler value it? It would be sound to say that, both when rulers select scholars and when scholars conduct themselves, they should not shun reputation but must give substance priority. Chen Xun…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂後世之士惟恐其不好名似矣謂三
代之士惟恐其好名則有激之言而未足
為通論也成王之告君陳曰終有辭於永
世康王之命畢公曰亦有無窮之聞三代
之上何嘗以名為病乎使三代而果以名
為病也則後世奚取焉若曰三代之世未
嘗不勸人以名而必責人以實則善矣荀
爽謁李膺而歸也以得御為喜曹嵩因趙
咨之過營陽也以不留為愧東漢之士以
===
===
聲名相高如此其弊也黨錮成而漢禍起
豈非好名之為祟哉然以曹操之彊而猶
憚一孔融未必非名節之重有以繫之也
使東漢之君不務抑其名而必責其實則
光武明章之治雖復見可也謝安以友人
之故取蒲葵題之而價增數倍王導以帑
藏之乏取練布衣之而練價騰湧東晉之
士以聲名相高如此其弊也清談盛而晉
室衰豈非虚名之為累哉然以偏安之勢
punctuated:
所謂後世之士惟恐其不好名，似矣；謂三代之士惟恐其好名，則有激之言，而未足為通論也。成王之告君陳曰：「終有辭於永世。」康王之命畢公曰：「亦有無窮之聞。」三代之上，何嘗以名為病乎？使三代而果以名為病也，則後世奚取焉？若曰三代之世未嘗不勸人以名，而必責人以實，則善矣。
荀爽謁李膺而歸也，以得御為喜；曹嵩因趙咨之過營陽也，以不留為愧。東漢之士以聲名相高如此，其弊也，黨錮成而漢禍起，豈非好名之為祟哉？然以曹操之彊，而猶憚一孔融，未必非名節之重有以繫之也。使東漢之君不務抑其名而必責其實，則光武、明、章之治，雖復見可也。
謝安以友人之故，取蒲葵題之，而價增數倍；王導以帑藏之乏，取練布衣之，而練價騰湧。東晉之士以聲名相高如此，其弊也，清談盛而晉室衰，豈非虚名之為累哉？然以偏安之勢
translation_en:
…the assertion that, among scholars of later ages, the only fear was that they might not cherish a good name seems right. But to say that, among scholars of the Three Dynasties, the only fear was that they might cherish a good name is a deliberately pointed statement, insufficient as a general judgment. King Cheng admonished Jun Chen, saying: “You will forever be spoken of in ages to come.” King Kang charged the Duke of Bi, saying: “You too will have unending renown.” In the ancient days of the Three Dynasties, when was reputation ever considered a fault? If the Three Dynasties had truly regarded it as a fault, what could later ages learn from them? It would be sound to say that the Three Dynasties never failed to encourage people through reputation, but invariably demanded substance from them.
When Xun Shuang returned from visiting Li Ying, he rejoiced at having been allowed to drive his carriage. When Zhao Zi passed through Yingyang [?], Cao Song [?] felt ashamed that he had failed to persuade him to stay. Such was the way scholars of the Eastern Han competed for eminence through reputation. Its harmful consequence was that the proscriptions against partisan groups took shape and calamity arose for the Han. Was this not the mischief wrought by the love of fame? Yet even Cao Cao, powerful as he was, still feared a single Kong Rong. It may well have been the weight of reputation and moral integrity that exerted some restraint upon him. Had the rulers of the Eastern Han insisted on substance rather than making it their business to suppress these men's reputations, the good government of Emperors Guangwu, Ming, and Zhang might have been seen again.
For a friend's sake, Xie An took palm-leaf fans and inscribed them [?], and their price rose severalfold. Because the treasury was depleted, Wang Dao took a garment of bleached silk and wore it, whereupon the price of that silk soared. Such was the way scholars of the Eastern Jin competed for eminence through reputation. Its harmful consequence was that pure conversation flourished while the Jin ruling house declined. Was this not the burden imposed by empty fame? Yet, given the dynasty's position, maintaining itself in only one part of the realm…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而江左賴以寧謐未必非王謝之賢有以
維之也使晉之君不徒崇其名而必責其
實焉則王導謝安之徒雖比肩可也龐統
性好人倫稱述多過曰不加美言則聲名
不足慕而為善者少奬進人材者不當如
此耶韓康賣藥長安以女子知名曰本欲
避名今女子皆知有我入霸陵山以避之
隱者之志也是或一道矣宋之魏琰之汲
引後進推輓成就有訾其好名者則曰使
===
夫人而避此則為善之路絕矣元之程思
廉恤孤賑窮薦達人物有譏其好名者曰
若避好名之嫌人不敢復為善矣此二子
者信於心而不疑於迹不亦可以為訓乎
哉執事又欲使士之所以自持審擇於斯
二者而知所輕重
國之所以取士斟酌於斯二者而知所折衷
名實參而由焉此執事欲使天下砥礪名
行以不負
punctuated:
而江左賴以寧謐，未必非王謝之賢有以維之也。使晉之君不徒崇其名，而必責其實焉，則王導、謝安之徒雖比肩可也。龐統性好人倫，稱述多過，曰：「不加美言，則聲名不足慕，而為善者少。」奬進人材者不當如此耶？韓康賣藥長安，以女子知名，曰：「本欲避名，今女子皆知有我。」入霸陵山以避之，隱者之志也，是或一道矣。宋之魏琰之汲引後進，推輓成就，有訾其好名者，則曰：「使夫人而避此，則為善之路絕矣。」元之程思廉恤孤賑窮，薦達人物，有譏其好名者，曰：「若避好名之嫌，人不敢復為善矣。」此二子者，信於心而不疑於迹，不亦可以為訓乎哉？

執事又欲使士之所以自持，審擇於斯二者而知所輕重；國之所以取士，斟酌於斯二者而知所折衷。名實參而由焉，此執事欲使天下砥礪名行，以不負
translation_en:
…and the lands south of the Yangzi depended on this for their peace and tranquility; surely the worthiness of Wang Dao and Xie An may have helped sustain them. Had the rulers of Jin done more than exalt their reputations, and insisted on substantive achievement, men like Wang Dao and Xie An might have stood shoulder to shoulder in abundance. Pang Tong was by disposition fond of appraising people, and his praise often exceeded their merits. He said: “Unless one adds fine words, their reputations will not be sufficient to inspire admiration, and few people will do good.” Should those who encourage and advance talent not act in this way? Han Kang sold medicines in Chang’an. When a woman recognized him, he said: “I originally wished to escape fame, but now even women know of me.” He entered the mountains of Baling to escape it. Such was a recluse’s resolve; this, perhaps, is one way to proceed. Wei Yanzhi [?] of the Song drew younger men forward, promoting them and helping them establish themselves. When someone criticized him for seeking fame, he said: “If everyone were to avoid this, the path to doing good would be cut off.” Cheng Silian of the Yuan cared for orphans, relieved the poor, and recommended worthy men for advancement. When someone mocked him for seeking fame, he said: “If people avoided the suspicion of seeking fame, they would no longer dare to do good.” These two men trusted what was in their hearts and were not troubled by how their actions appeared. Might they not serve as examples?

You further wish scholars, in determining how to conduct themselves, to weigh these two considerations carefully and understand their relative importance; and the state, in selecting scholars, to deliberate upon these two considerations and understand how to strike the proper balance. Reputation and substance should be considered together and made the basis for action. This is your wish to have all under Heaven cultivate their reputations and conduct, so as not to fail…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
明時之盛心也竊謂世道轉移之機在上而不
在下在近而不在遠故高結大袖猶足移
俗而况樹之以風聲先之以好惡乎方人
之欲化民成俗者將欲抑名而退之與則
惡成樂敗多訾少譽世已不好名矣好稱
人之善孰為龐士元若之何其抑之也欲
崇名而進之與則授徒養交釣合虛譽世
已好名矣避名不居孰為韓伯休若之何
其崇之也故愚以為
===
國之所以取士必若薛季宣陳傅良所謂惟恐
其不好名而參以司馬光采實之論是之
謂知所折衷士之所以自持者必若魏琰
之程思廉不避好名之嫌而復戒趙李王
謝標榜之非是之謂知所輕重名實參而
由焉則風行令流道德材藝之士彬彬於
聖世而
社稷靈長之慶終將賴之矣雖然愚生又有說
焉龐統之獎進人材善突然稱述太過是
punctuated: 明時之盛心也。竊謂世道轉移之機，在上而不在下，在近而不在遠。故高結大袖，猶足移俗，而况樹之以風聲，先之以好惡乎？方人之欲化民成俗者，將欲抑名而退之與？則惡成樂敗，多訾少譽，世已不好名矣。好稱人之善，孰為龐士元？若之何其抑之也？欲崇名而進之與？則授徒養交，釣合虛譽，世已好名矣。避名不居，孰為韓伯休？若之何其崇之也？故愚以為，國之所以取士，必若薛季宣、陳傅良所謂惟恐其不好名，而參以司馬光采實之論，是之謂知所折衷。士之所以自持者，必若魏琰之、程思廉不避好名之嫌，而復戒趙李王謝標榜之非，是之謂知所輕重。名實參而由焉，則風行令流，道德材藝之士彬彬於聖世，而社稷靈長之慶，終將賴之矣。雖然，愚生又有說焉。龐統之獎進人材，善突，然稱述太過，是
translation_en:
…the lofty intention of this enlightened age. I venture to suggest that the power to transform the ways of the world lies with those above, not those below, and in what is near, not what is distant. Thus even high hair-knots and broad sleeves suffice to change customs; how much more so when standards are established through moral influence and the lead is given through expressed likes and dislikes!

Should those who wish to transform the people and shape their customs now seek to depreciate reputation and discourage its pursuit? Yet people resent others’ success and rejoice in their failure; they disparage much and praise little. The world already cares little for a good name. Who, like Pang Shiyuan, delights in praising others’ goodness? How, then, could one suppress concern for reputation? Should one instead exalt reputation and encourage its pursuit? Yet people gather disciples and cultivate connections, angling for undeserved acclaim. The world already covets reputation. Who, like Han Boxiu, shuns fame and refuses to claim it? How, then, could one exalt it?

Thus, in my humble view, when the state selects men for office, it must follow what Xue Jixuan and Chen Fuliang advocated—fearing only that men might not care for a good name—while weighing this against Sima Guang’s argument for seeking actual merit. This is what it means to know how to strike the proper balance. In their own conduct, scholars must, like Wei Yanzhi [?] and Cheng Silian, refuse to shrink from the suspicion that they seek a good name, while also guarding against the fault of mutual promotion exemplified by Zhao, Li, Wang, and Xie. This is what it means to know the relative importance of things. If reputation and substance are weighed together and made the basis for action, moral influence will spread and commands will circulate freely. Men of virtue, talent, and accomplishment will flourish in this sagely age, and the blessing of the dynasty’s enduring longevity will ultimately depend upon them.

Nevertheless, this humble scholar has a further point to make. Pang Tong’s encouragement and advancement of talented men was commendable [?]; yet his praise was excessive. This is …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
爽實也孰若郭林宗之獎拔士類後皆如
其所言不亦庶幾於夫子所譽必有所試
之旨乎韓康之逃名入山善矣然自爲太
甚是絶物也孰若范史雲之童豎知名嘆
息益以自勵不亦庶幾於夫子俛焉日有
孳孳之訓乎魏揆之程思廉之不避好名
之嫌此特其自爲者耳猶其小者也孰若
趙充國所謂豈嫌伐一時事用兵國之大
事當明言利害以爲後法范忠宣所謂區
===
區愛君之心不能自已若避好名之嫌則
無爲善之路其忠於謀國有如此者不亦
庶幾於夫子于其身以善其君之義乎愚
生尚友之志如此未知其果不詭於聖門
爲己之學否也執事幸與其進而教之
第五問
陳文燧
同考試官教諭汪批〔議論有識見似老將躬履行陣者他日大用可見經略於此作矣〕
punctuated:
爽實也。孰若郭林宗之獎拔士類，後皆如其所言，不亦庶幾於夫子「所譽必有所試」之旨乎？韓康之逃名入山，善矣，然自爲太甚，是絶物也。孰若范史雲之童豎知名，嘆息益以自勵，不亦庶幾於夫子「俛焉日有孳孳」之訓乎？魏揆之、程思廉之不避好名之嫌，此特其自爲者耳，猶其小者也。孰若趙充國所謂「豈嫌伐一時事？用兵，國之大事，當明言利害，以爲後法」，范忠宣所謂「區區愛君之心不能自已，若避好名之嫌，則無爲善之路」？其忠於謀國有如此者，不亦庶幾於夫子「于其身以善其君」之義乎？愚生尚友之志如此，未知其果不詭於聖門爲己之學否也。執事幸與其進而教之。

第五問
陳文燧
同考試官教諭汪批〔議論有識見，似老將躬履行陣者。他日大用，可見經略於此作矣。〕
translation_en:
…this departs from the truth. How could it compare with Guo Linzong’s promotion of worthy scholars, who afterward all proved to be as he had described them? Does this not approach the purport of the Master’s saying, “Those whom I praise must have been put to the test”?

Han Kang’s retreat into the mountains to escape fame was admirable. Yet he went too far in acting for himself: this was to cut himself off from others. How could it compare with Fan Shiyun, who, when even children knew his name, sighed and urged himself on all the more? Does this not approach the Master’s teaching to “exert oneself diligently day after day”?

Wei Kuizhi and Cheng Silian did not shrink from the suspicion of seeking fame, but this concerned only their own conduct; it was still a lesser matter. How could it compare with Zhao Chongguo’s statement, “Why fear the suspicion of boasting about a single undertaking? Warfare is a great affair of state. Its advantages and disadvantages must be clearly stated, to provide a model for later generations”; or with Fan Zhongxuan’s statement, “My humble devotion to my sovereign cannot restrain itself. If I avoid the suspicion of seeking fame, there will be no path left for doing good”? Such was their loyalty in planning for the state. Does this not approach the Master’s principle of “[exerting?] oneself to make one’s ruler good” [?]?

Such is my aspiration, as a humble student, to seek fellowship with the worthy men of antiquity. I do not know whether it truly accords with the learning for one’s own moral improvement taught in the school of the Sage. I hope that you, Sir, will approve my efforts to advance and instruct me.

Fifth Question
Chen Wensui

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔The argument shows discernment, like that of a veteran general who has personally served in the ranks. Should he be entrusted with great responsibilities in the future, his capacity for strategic planning can already be seen in this composition.〕

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭黎批洞見時機非徒剿竊成文
者子殆江右俊傑乎
考試官教諭蔡批論用兵不容已處嚴正矣
考試官教諭林批切實可行
執事發策而以弭盜下詢愚聞魯爲稷曲
之戰用矛入齊冉有爲之泗上之役選徒
奔吳有若與焉此皆章逢之士有事用之
於戰闘者也故四郊多壘非特卿大夫之
辱亦士之耻也邇者惵惡之民弄兵於閩
===
廣滋蔓於江右以爲執事憂執干戈以敵
愾愚愧未能也明問弭盜之策敢無辭以
對荀卿有言口能言之身雖不能行之國
用也或者其庶幾乎書稱蠻夷猾夏寇賊
姦宄唐虞之世盖已有之自倭夷跳梁於
東南而閩廣山峒海島之民煽結爲盜揆
厥所原以爲歲歉艱食所致此特其一耳
而政失於撫綏法漏於疎網守令之臣有
不得辭其責者矣吉贛之荼毒撫建之鈔
punctuated:
同考試官教諭黎批：洞見時機，非徒剿竊成文者，子殆江右俊傑乎！
考試官教諭蔡批：論用兵不容已處，嚴正矣。
考試官教諭林批：切實可行。
執事發策而以弭盜下詢。愚聞魯爲稷曲之戰，用矛入齊，冉有爲之；泗上之役，選徒奔吳，有若與焉。此皆章逢之士，有事用之於戰闘者也。故四郊多壘，非特卿大夫之辱，亦士之耻也。邇者惵惡之民，弄兵於閩廣，滋蔓於江右，以爲執事憂。執干戈以敵愾，愚愧未能也。明問弭盜之策，敢無辭以對？荀卿有言：「口能言之，身雖不能行之，國用也。」或者其庶幾乎？《書》稱：「蠻夷猾夏，寇賊姦宄。」唐虞之世，盖已有之。自倭夷跳梁於東南，而閩廣山峒海島之民，煽結爲盜。揆厥所原，以爲歲歉艱食所致，此特其一耳。而政失於撫綏，法漏於疎網，守令之臣有不得辭其責者矣。吉贛之荼毒，撫建之鈔
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: You perceive the circumstances of the time with penetrating insight; you are no mere plagiarist of existing writings. Surely you are an outstanding talent of Jiangyou!

Comment by Examiner Cai, Instructor: Your discussion of the circumstances in which employing troops is unavoidable is rigorous and sound.

Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: Practical and feasible.

You have set a policy question, condescending to ask about suppressing banditry. I have heard that when Lu fought the battle of Jiqu, Ran You wielded a spear and entered Qi [?]; and that in the campaign on the Si River, when selected foot soldiers hastened against Wu, You Ruo took part. These were both scholars wearing the robes and caps of their calling, who were employed in battle when circumstances required it. Thus, when enemy fortifications abound on all four outskirts, the disgrace belongs not only to ministers and grandees: scholars too should feel ashamed. Recently, wicked people [?] have taken up arms in Fujian and Guangdong, and their depredations have spread into Jiangyou, causing you concern. I am ashamed that I have been unable to take up shield and spear to resist the enemy. Yet when you expressly ask for a policy to suppress banditry, how could I venture to offer no reply? Xun Qing said: “One who can articulate it, even if unable to carry it out himself, can be useful to the state.” Perhaps I might approach that standard?

The Book of Documents says: “The Man and Yi disturb Xia; there are robbers, malefactors, and wrongdoers within and without.” Such people evidently existed even in the age of Tang and Yu. Since the Japanese marauders began running rampant in the southeast, inhabitants of the mountain valleys and offshore islands of Fujian and Guangdong have incited one another and banded together as bandits. To trace the origins of this and attribute it to poor harvests and difficulty obtaining food identifies only one cause. Government has failed to pacify and reassure the people, while the loose mesh of the law has let offenders escape. Prefects and county magistrates cannot evade their responsibility for this. The devastation of Ji’an and Ganzhou, the pillaging of Fuzhou and Jianchang…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
掠江右之民欲得而甘心之日久矣然而
獻謀畫計言之罔效者何也意者縢囊捃
背之說乎執事謂聚兵散走罷兵復來則
禦之難山谷阻深草木蓊翳則追之難彼
以飽待饑我米籸不饜則糧餉之難崑崗
之炎玉石俱焚巫山之火芝艾罔辨則處
勝之難是固然矣愚以為盜之方至則聚
兵以扼其來盜之既去則伏兵以邀其歸
或先其未備而攻之或伺其懈怠而取之
===
不分兵以為守必併力以為戰形人而我
無形致人而不致於人則不患於禦盜追
盜之難矣臨期而徵糧於郡邑則遲緩而
後時負檐而責成於編甿則驚竄而僨事
故莫若十人之外別選一人以為餘卒而
專官以督其事糧餉先期而徵辦餘卒隨
軍而轉輸戮黨附以杜其原赦脅從以携
其黨則不患於糧餉處勝之難矣或廣中
驅之法不可行於谿谷草澤風雲蛇鳥之
punctuated: 掠，江右之民欲得而甘心之日久矣。然而獻謀畫計，言之罔效者，何也？意者縢囊捃背之說乎？執事謂聚兵散走，罷兵復來，則禦之難；山谷阻深，草木蓊翳，則追之難；彼以飽待饑，我米籸不饜，則糧餉之難；崑崗之炎，玉石俱焚，巫山之火，芝艾罔辨，則處勝之難。是固然矣。愚以為盜之方至，則聚兵以扼其來；盜之既去，則伏兵以邀其歸。或先其未備而攻之，或伺其懈怠而取之。不分兵以為守，必併力以為戰。形人而我無形，致人而不致於人，則不患於禦盜、追盜之難矣。臨期而徵糧於郡邑，則遲緩而後時；負檐而責成於編甿，則驚竄而僨事。故莫若十人之外，別選一人以為餘卒，而專官以督其事。糧餉先期而徵辦，餘卒隨軍而轉輸。戮黨附以杜其原，赦脅從以携其黨，則不患於糧餉、處勝之難矣。或廣中驅之法不可行於谿谷草澤，風雲蛇鳥之
translation_en:
…plundering—the people of Jiangyou have long wished to seize these bandits and satisfy their resentment. Yet why have the proposals and plans offered proved ineffective? Might this be a case of the saying about binding up a sack and gathering at the back [?]? You say that when troops assemble, the bandits scatter, and when troops withdraw, they return: hence the difficulty of resisting them. The mountain valleys are rugged and deep, and vegetation grows thick: hence the difficulty of pursuing them. They await us well fed while we go hungry, unable to obtain even enough rice and grain residue [?]: hence the difficulty of provisioning. As in a fire on the Kunlun ridges, jade and common stone burn together; as in a fire on Mount Wu, fragrant herbs and mugwort are not distinguished: hence the difficulty of handling victory. This is indeed so.

In my humble view, when bandits approach, troops should assemble to block their advance; once they depart, troops should lie in ambush to intercept their return. Sometimes we should attack before they are prepared; sometimes we should wait until they grow careless and then capture them. Rather than divide our troops for defense, we must concentrate our strength for battle. Make the enemy reveal his dispositions while concealing our own; make the enemy come to us without allowing ourselves to be drawn to him. Then the difficulties of resisting and pursuing bandits need cause no concern.

If grain is requisitioned from prefectures and counties only when it is needed, delays will make it arrive too late. If responsibility for carrying supplies on shoulder poles is imposed on the registered common people, they will flee in alarm and ruin the undertaking. Thus nothing is better than selecting one additional man for every ten to serve as an auxiliary soldier, and assigning a dedicated official to supervise the work. Grain and provisions should be requisitioned and prepared beforehand, while the auxiliary soldiers accompany the army to transport them. Execute willing adherents to cut off the source of banditry, and pardon those compelled to join, so as to split their following. Then the difficulties of provisioning and handling victory need cause no concern.

Perhaps methods of driving forward across open ground cannot be employed in ravines and marshy thickets, and the wind, cloud, snake, and bird formations…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
制不可行於險阻陿阨故常以數倍之師
攻賊而反為其所困何也愚以為古之陣
法不過分合奇正而已我兵雖多聚而不
分賊兵雖寡以伏為奇非兵之不多用之
者失也苟能師其意而用之奇兵數出使
賊不知其所攻首尾夾攻使賊不知其所
備遣良將以踰伏率精銳以奮擊雖剪滅
之而後朝食可也此所謂師古之意而不
用其迹者也古法何嘗不可行於今乎摧
===
堅陷陣莫若火器執事謂製之不善用之
不精則反為害者是也故不知火器之害
者不盡知其利製火器者必先眠其管欲
其管之直也不直則不能以中眠其銅鐵
之厚薄欲其厚薄之均也不均則劈裂而
反害今之製器者果盡合於此乎所用非
所習心戰手慄而不能以命中未見賊而
先發意在虛誑而不期於殺賊今之用器
者果能免於此乎故議者欲選閩浙之善
punctuated:
制不可行於險阻陿阨，故常以數倍之師攻賊，而反為其所困，何也？愚以為古之陣法，不過分合奇正而已。我兵雖多，聚而不分；賊兵雖寡，以伏為奇。非兵之不多，用之者失也。苟能師其意而用之，奇兵數出，使賊不知其所攻；首尾夾攻，使賊不知其所備；遣良將以踰伏，率精銳以奮擊，雖剪滅之而後朝食可也。此所謂師古之意而不用其迹者也。古法何嘗不可行於今乎？

摧堅陷陣，莫若火器。執事謂製之不善、用之不精，則反為害者，是也。故不知火器之害者，不盡知其利。製火器者必先眠其管，欲其管之直也；不直，則不能以中。眠其銅鐵之厚薄，欲其厚薄之均也；不均，則劈裂而反害。今之製器者，果盡合於此乎？所用非所習，心戰手慄，而不能以命中；未見賊而先發，意在虛誑，而不期於殺賊。今之用器者，果能免於此乎？故議者欲選閩浙之善
translation_en:
…formations cannot be employed in rugged terrain and narrow defiles. Thus we often attack the bandits with forces several times their number, only to find ourselves hard pressed by them. Why is this? In my humble view, ancient methods of battle formation amounted simply to dividing and combining forces and employing surprise and regular tactics. Though our troops are numerous, they mass together without dividing; though the bandits’ troops are few, they use ambushes to achieve surprise. The trouble is not insufficient troops, but errors by those who employ them. If we can follow the underlying principles and apply them, repeatedly sending out surprise forces so that the bandits do not know where we will attack, attacking their front and rear together so that they do not know where to defend, and dispatching capable generals to pass beyond their ambushes [?] and lead picked troops in vigorous assaults, we could even annihilate them before taking our morning meal. This is what is meant by following the intentions of the ancients without adopting their outward forms. When have ancient methods ever been inapplicable to the present?

For breaking strong positions and penetrating battle formations, nothing equals firearms. You are right to say that, if poorly made or ineptly used, they instead cause harm. Thus those who do not understand the dangers of firearms do not fully understand their advantages. Those who make firearms must first inspect [?] their barrels, ensuring that they are straight; otherwise they cannot hit the target. They must inspect [?] the thickness of the copper and iron, ensuring that it is uniform; otherwise the weapon will split and cause injury to its own side. Do those who manufacture weapons today truly meet all these requirements? Men use weapons with which they have not trained: their hearts quake and their hands tremble, and they cannot hit the target. They fire before even seeing the bandits, intending merely to bluff rather than expecting to kill them. Can those who use firearms today truly avoid these faults? Thus those discussing the matter wish to select men from Fujian and Zhejiang who are skilled…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
於製器用器者而敎練江右之兵其說善
矣射疏及遠莫若弓弩執事謂射生之徒
毒藥以傅弩矢爲江右長技是也然不知
其不可用者不盡知其可用山谷之民未
嘗見敵未免驚疑潰散之患以之守城則
爲長技以之野戰非其所長且弩箭所及
不過五十步不若勁弓嚆矢之遠也今南
昌之弓手頗嘗敎習而列郡之精兵徒應
故事故議者欲使郡縣弩手專習藥弩之
===
法訓練精兵必以弓箭爲先其說善矣五
兵之用各有相制刀盾稍棒缺一不可而
江右之兵唯用長槍弱竿鈍鐵無裨實用
夫程饒之賊以旗戰爲長技廣之潰卒以
刀盾爲長技而以長槍當之所謂五不當
一者也故搴旗者必用長鉤制刀盾者必
用巨斧兵者因時而制變者也苟能深達
五兵之用相機而定制斟酌古今之變料
敵而設竒雖創以已意可也跳盪背嵬古
punctuated:
於製器用器者，而敎練江右之兵，其說善矣。射疏及遠，莫若弓弩。執事謂射生之徒，毒藥以傅弩矢，爲江右長技，是也。然不知其不可用者，不盡知其可用。山谷之民，未嘗見敵，未免驚疑潰散之患；以之守城，則爲長技；以之野戰，非其所長。且弩箭所及，不過五十步，不若勁弓嚆矢之遠也。今南昌之弓手，頗嘗敎習，而列郡之精兵，徒應故事。故議者欲使郡縣弩手專習藥弩之法，訓練精兵，必以弓箭爲先，其說善矣。
五兵之用，各有相制，刀盾稍棒，缺一不可。而江右之兵，唯用長槍，弱竿鈍鐵，無裨實用。夫程饒之賊，以旗戰爲長技；廣之潰卒，以刀盾爲長技。而以長槍當之，所謂五不當一者也。故搴旗者必用長鉤，制刀盾者必用巨斧。兵者，因時而制變者也。苟能深達五兵之用，相機而定制，斟酌古今之變，料敵而設竒，雖創以已意可也。跳盪、背嵬，古
translation_en:
…at making and using these weapons, to train the troops of Jiangyou: this proposal is sound. For shooting at scattered targets and reaching distant ones, nothing surpasses bows and crossbows. You, sir, say that hunters coat their crossbow bolts with poison, and that this is a particular strength of Jiangyou. This is correct. Yet those who do not understand where such men cannot be employed do not fully understand where they can be employed. The inhabitants of the mountain valleys have never faced an enemy and remain liable to panic, uncertainty, and dispersal. Employing them to defend cities makes use of their strength; employing them in open battle does not. Moreover, crossbow bolts reach no farther than fifty paces, falling short of the range of whistling arrows shot from powerful bows. The bowmen of Nanchang have received some training, but the picked troops of the various prefectures merely go through the prescribed motions. Thus some propose that crossbowmen in the prefectures and counties should concentrate on learning the methods of poisoned crossbows, while the training of picked troops should give priority to bows and arrows. This proposal is sound.
The five types of weapons each have means of countering one another; sabers, shields, poles [?], and staves are all indispensable. Yet the troops of Jiangyou use only long spears, with weak shafts and blunt iron heads, of no practical benefit. The bandits of Cheng and Rao [?] excel at fighting with banners, while the routed soldiers from Guang excel at using sabers and shields. To oppose them with long spears is what is meant by saying that five are no match for one. Thus those who seize banners must use long hooks, and those who counter sabers and shields must use great axes. Warfare requires adapting to changing circumstances. If one thoroughly understands the uses of the five types of weapons, determines arrangements according to the circumstances, weighs changes in practice from antiquity to the present, and devises unexpected tactics after assessing the enemy, even innovations of one’s own devising are permissible. The assault troops known as tiaodang and the beiwei troops were, in antiquity…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
之選鋒唐宋之世用以决勝而江右精兵
常兵之制倣而行之别其等差定其額數
然精兵未必皆精鋭常兵未必皆孱弱而
糧賞各異所謂所養非所用者也况精兵
歲支不及十金恐未足以得投石超距之
士善用兵者化弱以為强苟能别精常之
等而時其教練選百金之士而用為軍鋒
雖不用調募可也或謂弭盜之法在行保
甲者控弦被練官健之責也今之官健猶
===
鷇㷤也而責禦盜於保甲出入相友守望
相助外可以禦寇內可以防奸保甲之法
行而盜賊可潜消矣則保甲非在所先與
昔人所行若兖州之樓鼓新鄭之義營此
其効也或謂弭盜之法在擇守令者執馘
獻功鶡冠之任也今之鶡冠皆紈袴也而
責弭盜於守令足兵食脩器械外禦輈張
之寇內禁竒袤之民守令得其人而保甲
無不行矣則守令不為尤要歟昔人所稱
punctuated:
之選鋒，唐宋之世用以决勝，而江右精兵、常兵之制倣而行之，别其等差，定其額數。然精兵未必皆精鋭，常兵未必皆孱弱，而糧賞各異，所謂所養非所用者也。况精兵歲支不及十金，恐未足以得投石超距之士。善用兵者化弱以為强，苟能别精常之等而時其教練，選百金之士而用為軍鋒，雖不用調募可也。

或謂弭盜之法在行保甲者，控弦被練，官健之責也。今之官健猶鷇㷤也，而責禦盜於保甲。出入相友，守望相助，外可以禦寇，內可以防奸，保甲之法行而盜賊可潜消矣，則保甲非在所先與？昔人所行，若兖州之樓鼓、新鄭之義營，此其効也。

或謂弭盜之法在擇守令者，執馘獻功，鶡冠之任也。今之鶡冠皆紈袴也，而責弭盜於守令。足兵食，脩器械，外禦輈張之寇，內禁竒袤之民，守令得其人而保甲無不行矣，則守令不為尤要歟？昔人所稱
translation_en:
…the picked vanguard troops of antiquity, employed to secure victory during the Tang and Song. Jiangyou’s system of elite and ordinary troops follows their example, distinguishing their grades and fixing their quotas. Yet the elite troops are not necessarily all crack soldiers, nor are the ordinary troops necessarily all weak; nevertheless, their provisions and rewards differ. This is what is meant by maintaining men who are not those actually put to use. Moreover, an elite soldier receives less than ten taels of silver a year, which, I fear, is insufficient to attract men capable of throwing stones and clearing great distances in a leap. Those skilled in employing troops turn weakness into strength. If we can distinguish the grades of elite and ordinary troops, train them at appropriate intervals, and select warriors worth a hundred taels to serve as the army’s vanguard, we could manage even without transferring or recruiting troops.

Some say that the means of suppressing banditry lies in implementing the baojia system of mutual household responsibility. Drawing bows and wearing armor are the responsibilities of government soldiers. Today’s government soldiers are like helpless nestlings [?], yet responsibility for resisting bandits is placed on the baojia. By keeping one another company when going out and coming home, and helping one another keep watch, people can resist raiders from outside and prevent wrongdoing within. Once the baojia system is implemented, banditry can gradually disappear. Should baojia, then, not take priority? Earlier practices, such as the watchtower drums of Yanzhou and the volunteer encampments of Xinzheng, demonstrate its effectiveness.

Some say that the means of suppressing banditry lies in choosing prefects and magistrates. Taking severed ears as trophies and presenting proof of military merit are the duties of military officers, the wearers of pheasant-feather caps. Today’s military officers are all pampered sons of wealthy families, yet responsibility for suppressing banditry is placed on prefects and magistrates. They must provide sufficient troops and provisions, repair weapons and equipment, resist rampant raiders from outside, and restrain unruly inhabitants [?] within. With the right men serving as prefects and magistrates, the baojia system will be implemented everywhere. Is choosing prefects and magistrates, then, not especially important? As men of former times declared…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
若得一良令如勝兵三千人得一良守如
勝兵三萬人者此其徵也或謂盜所從來
者閩廣也今程饒之山賊滋蔓三省不合
三省之兵擣其巢穴草薙而禽獮之則疽
食之勢浸淫而不止此探本之論弭盜之
原尤方今之首務宜遄發而早圖之者也
雖然邇者
聖天子以倭寇之不靖用諫臣之言黜貪殘之
吏今又大發諸道之兵以討程饒之賊而
===
專命三省撫臣司其事監察董其師總督
重臣兼其任則執事之所謂首務要機者
聖明已舉行之矣黔黎之息肩可計日而待矣
而愚生之私憂過計又有不容已於言者
惠潮汀漳數郡鞠為盜區郡邑守令必得
有文武才略者以鎮壓之而後可以望更
始之治今貪墨者雖去而才望者未擇循
資除授未必皆龔遂張敞之徒盜之所以
未弭者此也討捕之
punctuated:
若「得一良令，如勝兵三千人；得一良守，如勝兵三萬人」者，此其徵也。或謂盜所從來者，閩廣也。今程饒之山賊滋蔓三省，不合三省之兵，擣其巢穴，草薙而禽獮之，則疽食之勢浸淫而不止。此探本之論、弭盜之原，尤方今之首務，宜遄發而早圖之者也。
雖然，邇者聖天子以倭寇之不靖，用諫臣之言，黜貪殘之吏。今又大發諸道之兵，以討程饒之賊，而專命三省撫臣司其事，監察董其師，總督重臣兼其任，則執事之所謂首務要機者，聖明已舉行之矣。黔黎之息肩，可計日而待矣。
而愚生之私憂過計，又有不容已於言者。惠潮汀漳數郡，鞠為盜區，郡邑守令必得有文武才略者以鎮壓之，而後可以望更始之治。今貪墨者雖去，而才望者未擇，循資除授，未必皆龔遂、張敞之徒。盜之所以未弭者，此也。討捕之
translation_en:
…such as the saying, “To obtain one good county magistrate is equivalent to three thousand effective soldiers; to obtain one good prefect is equivalent to thirty thousand effective soldiers.” This bears it out. Some argue that the bandits originate in Fujian and Guangdong. Now the mountain bandits of Cheng and Rao [?] have spread through three provinces. Unless the troops of all three provinces are united to strike their lairs, mow them down like grass, and hunt them down like beasts, their advance will spread unchecked, like an ulcer eating into flesh. This argument probes the root of the problem and the fundamental means of suppressing banditry. It is above all the foremost task of the present time, requiring swift mobilization and early planning.
Nevertheless, recently the sagely Son of Heaven, because the Japanese pirates had not been pacified, accepted the advice of remonstrating officials and dismissed corrupt and cruel officials. Now he has also mobilized large numbers of troops from the various circuits to campaign against the bandits of Cheng and Rao [?]. He has specifically charged the grand coordinators of the three provinces with managing the undertaking, assigned censors to supervise their armies, and entrusted a senior supreme commander with concurrent responsibility. Thus what you, sir, have called the foremost tasks and crucial measures have already been put into effect by His Sagely Majesty. The day when the common people can lay down their burdens may now be counted and awaited.
Yet this foolish student has private anxieties and perhaps excessive concerns that he cannot refrain from expressing. The several prefectures of Huizhou, Chaozhou, Tingzhou, and Zhangzhou have become entirely overrun by bandits. Their prefects and county magistrates must be men with both civil and military ability and strategic judgment, capable of bringing the situation under control; only then can we hope for a fresh beginning in government. Although corrupt officials have now been removed, men of ability and standing have yet to be selected. Those appointed according to seniority will not necessarily all be men like Gong Sui and Zhang Chang. This is why banditry has not yet been quelled. As for suppressing and apprehending the bandits…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
命雖下尚恐有以勤民費財爲疑而爲招諭之
說者似不可不慮也自潰卒跳梁於閩界
假息於江右而惵惡之徒效尤日甚此所
謂爲虺弗摧爲蛇將柰之何者也故今日
之舉雖勤民費財而討捕之不可以已也
夫兵者凶器也不得已而用之者也櫛者
墜髮而爲之不止者以所去者少而所利
者多也是以知用兵之不可以已也狂瞽
之見如此不識執事以爲何如
punctuated: 命雖下，尚恐有以勤民費財爲疑，而爲招諭之說者，似不可不慮也。自潰卒跳梁於閩界，假息於江右，而惵惡之徒效尤日甚。此所謂爲虺弗摧，爲蛇將柰之何者也。故今日之舉，雖勤民費財，而討捕之不可以已也。夫兵者，凶器也，不得已而用之者也。櫛者墜髮，而爲之不止者，以所去者少，而所利者多也。是以知用兵之不可以已也。狂瞽之見如此，不識執事以爲何如？
translation_en: …although the order has been issued, I still fear that some may raise doubts on the grounds that it burdens the people and consumes resources, and advocate summoning the rebels to submit instead. This possibility, it seems, cannot be overlooked. Since the routed soldiers began running rampant within Fujian and found a temporary refuge in Jiangxi, evildoers [?] have increasingly followed their example. This is what is meant by the saying: “If you fail to crush a viper while it is small, what will you do when it becomes a great snake?” Thus, although the present undertaking burdens the people and consumes resources, the campaign to suppress and apprehend them must not cease. Weapons are instruments of ill omen, to be used only when there is no alternative. Combing makes hair fall out, yet people continue to do it because what is lost is little and the benefit is great. From this we know that military action must not cease. Such are my rash and benighted views; I do not know what you, sir, think of them.

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
歲辛酉江西賓貢典成有司
既歌鹿鳴以宴之矣應陽不
佞從諸執事後例有言廼進
諸士而告之曰諸士知所以
賓貢之典乎古者帝王中天
而治也薄海內外各以珎異
來貢所以備供用而昭臣職
也夏書禹貢蓋班班可攷矣
漢制令有司郡國歲各貢賢
良文學一人貢之義其昉於
此乎大江以西大禹之所敷
也彭蠡之所會也青原白鹿
之所融萃也元氣所鍾必生
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

歲辛酉，江西賓貢典成，有司既歌《鹿鳴》以宴之矣。應陽不佞，從諸執事後，例有言，廼進諸士而告之曰：「諸士知所以賓貢之典乎？古者帝王中天而治也，薄海內外，各以珎異來貢，所以備供用而昭臣職也。《夏書》《禹貢》蓋班班可攷矣。漢制，令有司郡國歲各貢賢良文學一人，貢之義其昉於此乎？大江以西，大禹之所敷也，彭蠡之所會也，青原、白鹿之所融萃也。元氣所鍾，必生
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the xinyou year [1561], Jiangxi’s ceremony of honoring and recommending candidates was completed, and the responsible officials had already sung “The Deer Call” to feast them. I, Yingyang, unworthy though I am, followed behind the officials conducting the proceedings and, as customary, had some words to offer. I therefore called the gentlemen forward and addressed them:

“Do you gentlemen understand the purpose of this ceremony of honoring and recommending candidates? In antiquity, emperors and kings occupied the center beneath Heaven and governed. Throughout the lands within and beyond the seas, each region brought its rare and extraordinary products as tribute, thereby providing for use at court and demonstrating the duties of subjects. This is clearly documented in the ‘Tribute of Yu’ in the Documents of Xia. Under Han institutions, the responsible officials in each commandery and kingdom were ordered annually to present one man of worth and integrity, learned in the classics. Did the meaning of ‘tribute’ as the presentation of men begin here?

“The land west of the great river is where Yu the Great brought the land into order, where the waters of Pengli converge, and where the influences of Qingyuan and Bailu blend and gather. Wherever primal vital energy concentrates, it must bring forth …

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
靈異而迺不見於夏書之所
