貢者抑又何耶豈山川之氣
獨祕於此乎應陽竊惟天地
之氣各有所鍾而其發也亦
異是故流而爲川峙而爲山
散殊而爲物而得其秀最靈
者爲人是人也者天地之正
===
氣也詩不云乎維嶽降神生
甫及申又曰王國克生維周
之楨言士之貴於物也江右
之治儉薄簡嗇固無所謂貢
矣然歷代名賢彬彬汗史豈
非天地間之至貴者乎玆不
暇遠引
punctuated: 靈異，而迺不見於夏書之所貢者，抑又何耶？豈山川之氣獨祕於此乎？應陽竊惟，天地之氣各有所鍾，而其發也亦異。是故流而爲川，峙而爲山，散殊而爲物，而得其秀最靈者爲人。是人也者，天地之正氣也。《詩》不云乎：「維嶽降神，生甫及申。」又曰：「王國克生，維周之楨。」言士之貴於物也。江右之治，儉薄簡嗇，固無所謂貢矣。然歷代名賢，彬彬汗史，豈非天地間之至貴者乎？玆不暇遠引。
translation_en: …beings of exceptional spiritual endowment. Yet why do they not appear among the tribute items recorded in the Documents of Xia? Could the vital force of mountains and rivers remain hidden in this region alone? I, Yingyang, humbly consider that the vital force of Heaven and Earth gathers in particular places and manifests itself in different ways. Thus, flowing, it becomes rivers; standing lofty, it becomes mountains; dispersing into diverse forms, it becomes things. Those who receive its finest essence and possess the greatest spiritual intelligence are human beings. Human beings, then, embody the upright vital force of Heaven and Earth. Does not the Book of Odes say, “The lofty mountains sent down their spirits, giving birth to Fu and Shen”? It also says, “The royal realm could bring them forth: they were the pillars of Zhou.” These lines speak of the greater worth of worthy men than of material things. The conditions of life in Jiangyou are frugal, meager, plain, and sparing; there are indeed no noteworthy tribute products to speak of. Yet its renowned worthies throughout successive dynasties grace the historical annals in splendid succession. Are they not the most precious things between Heaven and Earth? Here there is no time to cite examples from the distant past.

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
國初如楊文貞歷事
四朝相業焜燿至於今能頌之其
他耆德如胡司成忠讜若李
文毅先後媲美代不乏人是
故語其德則珪璋備矣語其
用則梁棟具矣語其文章則
雲錦黼黻燦矣是天地之至
===
===
寶也以此而貢于
天子之庭則雖璆鐵銀鏤不足以
為奇球琳琅玕不足以為寶
羽毛齒革不足以為文其為
貢也孰尚焉是皆諸士鄉之
所產者也矧我
皇上道久化成諸士涵濡
punctuated: 國初，如楊文貞，歷事四朝，相業焜燿，至於今能頌之。其他耆德如胡司成，忠讜若李文毅，先後媲美，代不乏人。是故語其德，則珪璋備矣；語其用，則梁棟具矣；語其文章，則雲錦黼黻燦矣。是天地之至寶也。以此而貢于天子之庭，則雖璆鐵銀鏤不足以為奇，球琳琅玕不足以為寶，羽毛齒革不足以為文。其為貢也，孰尚焉？是皆諸士鄉之所產者也。矧我皇上道久化成，諸士涵濡
translation_en: …At the beginning of the dynasty, there was Yang Wenzhen, who served four successive reigns. His achievements as chief minister shone brilliantly and are still celebrated today. Other venerable men of virtue, such as Director of Education Hu, and men of loyal forthrightness, such as Li Wenyi, matched one another in excellence in succession; no generation lacked such men. Thus, speaking of their virtue, they possess all the qualities of ceremonial jade tablets; speaking of their usefulness, they are fully fitted to serve as beams and pillars; speaking of their literary accomplishments, they shine like cloud-patterned brocade and embroidered ceremonial designs. These men are the supreme treasures of Heaven and Earth. When such men are presented as tribute at the Son of Heaven’s court, even jade chime stones, iron, silver, and steel cannot count as rarities; fine jades and langgan stones cannot count as treasures; feathers, hair, tusks, and hides cannot count as adornments. What could surpass such a tribute? These are all products of the native region of you gentlemen. Moreover, our emperor’s Way has long prevailed and his transforming influence has come to fruition; you gentlemen have been steeped in…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖化之日久矣濟濟多士上稽近
瀍則人文之盛豈特比隆成
周哉諸士行將行其所學以
儀羽
皇猷者誠能竭忠秉誠達其所蘊
則豈惟應陽輩藉以寡愆而
山川亦與有光澤矣若舍其
===
所學自蹈匪彝則豈惟自壞
其寶以貽二三子之辱而山
川所以篤祜於人者亦旣虛
矣其何貢之爲詩曰高山仰
止景行行止諸士其尚勗之
哉諸士其尚勗之哉
浙江衢州府江山縣儒學敎
punctuated:
聖化之日久矣。濟濟多士，上稽近瀍，則人文之盛，豈特比隆成周哉！諸士行將行其所學，以儀羽皇猷者，誠能竭忠秉誠，達其所蘊，則豈惟應陽輩藉以寡愆，而山川亦與有光澤矣。若舍其所學，自蹈匪彝，則豈惟自壞其寶，以貽二三子之辱，而山川所以篤祜於人者亦旣虛矣。其何貢之爲？《詩》曰：「高山仰止，景行行止。」諸士其尚勗之哉！諸士其尚勗之哉！
浙江衢州府江山縣儒學敎
translation_en:
…have long been steeped in the sage’s transforming influence. With so many accomplished scholars, looking back to antiquity and toward the Chan River [?], could the flourishing of cultural accomplishment merely equal the splendor of Chengzhou? You scholars will soon put your learning into practice to adorn and assist the imperial designs. If you truly exhaust your loyalty, hold fast to sincerity, and give expression to what you possess within, then not only will Yingyang and his fellows thereby have fewer faults, but the mountains and rivers will also share in the glory. If, however, you abandon your learning and yourselves tread paths contrary to established norms, you will not only destroy your own treasures and bring disgrace upon yourselves: the abundant blessings that the mountains and rivers bestow upon people will also have been bestowed in vain. What sort of tribute would that be? The Book of Odes says: “We look up to the lofty mountain; we follow the great road.” May you scholars strive toward this! May you scholars strive toward this!
Instructor at the Confucian School of Jiangshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang…

title: 嘉靖四十年江西鄉試錄
